findings.title: FORMULA: seven fields, trigger first, ends in a seam — not a prohibition
findings.detail:
Every trap in the file today is written as a POST-MORTEM: it opens with the version, the owner quote, or the symptom, and reaches the rule at the end. That ordering fires only for a reader who already has the bug. The condensed entry must invert it. Formula, in this fixed order:

1. `#### <ID> — <the mistake, stated as an outcome the reader would not want>` (<=70 chars, no version number in the title)
2. `**Fires when**` — the situation in the second person, phrased as what you are ABOUT to do, and containing the LITERAL identifiers that will be in the diff (`setPointerCapture`, `opacity:0`, `n.y`, `camTarget`, `locator.click`, `| head`). This line is the index; see the trigger-vocabulary findings.
3. `**Mechanism**` — one or two sentences of causal physics: WHY the obvious thing does not work. Warnings phrased as bare prohibitions get rationalised away; a mechanism cannot be, because it predicts.
4. `**Looks like**` — the observable when you have already done it. This is the SECOND index: half of all readers arrive from a symptom, not from an edit, and without this line they never reach the entry.
5. `**Count**` — a digit, the span of versions, and whether a gate or a human found it. This is the anti-decoration device: `6 recorded instances` is evidence, `be careful` is furniture.
6. `**Do**` — the named seam / API / helper. An entry that ends in a prohibition leaves the reader with no move; an entry that ends in `j.clickByMouse(sel)` does. Where the fix is unverified at known sites, say so HERE in capitals — a half-fixed trap is more dangerous than an unfixed one.
7. `**Archive**` — `Changelog-Archive.md § v1.X.Y` anchors for the full post-mortem.

Copy rules: <=120 words and <=8 lines per entry, hard; ONE trap per entry (the file currently fuses the pointer-capture and the invisible-overlay classes into one paragraph at L2839-2855, which is why their instance counts contradict each other); counts as digits; no owner quotes (they are narrative, they belong in the archive); no byte deltas, no gate snapshots, no mutation-kill tables.
findings.evidence: Current entries are post-mortem-ordered: L2064 opens 'SIXTH INSTANCE OF THE setPointerCapture BUG CLASS, and it was PRE-EXISTING' then reaches the rule ('Any new fixed overlay with controls goes in that list') on its last line, 7 lines later.

findings.title: FINISHED COPY (a): T-INPUT-1 — a control inside a fixed overlay is dead to the mouse
findings.detail:
Paste-ready. Condenses L610-614 (v1.81.3), L2839-2844 (v1.101.5), L2064-2071 (v1.123.0) and the v1.69.1 note at L2937.

#### T-INPUT-1 — a control inside a fixed overlay is dead to the mouse
**Fires when** you add, move or re-parent a clickable element inside a fixed overlay on the app root (`.ng-landcard`, `.ng-landfilm`, `.ng-seemore`, the option-detail sheet, the node card, any new one) — or you touch `attachInput`.
**Mechanism** `attachInput`'s `pointerdown` calls `setPointerCapture()` on the wrap. That RETARGETS the later `pointerup` to the wrap, so the browser resolves the click from the down/up common ancestor and the listener inside your overlay never runs. Separately, `pointer-events` is inherited and the overlay root disables it: a control that does not re-enable it INLINE is hit-tested straight through to the canvas.
**Looks like** the element measures correctly, `elementFromPoint` returns it, a real mouse click does nothing. Keyboard paths work — that is what hides it. `locator.click()` passes, because it dispatches on the element.
**Count** 6 recorded instances, v1.69.1 (coach Next button) through v1.123.0 (`.ng-seemore`, dead to the mouse for its entire existence). A human found every one.
**Do** add the overlay to `attachInput`'s early-return list so a gesture starting inside it returns before capture; set `pointer-events:auto` inline on the control; pin it with `j.clickByMouse(sel)` — never `locator.click()`.
**Archive** Changelog-Archive.md § v1.69.1, § v1.101.5, § v1.123.0.
findings.evidence: L610-614; L2064-2071 ('SIXTH INSTANCE'); L2839-2844 ('Fourth instance'); L2937 (pointer-events:auto is LOAD-BEARING).

findings.title: FINISHED COPY (b): T-INPUT-2 — a hidden overlay that still eats clicks
findings.detail:
Paste-ready. Condenses L2845-2855 (v1.100.2).

#### T-INPUT-2 — a hidden overlay that still eats clicks
**Fires when** you hide an overlay by writing `opacity:0` and/or `pointer-events:none` — `_suppressLand`, `applyDeckVisibility`, the option-detail-sheet pair, the mobile-pane pair, or any new hide-site.
**Mechanism** hit-testing ignores opacity, and `pointer-events` is inherited — so any descendant that re-enables it INLINE stays live across its whole box. `[data-land-foot]` does exactly that, deliberately, because it holds `More ▸` and the capture `+`. The overlay is invisible and still on top.
**Looks like** something UNDERNEATH the hidden element is dead to the mouse. `elementFromPoint` at your target returns the thing you thought was gone — measured: `<div data-land-foot="1">` at the centre of a capture button, 120s of Playwright retries.
**Count** 5 instances by v1.100.2. **STILL UNVERIFIED at three sites**: the option-detail-sheet pair and the mobile-pane pair write only opacity/pointer-events and were never changed.
**Do** also set `visibility:hidden !important`. It is inherited, nothing in this subtree escapes it with `visible`, and it removes the subtree from hit-testing outright. Assert inertness with `elementFromPoint`, not with a visual check.
**Archive** Changelog-Archive.md § v1.100.2.
findings.evidence: L2845-2855, incl. 'The three sibling hide-sites that write opacity/pointer-events directly ... share the shape of the hole and were NOT changed — unverified.'

findings.title: FINISHED COPY (c): T-SPEC-1 — never assert a render by re-implementing it
findings.detail:
Paste-ready. Condenses L1147-1153 (v1.126.0), L1011-1026 (v1.125.0) and the published-draw-state note at L1436-1447 (v1.129.0).

#### T-SPEC-1 — never assert a render by re-implementing it
**Fires when** a spec, probe or audit computes the expected answer itself: `nodes.filter(...)`, a private copy of a filter or of "what the node set is", a hand rebuilt from `adj`, a screen coordinate recomputed from `n.x`/`n.y`.
**Mechanism** you write the copy from the same reading of the code you are testing, usually with the fix already in it. The two agree by construction, so the assertion measures nothing.
**Looks like** green — on a build you have already broken. The v1.126.0 audit built to find this class committed it: its probe measured `nodes.filter(n => n.rep && …)` and reported "identical" about Explore's search, which was doubling every hit and halving its own 120-row cap.
**Count** 6 specs held private copies of the node set (v1.125.0), plus 1 in the audit that hunted them (v1.126.0).
**Do** drive the real entry point — `renderExplorer()`, `optionsFor()`, `draw()` — and assert on what it EMITTED: DOM rows, duplicate row text, read-back pixels. When the geometry lives in a draw-local closure (`halfW`, `ox`) you cannot recompute it at all: PUBLISH it (`_lastPairLabel`, `_lastRichLabel`, `this._LY = LY`) and read the published value. Reading the strings a frame passed to `fillText` is the render's output, not a second implementation. A second implementation is legitimate ONLY when it also asserts set-equality against the app's own result, so a disagreement fails loudly.
**Archive** Changelog-Archive.md § v1.125.0, § v1.126.0, § v1.129.0.
findings.evidence: L1147-1153 ('Never assert a render by re-implementing it'); L1011-1026 ('SIX SPECS HELD PRIVATE COPIES'); L1436-1447 ('THE RENDERER PUBLISHES WHAT IT DREW').

findings.title: TRIGGER VOCABULARY, rule 1: index by the token that will be in the diff, not by the lesson
findings.detail:
An agent about to break one of these does not grep for 'hit-testing pitfalls'. It has a symbol on screen and it greps for THAT: `attachInput`, `setPointerCapture`, `_suppressLand`, `opacity:0`, `pointer-events`, `visibility:hidden`, `n.y`, `LY(`, `pairMid`, `camTarget`, `rollCamTarget`, `_dockLandCard`, `locator.click`, `elementFromPoint`, `test.use`, `emulateMedia`, `reuseExistingServer`, `rng(`, `except Exception`, `| head`, `_tech_keys`, `adj[`. So the `**Fires when**` line is not prose — it is a KEYWORD MANIFEST written as a sentence, and its acceptance test is mechanical: for every trap, list the 3-6 identifiers a developer would have open while committing it, and confirm each appears verbatim in that line.

This is the compensating mechanism for the one thing CLAUDE.md cannot do: co-locate the warning with the hazard. It cannot sit next to the code, so it must be reachable in one grep FROM the code. A trap whose trigger line contains no identifier from the codebase is unreachable and should be demoted to Tier 2 or archived.

Second keyword layer, for the symptom-first reader: the `**Looks like**` line must contain the words a bug report uses — 'nothing happens', 'dead to the mouse', 'green', 'flake', 'passes in isolation', 'off screen', 'wrong number'. These are what an agent greps when it is debugging rather than editing.
findings.evidence: L2064-2071 buries `.ng-seemore` and `attachInput` inside a paragraph titled 'SIXTH INSTANCE OF THE setPointerCapture BUG CLASS' inside a section titled 'THE OVERFLOW HINT: ABOVE THE HAND' — reachable by symbol grep today only by luck.

findings.title: TRIGGER VOCABULARY, rule 2: group by the ACTION you are taking, and give every trap a stable ID
findings.detail:
Group by situation, not by subsystem and not by symptom, because the reader knows what they are about to do and does not yet know what will go wrong. Six groups, matching the six things anyone does in this repo:

- `T-INPUT-*` — pointers, clicks, hit-testing, fixed overlays, z-order, docking
- `T-CANVAS-*` — the draw path, node coordinates, labels, the camera
- `T-SPEC-*` — writing or reading a Playwright assertion
- `T-HARNESS-*` — the DSL, ports, payload rules, which build is under test
- `T-DATA-*` — joins, slugs, ids, settings keys, the wire
- `T-CI-*` — gates, workflows, surveys, blast-radius measurement

The IDs are the second load-bearing choice. They let the REST of CLAUDE.md stop re-explaining the same trap: a version block, a command-table row or a code comment can cite `(T-INPUT-1)` in one token. That is most of why this file is 337k chars — the pointer-capture class is explained in full four separate times. One canonical entry, cited everywhere, is both the compression and the correctness fix (see the instance-count contradiction finding).

IDs must be STABLE across edits and never renumbered — same discipline as the share-link ordinals, and for the same reason: a citation elsewhere in the tree must not silently come to mean a different trap. Retire an ID, do not reuse it.
findings.evidence: setPointerCapture is explained at full length at L610-614, L2064-2071, L2839-2844, and partially at L2937 — four copies, three different instance counts.

findings.title: TRIGGER VOCABULARY, rule 3: a one-screen TRIGGER INDEX above the bodies
findings.detail:
The bodies are for the reader who has already been caught by the index. The index is what a skim reads, and it must fit one screen. Two columns, `About to …` -> ID, <=12 words per row, sorted by group. It is the only part of the section designed to be read when the agent is NOT looking for it.

| About to … | Trap |
|---|---|
| put a clickable control inside a fixed overlay | T-INPUT-1 |
| hide an overlay with `opacity` / `pointer-events` | T-INPUT-2 |
| position fixed chrome with a CSS constant | T-INPUT-3 |
| read `n.x`/`n.y` for anything on screen | T-CANVAS-1 |
| assert where the camera is looking | T-CANVAS-2 |
| compute what a render SHOULD produce | T-SPEC-1 |
| click something in a test | T-SPEC-2 |
| call a change covered because a probe agreed | T-SPEC-3 |
| write a journey that ends an exchange | T-SPEC-4 |
| cite a green gate as evidence | T-SPEC-5 |
| add or rename a payload / port / fixture | T-HARNESS-1 |
| join two id spellings | T-DATA-1 |
| delete a settings key | T-DATA-2 |
| measure the blast radius of a rename | T-CI-1 |

Write the rows as verbs in the reader's own voice. `About to hide an overlay` fires; `Overlay visibility semantics` does not.

findings.title: CO-LOCATION: the only real fix is a one-line ID comment at each seam, outside CLAUDE.md
findings.detail:
The warnings literature's first finding is that a warning not co-located with the hazard is ignored, and CLAUDE.md is structurally incapable of co-location — it is one file, loaded before the agent knows what it is touching. The inline section is therefore a HUB, not a substitute for co-location, and it will keep failing for agents who jump straight to `app.src.jsx` from a task description.

Proposal (a separate, cheap, non-CLAUDE.md change): put a single-line comment carrying the trap ID at each named seam — above `attachInput`'s early-return list, above `_suppressLand`, above `_dockLandCard`, beside `this._LY = LY`, at the top of `e2e/dsl.ts`'s payload table. `// T-INPUT-1 — do not add an overlay with controls without adding it here.` Nothing else; the body stays in CLAUDE.md.

That buys grep in both directions: from the code to the trap, and from the trap ID to every place it binds. It also gives a cheap freshness gate later — a trap whose ID appears at zero seams is either archive material or its seam has been renamed under it.

Do not attempt this for Tier 2 or Tier 3; the value is entirely in the dozen seams that keep being edited.

findings.title: PLACEMENT: make it section 3, immediately after FORBIDDEN ACTIONS, and renumber the rest
findings.detail:
Argument from how the file is actually read.

1. Section 2 is already the prohibition slot, and it is the wrong half of the pair on its own. Its table says WHAT not to do with a one-clause 'Why' ('Breaks build, bad data'). The traps are the causal sibling: why the obvious thing fails. Two prohibition registers in different parts of one file means the reader learns neither is complete. Putting the traps directly under section 2 makes one contiguous 'things that will go wrong' region.

2. Primacy. Everything above `## 4. ARCHITECTURE` is read by an agent that then jumps to code; everything below it is read by an agent that is already in the file looking for something. The trigger index has to be in the first region, because its whole job is to be seen without being sought.

3. It must NOT go at the very bottom. The tail today is Resources — links, PostHog dashboards, a closing italic line. That is the safest region in the file to skip, and a reader who skims the bottom is looking for a run command, not for hazards.

4. Section 2's own table gains one row pointing at it: `| Ship a change to app.src.jsx or a spec without reading §3 | Six known classes of silent failure | Read the §3 trigger index |`. That is the handoff, in the table the reader is already in.

Cost: renumbering sections 3-8 to 4-9. Do it once and accept the churn; a trap section wedged in as `§2.5` reads as an appendix, which is the decoration failure mode arriving by layout instead of by length.
findings.evidence: Heading map: L58 '## 2. FORBIDDEN ACTIONS', L80 '## 3. PROJECT STRUCTURE', L136 '## 4. ARCHITECTURE'. Tail (L3327-3338) is Resources + a one-line closing italic.

findings.title: PLACEMENT: two back-pointers, because a top-and-bottom skimmer is the realistic reader
findings.detail:
Assume the reader skims the top and the bottom and greps the middle. Section 3 covers the top. Two cheap additions cover the rest:

1. The read-order block at L9-16 is literally the first content in the file and currently lists four documents. Add a fifth line INSIDE it: `0. §3 TRAPS  <- the index, before you touch app code or write a spec`. It is the one place guaranteed to be read by an agent following the stated workflow, and it costs ~60 chars.

2. The closing line at L3338 is currently `*This guide is for AI assistants. Focus on: validate -> edit JSON -> regenerate -> build.*` — which is a content-pipeline summary in a file that is 87% app narrative. Replace or extend it with a hazard pointer: `*Before you assert, click, draw, join or grep: §3 TRAPS.*` The bottom-skimmer's last impression should be the index, not a link list.

Do NOT duplicate trap prose into either place. Duplication is how the file got here, and a second copy is a second thing to keep true — the existing four copies of the pointer-capture trap already disagree with each other.
findings.evidence: L9-16 read-order block; L3338 closing line.

findings.title: PLACEMENT: the command table cites trap IDs, it does not restate them
findings.detail:
Section 5's `npm test` row (L3096) is one of the highest-traffic destinations in the file and already carries three harness traps inline: the `j.clickByMouse` / intercepting-ancestor rule, the late-payload `afterSim` semantics, and the `j.boot()` in-flight-write contract. `e2e:gen` (L3098) carries the cross-worktree port trap; `e2e:share` (L3099) and `e2e:replay` (L3100) carry the never-`locator.click()` and never-`camTarget` rules.

That placement is correct — it IS co-location, at the moment the reader is choosing a command — but the prose must not exist twice. Rule: the trap body lives in §3; the command row keeps a bare citation, `(T-SPEC-2, T-HARNESS-1)`. The row shrinks by hundreds of chars, the trap stops being maintained in two voices, and the citation is greppable in the direction that matters (from the command the agent is about to run, to the hazard).

Same treatment for the version-narrative cross-references being moved to the archive: where an archived block says 'the same lesson _dockLandCard learned', the archive keeps the sentence and the inline entry keeps the count.
findings.evidence: L3096 (npm test row, ~4,000 chars, three traps inline), L3098-3100.

findings.title: MAXIMUM: 12 inline Tier-1 entries, hard cap, with eviction required to admit a 13th
findings.detail:
Twelve. The defence is budget, skim-load, and the equal-weighting failure.

BUDGET. At the formula's ceiling (<=120 words, ~110 words typical, ~6.2 chars/word) an entry is ~700 chars. 12 entries = ~8,400 chars. Plus a 14-row index (~1,200) and a 20-line Tier-2 register (~2,200) = ~11,800 chars, 24% of a 50,000-char CLAUDE.md. Above that the hazard section starts competing for attention with the architecture the same agent needs to do the work, and you have rebuilt the current problem at 1/28th scale.

SKIM LOAD. The index must be read as a UNIT, not searched. 12 entries produce ~14 index rows — one screen. At 25 entries the index becomes a table you scan for a keyword, which means it only works for readers who already suspect a hazard, which is the population that did not need it.

EQUAL WEIGHTING. This is the decisive one. A wall of same-sized cautions is read as decoration; the reader learns the section carries no information about which of these will actually bite. Twelve entries can each carry a differentiating instance count (6, 5, 4, 3 …) and the differences stay legible. Forty cannot: the counts blur, and the count is the only thing in the entry that is evidence rather than exhortation.

ENFORCEMENT. The cap only holds if admission requires eviction. Rule to write into the section header: adding a 13th entry means demoting one in the SAME commit, and naming which and why. Default demotion criterion below.

findings.title: HONEST COUNT: ~39 distinct live trap classes, so tiering is mandatory, not optional
findings.detail:
I surveyed the file for distinct classes (not instances). Roughly 39 survive as genuinely live guidance:

INPUT/DOM (9): pointer-capture retargeting; opacity/pointer-events is not hidden; `pointer-events:auto` inherited; z trapped inside the `position:fixed` wrap; `style.color = ""` deletes rather than restores; fixed chrome positioned by a constant against a measured band; a 44px hit target setting a 24px row's geometry; `body[data-share-cue]` colliding with a control's own attribute so `querySelector` returns `<body>`; `_landHidden()`'s four latch holders.

CANVAS (7): `n.y` vs the drawn `LY`/`pairMid`; `halfW` vs `n.r*scale` for label anchoring; never assert the camera from `camTarget`; canvas oracles need a control frame and a per-sector delta; 'nothing is drawn' is false on a correct build; `page.mouse.wheel` must hit clear canvas; position titles carry a baked-in role that `splitName().main` does not strip.

SPEC/HARNESS (12): re-implementing the render; `locator.click()` is not a mouse; a probe is not a gate; an unrigged `rng()` tag; assertions stricter than their own claim; structurally blind green gates; payload patterns are substrings so a stale name matches nothing; `test.use({reducedMotion})` leaves `matchMedia` false; a spec needing a gitignored payload is collected by nothing; cross-worktree port reuse; `npm run build` does not rebuild the neural bundle; one `advance()` is not a frame.

DATA/CI (11): silent join spellings (`_tech_keys`); node index can never go in a URL; settings keys have no tombstone; a manifest stub is truthy; do not role-split `adj`; the de-overlap hoist; bare `except Exception` hiding a `NameError` so a check never ran; CI running a subset of the human chain; an allow-list of packaged paths rotting silently; `git diff --quiet` on an untracked file; truncated-grep surveys.

39 >> 12. Tiering is forced.

findings.title: ADMISSION TEST for Tier 1: it has recurred AND it fails silently — both, or it is not inline
findings.detail:
Two necessary conditions, plus a tie-breaker. Write them into the section header so future additions are arguable rather than negotiable.

(i) RECURRENCE. >=2 recorded instances, OR 1 instance plus a NAMED open class of code that can reproduce it ('any new fixed overlay with controls', 'any spec that converts a node to a screen position'). A one-off with no open class is a story, and stories belong in the archive.

(ii) SILENCE. The wrong version passes: it goes green, or it looks correct, or it prints a plausible number. This is the load-bearing condition. A trap that fails LOUDLY needs no warning — the error message is a better warning than CLAUDE.md can ever be, because it is perfectly co-located and perfectly timed. Spending one of twelve slots on a loud failure is spending it on nothing.

TIE-BREAKER: cross-role blast radius. Prefer the trap that can bite an agent who is not working on that feature — someone editing a spec for an unrelated journey, or renaming a symbol. Those readers have no chance of discovering it any other way.

Corollary and default DEMOTION rule: when a trap acquires a gate that fails loudly and names it, it stops satisfying (ii) and leaves Tier 1 that day, moving to Tier 2 WITH its gate named. That is what keeps the cap from being violated by accretion — the section shrinks as the machine gets better, which is the correct direction.

findings.title: TIER 1 ROSTER: the 12 that pass the admission test today
findings.detail:
Ranked by (instances x silence x blast radius). IDs as proposed.

T-INPUT-1 pointer-capture retargeting — 6 instances, silent, open class ('any new fixed overlay').
T-INPUT-2 opacity/pointer-events is not hidden — 5 instances, silent, 3 sites still unverified.
T-INPUT-3 fixed chrome positioned by a constant against a MEASURED band — 3 instances (`_dockLandCard`, `_dockOptionHint`, the phone challenge-cue collision, still open), silent at most viewports.
T-CANVAS-1 `n.y` where the renderer draws at `LY`/`pairMid` — 4 instances, silent (the spec reports 'nothing is drawn' about something that was drawn).
T-CANVAS-2 never assert the camera from `camTarget`; project through `draw()` — survived three reviews.
T-SPEC-1 never assert a render by re-implementing it — 7 instances, green-on-broken, committed by the audit built to catch it.
T-SPEC-2 `locator.click()` is not a mouse — masks T-INPUT-1 and T-INPUT-2 completely; use `j.clickByMouse`.
T-SPEC-3 a probe is not a gate — two consecutive versions shipped an uncovered fix that a mutant then survived.
T-SPEC-4 an unrigged `rng()` tag is a lottery ticket — 7.7% per run, four consecutive green suites hid it.
T-SPEC-5 a green gate can be structurally blind to your change — say what it cannot see, do not cite it.
T-DATA-1 a missed key spelling falls through to a plausible fallback and prints wrong numbers forever — 289 of 1,204 cards; the join must be COUNTED at the emitter.
T-CI-1 never measure a rename's blast radius through `| head`, and never let a check return inside a bare `except` — a swallowed `NameError` reported '0 disagreements' for months.

The first three and T-SPEC-1/2 are the highest-value: they are the ones a competent agent hits while doing something that looks routine.
findings.evidence: Counts read from L2064 (6th), L2853 (5th), L1804-1806 (third instance), L1020 (third time), L1011 (six specs) + L1151 (+1), L1783 (7.7%, p=0.18), L2048 (structurally blind), L1471-1475 (truncated grep), L849 (bare except).

findings.title: TIER 2: a one-line register, inline, no bodies — ~20 lines, greppable, deliberately unglamorous
findings.detail:
The owner's constraint is that traps survive IN CONTEXT, and 27 of the 39 cannot have 700-char bodies. They get ONE line each, in the same six groups, immediately below the Tier-1 bodies under a heading that says what they are: `### Also known, one line each (no body — see the archive)`.

Line formula: `<ID> <trigger token> — <mechanism in <=12 words> -> <the move>.` That is enough to fire if you grep the token, and short enough that 20 of them read as a list rather than as more prose. Examples, paste-ready:

- `T-INPUT-4` `z-index` inside the `position:fixed` wrap is trapped at plane 0 -> portal deliberate screens to the root plane; pick a z BAND, never a loose number.
- `T-INPUT-5` `style.color = ""` DELETES an inline declaration, it does not restore it -> write the resting value (`NG_LAND_MORE_COL`).
- `T-HARNESS-2` payload patterns are SUBSTRINGS of the request URL -> `flashcards.json` matched nothing for months; the guard only warned when EVERY rule missed.
- `T-HARNESS-3` `test.use({reducedMotion})` leaves `matchMedia` FALSE here -> `page.emulateMedia`.
- `T-HARNESS-4` a spec in a directory no config's `testDir` collects is a note, not a gate -> check collection before claiming coverage.
- `T-HARNESS-5` `npm run build` does NOT rebuild the neural bundle -> a stale `neural.js` looks like a 240s regression.
- `T-DATA-2` a settings key can never be deleted (no tombstone in the merge) -> stop READING it and say so where the reader was.
- `T-CI-2` CI must never run a subset of the chain a human runs -> `votes-refresh` stripped `strength` from 4,464 of 4,465 nodes.

No counts, no archive anchors on Tier 2 lines — the ID is the anchor. If a Tier-2 line needs a body to be understood, it is a Tier-1 candidate and something must be evicted for it.

findings.title: TIER 3: archive-only, and the demotion rule that keeps the cap honest
findings.detail:
Everything else goes to `docs/Changelog-Archive.md` with its full post-mortem and is reachable by version anchor from a Tier-1/2 `**Archive**` line. Qualifying shapes:

- ONE-OFF WITH NO OPEN CLASS: `git diff --quiet` reporting no change for an untracked file (keepalive); the `e2e-full.yml` tar allow-list; Node 20 -> 22. Each was fixed once, in one place, and cannot recur without someone rewriting that exact workflow.
- MECHANISED: anything now caught by a gate that names it — the ordinal lockfile (`validate:ordinals`), the `/l/*` header drift (`check_headers_cache.py` checks 6-8), the `export`-strip guard and duplicate-top-level-name guard in `build.mjs`, the payload ratchet. These fail loudly with the explanation in the failure text, which beats any inline paragraph.
- SUPERSEDED: guidance about surfaces that no longer exist (the in-node dossier's z-index, the legacy variant, the prototype `?dual` payloads).

DEMOTION RULE, written into the section header: `Admitting a Tier-1 entry requires demoting one in the same commit. Default demotion criterion: the trap now has a gate that fails loudly and names it — move it to Tier 2 with the gate's name, or to Tier 3 if the class is closed.` Without that sentence the cap is a wish; with it, the section can only shrink as the test suite grows, which is the direction the last thirty versions have actually been moving.

findings.title: COUNTS ARE CURRENTLY CONTRADICTORY — verify before freezing them into condensed copy
findings.detail:
The instance counts are the anti-decoration device, so they have to be right, and today they are not. v1.100.2 (L2853) calls the invisible-overlay bug 'Fifth instance of this repo's recurring bug class'. v1.101.5 — a LATER version — calls the pointer-capture bug 'Fourth instance' (L2840). v1.123.0 then calls pointer-capture the 'SIXTH INSTANCE' (L2064). Chronologically that reads 5, 4, 6.

The cause is diagnosable from the text: two different classes are being counted against one informal register ('this repo's recurring bug class'), sometimes together and sometimes apart. My Tier-1 roster keeps them separate (T-INPUT-1 pointer retargeting, T-INPUT-2 hit-testing-through-a-transparent-overlay) because their MECHANISMS and their FIXES are different — early-return list versus `visibility:hidden` — and a reader who conflates them applies the wrong fix.

Before the condensed section ships, re-count both classes against `neural/src/app.src.jsx` and the archive: enumerate the actual overlays in `attachInput`'s early-return list and the actual hide-sites writing opacity/pointer-events, and state each count as `N recorded instances as of vX.Y.Z`. Also re-verify the T-INPUT-2 'three sibling hide-sites, unverified' claim — it is from v1.100.2 and ~29 versions old; if they have since been fixed the entry is scaremongering, and if they have not it is the most actionable line in the section.

This is the one place where the condensation can make the file WORSE: a single wrong count in a 12-entry list is far more visible than the same wrong count buried in 293k chars of narrative.
findings.evidence: L2853 'Fifth instance' (v1.100.2) vs L2840 'Fourth instance' (v1.101.5) vs L2064 'SIXTH INSTANCE' (v1.123.0); L2853-2855 'were NOT changed — unverified'.

findings.title: DO NOT LAUNDER OWNER DECISIONS AND CANON INTO THE TRAP LIST
findings.detail:
The file's imperative-voice lines are not all traps, and mixing the two kinds is the fastest route to the section being read as decoration — because the reader learns that some entries are physics and some are preference, and cannot tell which without reading all of them.

Three kinds currently share the same 'do not' voice:

1. TRAPS — mechanism-bearing, recurrence-bearing, silent. `T-INPUT-1`. These are the section's subject.
2. OWNER DECISIONS — 'Do not silently reinstate Edge' (L1519), 'the item cap is enforced at add time', the loss-aversion default, the ▶-belongs-to-a-technique rule. These are reversible preferences with a named decider. They belong in a short CANON block, ideally beside the architecture they constrain, and they must be labelled as the owner's call so an agent knows the escape hatch is 'ask', not 'find the seam'.
3. INVARIANTS — 'Do not role-split `adj`' (L975), '`game-over` is the only sink', 'attempt probabilities sum to 100'. These are properties the system must hold. Some are trap-shaped (role-splitting `adj` fails silently and was found by a suite going red, so it earns a Tier-2 line); most are already stated in section 4 and should stay there, near the schema they constrain.

Apply the admission test literally: an owner decision has no MECHANISM line and no COUNT line, so the formula rejects it on its own. That is the point of making the formula seven mandatory fields — it is a filter, not a template.
findings.evidence: L1519 ('It is the owner's call. Do not silently reinstate "Edge".'), L975 ('Do not role-split adj.'), L2924, L2935.

findings.title: EVERY ENTRY MUST DECLARE GUARDED or UNGUARDED — a half-fixed trap is the dangerous one
findings.detail:
The `**Do**` field has a second job: telling the reader whether the machine will catch them. If a gate exists and names the failure, the reader can stop reading and move on — that is the section paying for its own length. If no gate exists, the reader has to be careful by hand, and must be told so in those words.

The file already models this well in places and badly in others. `CategoryNav.tsx` is explicitly labelled 'No gate guards them ... Treat it as unguarded' (L717-723); the Forward catalog is 'Treat the catalog as unguarded'; the three opacity hide-sites are 'NOT changed — unverified'. Those are the most useful sentences in their sections. Elsewhere a trap is written up with a spec name attached and the reader reasonably infers full coverage, when the spec pins one instance of a class that has six.

Rule for the condensed entries: the `**Do**` line ends in one of three forms — `Pinned by <spec>` / `UNGUARDED — <what you must check by hand>` / `Partially pinned: <spec> covers <case>, not <case>`. T-INPUT-1 is the clearest example of the third form: `j.clickByMouse` exists and is excellent, but it only fires for overlays somebody wrote a mouse journey for, and `.ng-seemore` went its entire life without one.

This also gives the demotion rule its input: a trap whose line reads `Pinned by <spec>` for the whole class is a Tier-2 candidate at the next review.
findings.evidence: L717-723 ('No gate guards them ... Treat it as unguarded'); L2853-2855 ('NOT changed — unverified'); L2403-2406 ('Treat the catalog as unguarded'); L2069-2071 (`.ng-seemore` 'dead to the mouse for as long as it has existed').

ergonomist.headline: Every trap in this file is written in post-mortem order — version, owner quote, symptom, then the rule — so it fires only for a reader who already has the bug; the fix is not compression but inversion: trigger-first entries indexed by the literal identifier that will be sitting in the agent's diff, capped at twelve, with admission requiring eviction.

findings.title: CLASS 1: Absence produces a plausible answer — a check that never ran reads as a pass
findings.detail:
THE LARGEST CLASS IN THE FILE, AND IT IS NEVER NAMED. 17 instances in 5 vocabularies. (a) L849 `check_position_type_vs_score` never ran — `os.path.dirname` with no `import os`, `NameError` swallowed by a bare `except Exception: return issues`; "0 disagreements across all 272 position-roles" meant "the check never executed" (real figure: 95). (b) L847 the harness held `"flashcards.json"`, a URL the app has never fetched since v1.80.4 — "the rule matched nothing" and every cold-start assertion measured a warm boot; root cause of 15 red journeys. (c) L848 two of `build.mjs`'s four fetch rewrites "could not fire" and "the guard only warned when EVERY rule missed". (d) L864-874 the `cal` join spelled the key wrong, 294/297 submissions shipped no odds, `calSuccess()` returned null and a fallback printed a plausible ~45.6% on ~289 of 1,204 dealt cards for months. (e) L585-588 the headers gate passed a Function that stopped setting `Cache-Control` because "the comparison loop had nothing to iterate". (f) L856 `keepalive.yml` "has never committed anything" — `git diff --quiet` on an untracked file. (g) L2554 the `withDeck` filter "was a no-op". (h) L904 `_urlSeeded` "assigned at boot and read by nothing". (i) L3251 `npm run validate:affiliate` "documented for months but did not exist". (j) L2870 `test.use({reducedMotion})` leaves matchMedia FALSE so the spec "asserts nothing and passes forever". (k) L2064-2069 `.ng-seemore` "dead to the mouse for as long as it has existed". Plus L690, L719, L2595, L2652, L1677.
RULE: every matcher, join, gate and rewrite must emit a POSITIVE coverage count and hard-fail below a floor — a bare `except`, a null return and a zero-length loop must print, because a negative result and a non-execution are indistinguishable from the outside.
findings.evidence: The repo independently invented the SAME fix five times without naming the class: build.mjs throws per-rule (L848), the cal emitter refuses <95% (L883), the EDGE join gate (L2148-2149), the `mc_pool_cold` beat (L791), the `land_warm_stalled` beat (L845). Five inventions, zero cross-references.

findings.title: CLASS 2: A gate cited as evidence that is structurally unable to fail on its subject
findings.detail:
12 instances; the file uses the phrase "structurally blind"/"structurally incapable"/"unguarded" four times without joining them. L2045-2048 `payload-first-hand` pins a 7-card hand so it "reports the same bytes with the cap and without it — do not read a green payload gate as evidence about hand size". L2322-2332 `replay-digest` is "structurally incapable of seeing" the outcome-kernel fix. L2402-2406 the same digest "STRUCTURALLY unable to see" the cardOrder retirement. L2478-2481 same again for lossAversion. L1734-1736 that digest carries "0 land options", so half of it "is currently contributing nothing". L663-669 CategoryNav: "No gate guards them… Delete CategoryNav and every gate stays green. Treat it as unguarded." L2407-2411 the Forward catalog: "Treat the catalog as unguarded" (a retired row had been stale since v1.105.0). L1674-1683 `e2e/prototype/`: "No gate has ever collected that directory" — through 13 versions, including the one that made its subject the default. L1811-1819 the segBtn aria gap survives because a spec works around it. Plus L852 (the PR gate could not pass at all), L854 (baseline 76 vs deploy's 0), L855 (paths filter omitted its own gate's input).
RULE: a gate may only be cited for a claim a mutant of that claim makes red; otherwise write its blind spot in the same sentence as the green.

findings.title: CLASS 3: Fixed chrome positioned by a constant against a band that is computed
findings.detail:
Self-named "the third instance" at L1804 — the real count is 12, and it is still recurring at v1.129.6. L506-514 `_dockLandCard`: the tray has no height and grows upward; measured 63px overlap over the option cards. L2057-2063 `_dockOptionHint`: the hint sat 2px above the account chip at EVERY width. L1795-1807 the challenge cue writes across the focus label on a phone (6,700 px² overlap) — named as the third instance, NOT FIXED. L2537 `.ng-landfilm` "duplicated the card's DESKTOP rule as a constant" and never knew about its mobile override. L1899 the desktop constant `bottom:236px` vs a taller escape tray (7px overlap under a 4-9s clock). L2991-2998 `max-height:min(620px,74vh)` grew the card to top −28 with no internal scroll. L2050-2056 a width-only breakpoint missed the landscape phone (844px WIDE). L1278-1286 a 44px pixel threshold "fired for nothing" because the lift is radius-anchored (2.2x spread in one frame). L1539-1548 the cold fallback `H - 240` "is not a band, it is very nearly the whole screen". L2668-2670 `lift = 0.34*H` "tuned at 1440x900 and wrong at every other height". L1869-1881 `_bandBot` flicker + "an UNDOCKED element is not a constraint" (rect.top reads 0 for a frame).
RULE: one surface's geometry may never be a constant copied from another surface's current size — measure at runtime, keep the tightest measurement, and treat a not-yet-laid-out element as SKIP, never as zero.

findings.title: CLASS 4: The spec re-implements the thing it is supposed to observe
findings.detail:
10 instances. The file names it once (L1151 "Never assert a render by re-implementing it") and links it to one prior case; it is far wider. L1148-1153 the audit probe measured `nodes.filter(n => n.rep && …)` — "a private copy of the filter, with the fix already in it, so it reported 'identical' about a path that was broken", "committed by the tool built to find them". L1011-1019 six specs held private copies of the node set. L1439-1447 three pixel oracles in a row failed to kill a mutant because `ox` lives in a draw-local closure. L1623-1631 three specs were pinned to where the label used to be. L2880 "Never assert camera behaviour by reading `camTarget` — that is exactly how this bug survived three reviews." L2139-2145 `option-hand`'s pool is a deliberate second copy, made safe only by asserting SET EQUALITY. L2943 `challenge-curriculum`'s camTarget±60 contract retired. L1361-1365, L2597-2608, L2633-2640 canvas oracles that measured something else.
RULE: assert a render by reading what the renderer PUBLISHED (`this._LY`, `_lastPairLabel`, `_lastRichLabel`) or by projecting through the real transform — a spec-side re-derivation is a second implementation that drifts, and it drifts toward agreeing with itself.

findings.title: CLASS 5: Reachable, visible and existing are three different facts; the hit-test is the only oracle
findings.detail:
The file explicitly numbers this to SIX (L2064 "SIXTH INSTANCE OF THE `setPointerCapture` BUG CLASS"; L2840 "Fourth instance"; L2852 "Fifth instance of this repo's recurring bug class") but the mechanism list is wider — 10+ across four different physical causes. setPointerCapture retargeting: L610-614, L2064-2071, L2838-2844, L1898. Inherited `pointer-events`: L2937 ("keyboard paths masked it"). Opacity is not hiding: L2845-2855 an INVISIBLE footer strip ate clicks across its whole box; L499-504 the share cue was "fully CLICKABLE at opacity:0". Z-order: L608-609 (dossier at z:3 under a z:4 pill), L2826-2837 (the pane trapped in a fixed wrap, painted over by z:5). Wrong hit-test coordinate: L1841-1844 (`_updateHover` compared `n.y` against a 28px radius, ~37px off — clicking a VISIBLE orb matched nothing). Foreign chrome: L1801-1803 the challenge cue's `elementFromPoint` returns BUTTON over your own node.
RULE: prove reachability with a real pointer at measured coordinates plus `elementFromPoint` (`j.clickByMouse`, L3096) — `locator.click()` dispatches on the element and therefore proves nothing (L524, L2070, L2842).

findings.title: CLASS 6: A second, stale implementation of a question that already had a seam
findings.detail:
9 instances; self-named once at L1183 ("this is the v1.104.5 'second stale implementation' defect one level down"). L860 `playFrom` was a whole stale copy of `rollFromPosition` — hard-coded camera, no archive, no state reset. L1177-1185 `rollFromPosition` walked `adj[]` for a technique's origin while `confirmPlayFrom` "had it right all along"; measured wrong on 907 of 1,331 techniques and the tapped technique absent from the dealt hand 68.4% of the time. L2969-2973 `rollFromPosition` hard-coded `vw: graphW*0.42` after `rollCamTarget` existed. L1865-1868 the same function still aimed at `{n.x, n.y}` — "Same defect, missed once." L2535 two sites wrote the More-toggle colour. L2537 the film strip duplicated the card's rule. L365-367 one cap under two names (`NG_LIST_ITEM_CAP` / `NG_LIST_MAX_ITEMS`). L1479-1490 a two-branch tap rule "written before v1.101.5 added a third, and never updated". L2237-2254 `opponentDefend` is a second, incompatible implementation of "the opponent" (11.7% overlap with the model's).
RULE: when one question is answered in two places, one of them is already wrong — collapse to a named seam BEFORE adding a third caller, and delete the copy rather than syncing it.

findings.title: CLASS 7: A heuristic standing in for a fact the data states outright
findings.detail:
9 instances; the file names the pairing once (L2541 "the same defect class as roleIdx-vs-valIdx"). L3012-3016 `optionsFor` inferred the performer from `myVal < oppVal - 0.05` while every technique carries `fromRole`. L3004-3011 `roleIdx()` indexed both meanings of `s` with a top/bottom index — "a bottom player was shown ZERO of the 297 submission nodes". L2541 `performerRole(...) === "top"` stood in for an offence/defence test. L2555 "Do not derive the role from the node title" — the derivation is the constant `top` across all 136. L1191-1193 `seatRole` exists because that same derive answers "top" for 596 bottom-authored techniques. L1344-1352 `splitName().main` left the role baked into 136 of 136 position titles. L1177-1185 adjacency walked instead of reading `fromPositionId`. L1002 `giAllows` falling through to a name heuristic. L2530 `s[0]` instead of the side's own `sv`.
RULE: if the data states it, read it — and a derivation that returns the SAME answer for the whole corpus is not a derivation, it is a constant with a function around it.

findings.title: CLASS 8: A single-slot resource with many writers and no declared owner
findings.detail:
9 instances, always discovered as "the message/frame/scroll I wrote is not there any more". L549-552 `setEvent` has ONE slot and the roll overwrites it "within a couple of seconds, so the toast alone never reached a real recipient". L2886 arrival copy must be HELD, not fired at t=0. L1309-1318 "Decide 1…" got stuck; fixed by making the countdown OWN its lifetime with a stamp released by every other writer. L1319-1324 "Time's up" never reaches the screen at all — overwritten SYNCHRONOUSLY on the next line; still unfixed as of v1.128.1. L1401-1407 `HESITATE_HOLD` exists solely because that one slot would reproduce the defect, and `clearOptions()` must run BEFORE the sentence. L2875-2880 the camera: `updateCamera()` rewrites `camTarget` every frame, so every selection flight "used to be overwritten within one frame" — fixed with a LEASE. L1652-1654 "ONE rAF OWNS `scrollLeft`". L780 `_bumpStageVer()` is the ONE writer of `_stageVer`. L2863 the announcer slot snapshotted across a replay.
RULE: a single-slot resource needs a stamped owner and an explicit lifetime (hold/lease/latch), never an assumption that your write is the last one.

findings.title: CLASS 9: The measurement is sound and its SUBJECT is wrong — canon numbers that do not reproduce
findings.detail:
8 instances. L2255-2261 the opponent-gap figure (9.1 / 23.2% / 2476) "was measuring a set the model never holds… it was not a bad measurement, it was a measurement of the wrong thing — and it disclosed the gap at roughly half its real size", with the file's own verdict: "A canon number nobody can reproduce is worse than no number." L2528-2531 "THE CONTENT FIGURE IS 115 OF 136 (85%), NOT 85 OF 136 (62%)" — and it read 84 on the day it was written; no threshold reproduces 85. L2094-2107 the tray-drag premise "rested on a reading taken 450ms after touchend" — "the measurement was confounded, so the premise was never proven". L1361-1365 a 340px sweep read OTHER nodes' labels. L2445-2448 a raw-innerHTML jargon check hits `class="paceVal"` and "reports a leak that is not on screen". L2884 `body[data-share-cue]` made every measurement "silently become the whole 390x844 viewport". L849 the "0 disagreements" figure. L1471-1475 the truncated blast-radius grep.
RULE: every canon figure carries its SET DEFINITION and the exact command that recomputes it, in the same sentence — a number without a reproduction recipe is a story.
findings.evidence: Two figures in this file have already been re-measured and found wrong (opponent gap ~2x understated; 85→115 of 136). At least one more is knife-edge by the file's own admission (L2304 "`> 0.10 on 276` is a knife-edge count").

findings.title: CLASS 10: A fallback that substitutes a plausible value and never says it fired
findings.detail:
8 instances — the runtime twin of Class 1, and the reason Class 1's bugs survived so long. L869-874 "A missing `cal` does not crash — `calSuccess()` returns null and `moveChance` falls back to `0.36 + dom*0.1`", so every submission printed ~45.5-45.7% and looked fine. L3027 "54 of 136 positions had an empty hand and ran entirely on the fallback". L1188-1189 `posIdx` fell back to the technique itself: "1,331 of 2,934 nodes staged a roll ON A TECHNIQUE NODE". L2313-2315 an empty outcome branch falls back to the whole table, and the fallback is chosen BEFORE the draw so the rng call count cannot depend on content. L1975-1976 `_evLamIdx()` falls back rather than guessing, "because a wrong λ block is a silently WRONG ranking, not a missing one". L2186-2190 / L3015 the no-candidates fallback relaxes ORIGIN but must never relax ROLE. The two good patterns are L791 `mc_pool_cold` and L845 `land_warm_stalled`.
RULE: every fallback emits a named beat or a counter — a fallback that produces plausible output is strictly worse than a crash, because it buys months of silence.

findings.title: CLASS 11: Reading stored state where the renderer uses derived state
findings.detail:
Self-counted to "the third time" at L1020; the real count is 5+ and each rediscovery cost a different surface. L1828-1830 the root cause stated once: "code reading `n.y` where the renderer draws at `LY(n)`" — the lift is ~37px at roll zoom. Instances: the hover label and THE TAP HANDLER (L1841-1844, clicking a visible orb "matched NOTHING"); `rollFromPosition`'s camera aim (L1865-1868); `graph-naming`'s `parkOn` AND its `profile` plus `url-arrival`'s re-derivation (L1020-1025); the mutation confirmation at L1701. The same shape in a different quantity: L993-997 `deg` (geometry, split) vs `siteDeg` (state, whole) — reading the split number in `movePotential` "would halve a value the escape tray prints".
RULE: when the renderer derives a value, publish the derivation (`this._LY = LY`) and make it the ONLY conversion any consumer or spec may use; the stored field is an input, never a position.

findings.title: CLASS 12: Nothing in a permanent namespace can be deleted — retire by ceasing to read
findings.detail:
8 instances across three storage layers. Settings: L2384-2390 "A SETTINGS KEY CANNOT BE DELETED" — `_pullAndMerge` has "no tombstone", so "a key deleted locally is unconditionally RE-ADDED by the first pull from any device that still carries it"; same shape named for `studyOrder` and `challengePinnedTrack`. Lists: L369-374 add-wins merge means "a DELETE loses to a stale device" (deliberate). Wire: L339-341 "v1 still decodes, forever — a code is a permanent promise like an ordinal". Ordinals: L309-312 "retired, not removed". URLs: L651-652 `?variant=legacy` and L1087-1090 `?dual=iso|fixed|force` are "accepted-and-ignored, not rejected". API: L2550 `keepCoach` accepted-and-ignored. And the inverse trap at L2913: an auto-flip driven by state rather than by a one-time mint "would re-enable it on every device forever through settings LWW". L417-421 is the design counterpart — do not persist keys minted from `Date.now()`.
RULE: in any append-only or tombstone-free store (URL, wire code, ordinal, LWW settings key), retirement means stop READING and say so where the reader used to be; never prune, never reject.

findings.title: CLASS 13: The harness is not the product — assertions satisfiable by what the harness omits
findings.detail:
7 instances. L2870 `test.use({reducedMotion})` leaves `matchMedia` FALSE "so a spec relying on the fixture option asserts nothing and passes forever". L1690-1692 "there is no film strip under the harness (the DSL serves `{}` for dossier chunks)" — an assertion measured against a surface that does not exist there. L2812-2813 "journeys about the fold must AUTHOR content — the DSL serves `{}`, so most states legitimately have no `More` under test". L1791-1794 "a screenshot taken under the harness photographs the harness, not the product". L785-792 MC distractors must not depend on residency or "network timing would pick the options and rigged journeys would drift". L2945 "the harness aborts non-localhost requests" — which is why a `.catch` is load-bearing. L923-926 the landing card ANIMATES IN, so "a camera read taken inside one `advance()` describes nothing".
RULE: beside every assertion, name what the harness does NOT serve — if the absence alone would satisfy the assertion, the assertion is about the harness.

findings.title: CLASS 14: CI runs a subset of the chain a human runs, or an allow-list that rots silently
findings.detail:
7 instances, all found at once in v1.104.6 and never generalised. L853 `votes-refresh.yml` ran bare `regenerate_graph.py` and committed a graph.json "stripping `strength` from 4,464 of 4,465 nodes" — the file's own rule, stated and then not applied elsewhere: "CI must never run a subset of the chain a human runs." L852 `e2e-full.yml` tarred six allow-listed paths so "the PR gate for BOTH main and dev could not pass" — "an allow-list rots silently and this one predated every spec that broke on it". L855 `ci-validate.yml`'s paths filter omitted `globalGraphLayout.json`, the INPUT its own ordinal gate reads, and `neural/src/**`. L857 Node 20 EOL in three workflows; `seo-monitor.yml` ran Python with no `setup-python`; `serve` — the server every e2e gate needs — was only in the lockfile. And the standing hazard: L318-319, L604, L3085 "deploy does not run root `npm run build`… the workflows re-list steps inline", which is the mechanism that lets any new build step be silently absent in production.
RULE: deploy invokes the same umbrella script a human invokes; if steps must be re-listed, a gate asserts the two lists are equal, and no emitted path is ever allow-listed (use --exclude).

findings.title: CLASS 15: A read taken on a frame where the value is not yet real
findings.detail:
6 instances. L923-926 "a camera read taken inside one `advance()` describes nothing" — the card's top was 588 on one frame and 376 on the next; "a second bare `advance` is NOT enough; an intervening `page.evaluate` is what forces layout". L1872-1881 the band "FLICKERED FRAME TO FRAME" because card and film mount on different frames, and "an UNDOCKED element is not a constraint" — `rect.top` reads 0 for one frame and threw the camera. L912-919 the card is built 0.6s AFTER the frame that measures the band. L2635-2640 "`parkOn` pauses, and `this.now` IS the game clock" — a paused roll froze `age` and the floor assertion passed against a build with the glow deleted. L822 "a blur from DETACH is not a decision" — Chrome dispatches it while `isConnected` still reads TRUE. L2098-2100 a reading taken 450ms after touchend measured a state the app had already reset.
RULE: before reading a measured value, prove the thing measured has laid out and the clock you depend on is running; "not yet laid out" is SKIP, and a paused clock freezes every age-derived assertion into a false pass.

findings.title: CLASS 16: A latch with no enumerated lifter
findings.detail:
6 instances, and the file supplies its own audit tool at L1579 without generalising it. L1562-1582 `_bgRestore()` "had exactly ONE caller, `setPaused(false)`, so the only way back was the PLAY BUTTON" — the stand-down had been un-liftable-by-tap since it shipped; the app did all its work "underneath a suppression that nobody lifted". The transferable artefact is right there: "`_landHidden()` asks FOUR holders… Any one of them stuck leaves a built, mounted, correctly populated card invisible while every other surface behaves. When a report says 'nothing happens but the node lights up', read the holders before reading the render path." L1882-1884 `userActiveNow()` measures the GAME clock, so on a paused board one click "latched 'the user is active' FOREVER and silently disabled v1.114.2's staged tracking". L904 `_urlSeeded` set and never read. L822 the `_listEditClosedAt` 400ms latch. The good pattern: one latch per pauser (L2731 `_landAutoPaused`, L832 `_paneAutoPaused`, L2863 `_replayAutoPaused`) so releasing gives back only the pause you took.
RULE: every suppression flag declares its complete set of lifters at the definition, and every multi-holder surface gets a `_xHidden()`-style audit that names which holder is standing.

findings.title: CLASS 17: A probe is not a gate — a surviving mutant is a missing spec, not a nuisance
findings.detail:
6 instances, and the file catches itself repeating it two versions running. L1357-1360 "M2 survived — because the mobile framing had been PROBED and never pinned by a journey. A probe is evidence for a commit message; only a spec is a gate." L1524-1526 "the kicker mutant SURVIVED the first red-proof pass because no journey covered it — the same 'a probe is not a gate' lesson as v1.128.1's mobile framing, two versions running." L2468-2472 mutant L7 survived "the version of that test that poked the key directly, because the handler never ran" — the journey must drive the real BUTTON. L2094-2103 the tray drag: "A change whose own mutant cannot kill its test is not evidence", and it was reverted for exactly that. L1696-1712 six mutants, four kills, and "the two non-kills are the finding" — written into the spec header so it cannot later be read as covered. L2146-2151 the mutant that needs THREE edits because two build gates refuse the bad wire first.
RULE: mutate every claim; a surviving mutant means the claim has no gate — and record non-kills in the spec's own header so nobody later reads the spec as covering them.

findings.title: CLASS 18: The name you queried is not the object you meant (selector and scope collisions)
findings.detail:
6 instances. L2884 `body[data-share-cue]` collided with the cue BUTTON's own attribute, so `querySelector` returned `<body>` and "every 'where is the cue' measurement silently becomes the whole 390x844 viewport" — three share journeys red. L594-598 `HTMLRewriter`'s `.on("title", …)` "matches by element NAME, and the shell carries a second `<title>` — inside the search button's inline SVG"; fixed with `title[data-share-title]`, "a marker `build_share_shell.mjs` writes and asserts exactly once". L365-367 two source files "share ONE scope in the bundle, so no top-level name may collide". L354-356 that duplicate-name guard "used to scan only `function|const`, so a colliding `let` walked past it into the same SyntaxError it exists to prevent". L1629-1631 "`_lastPairLabel` holds whichever group drew LAST in the frame" — re-reading returned the wrong label (idx 145 where 1682 was expected). L817 a CSS-border triangle's computed `width` is 8px, not 0.
RULE: scope every selector to a marker you own and assert it appears exactly once; never query by a shape (element name, attribute, computed width) that another object can also have.

findings.title: CLASS 19: One fact printed by two subsystems — the 'stated twice' defect
findings.detail:
6 instances, and the file connects two of them but not the set. L1264-1276 the pair label group: two different answers to one question on one graph, "the same 'printed twice' defect the in-node pass was deleted for in v1.114.0, arriving by a different door". L1504-1509 the focus kicker said "position: top" beside a shape that already means position — "the same 'stated twice' defect the in-node pass was deleted for". L810 the knowledge header "with the tab subtitles it triple-stated the score". L2677-2680 owner: «the "The Chill Dog" and "Bottom" is repeated info». L2779-2782 the option-detail overview printed twice — "205 of 997 (21%) are >80% the same text". L2793-2805 "Attacks from here" restated the hand and got it wrong doing it (only 11.5% legitimately yours). L1845-1852 the per-node hover label suppressed for a focused pair member "or the name would print twice".
RULE: one fact, one channel — before adding a word, check whether shape, position, colour or an adjacent surface already carries it, and delete rather than duplicate.

findings.title: CLASS 20: Two places must hold one value — derive N−1 or gate byte-equality AND omission
findings.detail:
6 instances. L571-583 `/l/*` headers come from "two mutually exclusive header sources… and the failure available here is them DISAGREEING" — `SHARE_CACHE_CONTROL` is byte-identical to `_headers`, gated by checks 6-8. L585-592 the gate then had to be extended to OMISSION: "a `SHARE_STATIC_HEADERS` block that is declared but never written into the response passed every value comparison while shipping none of the headers", and it had to run against the EMITTED `_headers`, not only its canonical input. L2945 `https://api.github.com` lives in `connect-src` "in THREE places". L3280-3293 the affiliate disclosure lives in one block "and NOWHERE else", read by `check_affiliate_surface.py` as its source of truth. L600-604 `l.html` is derived from the BUILT `index.html` — "one source of truth". L365-367 one cap under two names, "a test pins them equal". L2535 one colour under a shared constant "so the two sites that write it cannot drift again".
RULE: when a value must exist in N places, derive N−1 of them; if you cannot, gate byte-equality AND presence, because a value that is declared but never applied passes every equality check.

findings.title: CLASS 21: An index-keyed or positional format fails plausibly and reports nothing
findings.detail:
6 instances. L1124-1132 is the fullest statement: "Nothing in the format is self-describing… A wrong remap still finds rows, still prints integers on every card, and prints the WRONG technique's number on each — no exception, no warning, no blank", which is why the gate compares whole structures and asserts >1200 cards carry a real mark "so it cannot pass on a build where `_ev` came back empty on BOTH sides". L3004-3011 `s` is two different pairs behind one shape. L3025-3030 `posId` was a path where `fromPositionId` is a slug — origin filter rejected everything, 54/136 empty hands. L864-868 the `cal` key's flat-kebab vs authored-path spelling — 0 of 297 matched. L993-997 `deg` vs `siteDeg`. L758-760 `links` as index pairs, safe ONLY because "indices never leave the file".
RULE: an index/positional join gets a whole-structure DIFFERENTIAL against a known-good graph plus a non-triviality floor — never a non-null count, which a wrong-but-complete remap satisfies perfectly.

findings.title: CLASS 22: An assertion stricter than its own claim goes red on a correct build
findings.detail:
5 instances, and the file names three of them together at L1367 ("one mistake wearing three hats — pinning an incidental fact instead of the thing that was asked for"). Those three: "nothing is drawn above the name" (the name's own ascenders reach into that band); "nothing is drawn at merge scale" (false — the ordinary label takes the hover back); "the announcer is blank after staging" (false — the staged landing may legitimately say something else). L1623-1631 three MORE specs pinned to where the label used to be, all red on a correct build the moment the block moved. L2597-2608 five mutants were needed "to get the statistic right" and the two survivors are the lesson — a sparse ring measured empty sky and an angular-coverage score was already saturated by the dealt hand. The working shape, twice: a CONTROL FRAME plus a DIFFERENTIAL, "where the name's constant contribution cancels" (L1373) and "everything the graph would draw anyway subtracts to zero" (L2605).
RULE: assert the DIFFERENTIAL the change is about, against a control frame — and after relaxing an assertion, re-run its mutant so "less strict" does not become "less able to fail" (L1380).

findings.title: CLASS 23: Order decided by an accident of iteration
findings.detail:
5 instances, three of them user-visible. L303-308 the founding case: `rglob('*.json')` is unsorted and the layout derives its node list from "`adjacency` DICT INSERTION order seeded by that iteration — so adding one content file renumbers pre-existing entries"; an index-encoded share link "would silently open a DIFFERENT set of techniques, with no error anywhere". L2119-2124 "`Array#sort` is stable, so a comparator that can return 0 silently hands the decision to the node index" — and 21 pairs tie on EDGE, odds AND attempt%, so the name tiebreak is load-bearing. L1965-1971 `movePotential` returned a constant 1 for every submission, so the cap "dealt the first ten ALPHABETICALLY" and truncated the state's most-attempted move. L1304-1305 "a tie decided by array order picks a different pair per run, and every threshold is a function of which pair got picked". L1141-1147 a `.slice(0,120)` cap over a doubled list HALVED reach.
RULE: any ordering a user or a URL can see needs a strict total order whose final tiebreak is stable CONTENT — never array index, dict insertion order or filesystem order — and a cap over an unordered list is a random sample.

findings.title: CLASS 24: A constant in the code standing in for a value in the data
findings.detail:
4 instances, and the file states the tell precisely at L2128: "AN EXACT TIE ON SCREEN IS A TIE IN THE DATA, NEVER A CONSTANT IN THE CODE. This is the shape of the bug the feature replaced (`+100` on every submission)." Instances: L1965-1971 `if (n.ty === "submissions") return 1` made the sort key a constant across all 297; L869-874 the dominance fallback "prices the whole corpus at 2 distinct values" and printed a fabricated success rate on ~289 of 1,204 cards where the authored range is 10-74%; L1895 "'30+ weak spots' was the DAILY GOAL" — `get("dailyGoal",30)+"+"`, so it read the same for a player with 3 gaps and one with 700 and never moved; L2554 the `withDeck` no-op filter. The gate shape that catches it (L2128-2133): where printed values are bit-identical, assert the underlying wire rows are identical too — 42 of 42.
RULE: a value that is identical across a whole category on screen is a constant until proven otherwise — assert that on-screen ties correspond to ties in the source rows, and count the distinct values a field actually produces.

findings.title: CLASS 25: Deleting a component deletes its telemetry and its capability, and no gate reports it
findings.detail:
5 instances. L701-705 deleting `AffiliateTracking` "removed the only emitter of the `affiliate_clickout` / `related_system_card_click` / `system_page_view` PostHog events. The affiliate links themselves are untouched and still earn; the *measurement* stopped." L707-715 deleting `SystemProgress` removed a whole UX from 48 pages and "was the only emitter of `system_node_marked_known`…  this is a capability *lost*, not merely moved. Any per-system completion figure in PostHog dashboards goes flat from the deploy date; do not read that as a usage collapse." L716-723 its dead markup still ships (~600 B × 48 pages) because the shell is emitted by a template, not the component. L1411-1414 retiring `auto_pick` ("retiring one means deleting it" — the cue) broke four gen specs. L2550 the coach deletion took eleven specs, a funnel property and a localStorage writer with it.
RULE: treat an emitter deletion as a data-loss event — enumerate in the same commit every event, capability and dashboard it was the ONLY source of, and check for dead markup emitted by templates rather than by the component.

findings.title: CLASS 26: Shared mutable environment — the run measured someone else's artifact
findings.detail:
5 instances. L616-625 / L3098 ports: a config with `reuseExistingServer: true` on a shared :8123 means "whichever WORKTREE started :8123 first owns it and every later run tests THAT worktree's `source/public`" — measured, a run was served a 343,153-byte `neural.js` from a sibling worktree where its own was 364,190; "a config that reuses a server started by ANOTHER worktree tests someone else's `source/public`, which makes any result from it unreportable". L3096 the Playwright browser cache was keyed per package-lock hash in a repo that bumps the version every commit, so "a lockfile key missed every run while still uploading 261 MiB". L1217-1226 a flake seen twice, "both times the machine was rebuilding a bundle in the background" — chased with a matched-pair measurement and Fisher exact rather than waved away. The project memory records the same shape a third way: `npm run build` does not rebuild the neural bundle, so a stale served bundle makes neural journeys time out and "looks like contention/regression but isn't".
RULE: every suite owns a dedicated port with `reuseExistingServer:false`; cache keys name the RESOLVED artifact version, never a file that changes on every commit; and a result taken while another process could write the tree under test is not a result.

findings.title: CLASS 27: An unrigged rng() tag is not a chosen branch — it is a lottery ticket
findings.detail:
3 instances but a very high blast radius, since it invalidates every green run that preceded discovery. L1762-1789 `graph-naming`'s bloom journey "has been a coin toss on this branch in every version it has existed" because `dsl.land()` rigs only `ai-skill`/`role`/`max-moves` and `rng("opp-finish")` was a live `Math.random`; measured at 7.7% per run, so "P(four consecutive green full suites) ≈ 0.73, so the three earlier clean reports were never evidence of absence". The fix is stated as a deductive claim, not a statistical one: rig the draw so the branch is UNREACHABLE, and say explicitly that the counts are corroboration, not proof. L1217-1226 and L1465-1469 are the two other flakes in the file, both recorded as "NOT fixed and not caused" with their own measurements.
RULE: when a journey's subject is what happens AFTER an exchange, rig every rng() tag that can end the exchange early — and never read N green runs as evidence of absence without computing P(all green) at the observed rate.

findings.title: CLASS 28: A truncated or narrowed survey before a rename, deletion or retirement
findings.detail:
2 explicit instances but the file gives it its own heading, and it is the cheapest trap to avoid. L1471-1475: "A TRUNCATED GREP IS HOW YOU MISS A CONSUMER. The blast radius was first measured with `grep -rn auto_pick … | head`, which showed the sound catalog, the app and ONE gen spec — so the retirement looked cheap. The real list is 7 gen specs + 2 core specs, and the core one only surfaced when the full suite went red. Never pipe the survey that decides a rename through `head`." The same shape, differently caused: L852 the six-path allow-list that "predated every spec that broke on it"; L2064-2069 `.ng-seemore` was never in the pointer-capture early-return list, and "any new fixed overlay with controls goes in that list" is a hand-maintained enumeration with no gate.
RULE: a survey that decides a rename or deletion is counted in full (`| wc -l` first, then read all) and, where the enumeration is hand-maintained, replaced with a gate that derives it.

findings.title: CLASS 29: The inner gate is weaker than the outer gate it is supposed to protect
findings.detail:
3 instances. L854 "The PR ratchet was weaker than the deploy gate it protects: `graph_validation_baseline.json` allowed 76 errors while both deploys hard-fail on the first. Actual errors are 0, so the baseline is now 0." L1749-1760 the `e2e:gen` 13-red baseline was quoted as "the same 13 names" across FOUR versions of gates blocks "without ever writing them down, which makes the phrase uncheckable" — a baseline nobody can verify is not a baseline; two of the thirteen also burn 4.0m each on a timeout, most of the suite's wall time. L1243 / L1456-1464 the baseline then moved 13 → 14 and the file had to argue each name individually.
RULE: a tolerance baseline must be at least as strict as the gate downstream of it, and it must ENUMERATE what it tolerates by name — an aggregate count is unfalsifiable and drifts into permanent noise.

findings.title: META: the file names 4 classes and misses ~25 — organise the trap list by class, not by version
findings.detail:
The file explicitly numbers exactly four recurrences: the `setPointerCapture`/hit-test class ("Fourth" L2840, "Fifth" L2852, "SIXTH INSTANCE" L2064), the docked-chrome class ("the third instance" L1804), the `n.y`-vs-`LY(n)` class ("for the third time" L1020), and the roleIdx-vs-valIdx heuristic class ("the same defect class" L2541, "second stale implementation" L1183). Every other class above recurred across sections written months apart with NO cross-reference — the strongest evidence being that the fix for Class 1 was independently invented five times (`build.mjs` throws per rule L848; the cal emitter refuses <95% L883; the EDGE join gate L2148; the `mc_pool_cold` beat L791; the `land_warm_stalled` beat L845) and named zero times. The narratives are chronologically ordered, so two instances of one class are hundreds of lines and many months apart; a reader hits the trap before reaching the section that describes it.
RULE: the inline survivor must be a CLASS-INDEXED trap list — class name, the rule, and the instance count — because a trap is only useful when you can find it BEFORE you fall in, and version order guarantees you cannot.
findings.evidence: Measured on the file: 3,338 lines; 116 occurrences of 'measured', 42 of 'mutant', 17 owner quotes — but only 5 lines contain an explicit instance-count of a recurring class.

archaeologist.headline: The file's largest failure class is one it never names — \"absence produces a plausible answer\" (17 instances: a check that NameError'd into silence, a harness rule naming a URL the app never fetches, two build rewrites whose 'from' strings were absent, a join that shipped fabricated odds on ~289 of 1,204 cards) — and the repo independently invented the identical fix five separate times (emit a positive coverage count and fail on zero) without ever connecting them.

architect.headline: CLAUDE.md has no working retrieval path at all — its own outline lies (an empty `###` at L295, and two headings named for v1.127.0 and v1.124.0 that between them swallow 133,749 chars covering ~40 unrelated versions), so the split's real job is not shrinking the file but giving it an index keyed on what the reader is about to touch; and the two-destination plan is short one destination, because a third of the narrative mass is neither trap nor history but the app's only live behaviour spec.

findings.title: The outline lies: headings do not bound their content, so no heading is a retrieval path
findings.detail: Measured section spans show the `###` structure is decorative. L295 `### ONE front-end: the legacy Quartz page UI was deleted (v1.80.0)` has a 67-char body and is *immediately* followed by another heading — its actual body sits 332 lines later at L627 under `### Training System (SRS) — embedded UX (v1.20.0+)`, a title that says the opposite of its content (that block is about the DELETION of the SRS UX). `### THE PAIR JOURNEYS COME HOME (v1.127.0)` (L1672-2152, 45,299 chars) contains v1.114.3, v1.114.4, v1.104.5, v1.104.4, v1.104.3, EDGE v1.118.0, v1.123.0 and v1.119.0. `### WINNING vs NOT LOSING (v1.124.0)` (L2413-3044, 88,450 chars) contains v1.127.1, v1.104.x, v1.82.3, v1.114.x, v1.101.x, v1.106.5, v1.81.4, v1.74.0, v1.70.0, v1.75.0, v1.95.1, v1.105.x and v1.103.x. Order is neither ascending nor descending (v1.129.6 at L1532 precedes v1.129.5 at L1555; v1.125.0 at L928 precedes v1.126.0 at L1077). Consequence for the split: you cannot move 'the version narratives' by cutting at headings — the unit of movement is the bold-lead paragraph block (`^\*\*[A-Z]`), of which there are ~150. Any script or human doing the extraction must operate on that unit, and each extracted block must be re-titled with the version it actually describes.
findings.evidence: awk per-section char counts; grep -n '^\*\*[A-Z]' over L1672-3044 lists 60+ bold blocks under two headings

findings.title: Reader-question inventory: 18 arrival questions and the shortest honest path to each
findings.detail:
Every question below is one a human or agent actually arrives holding; the routing target is what the ~50k CLAUDE.md must either answer or point at in one hop.
1. 'Can I edit this file?' (content/*.md vs *.json vs templates/) → CLAUDE.md §1 Non-negotiables, inline, 3 lines.
2. 'What do I run to regenerate/validate/build?' → CLAUDE.md §4 command table, one row each + `--help`.
3. 'What am I allowed to commit / how do I version?' → CLAUDE.md §1.
4. 'What is a role-node / hub / what may an outcome point at?' → CLAUDE.md §3 invariant list (inline, ~30 lines); depth in docs/Architecture.md.
5. 'I'm editing app.src.jsx near X — what will I break?' → CLAUDE.md §6 TRAP LIST, grep by symbol. THE primary question; today it has no answer path.
6. 'Why does the option card print a signed integer?' → docs/Neural.md (new) EDGE section; CLAUDE.md carries a 3-line definition + pointer.
7. 'My click works in tests and not in the browser.' → §6 trap `attachInput`/`setPointerCapture`.
8. 'A built card is invisible.' → §6 trap `_landHidden` four holders.
9. 'My e2e is red — mine or known?' → e2e/gen/ledger.json + a known-red policy line in §8. NOT a name list in CLAUDE.md.
10. 'How do I assert something about the canvas/camera/mouse honestly?' → §6 test-honesty traps + docs/Testing.md.
11. 'Can I delete this dead-looking file/component?' → §6 'looks deletable, isn't' registry.
12. 'Why is this the way it is / did we already try the other thing?' → docs/Changelog-Archive.md, grep by symbol.
13. 'Where are lists stored and why did my capture vanish?' → §6 `siteIdOf` trap + docs/Neural.md.
14. 'Why can't I delete a settings key?' → §6 persistence trap (no tombstone in per-key LWW).
15. 'I'm adding an overlay — what z / what rules?' → §6 z-ladder + overlay traps.
16. 'Success-rate format? wikilink format?' → CLAUDE.md §7 quick ref; depth in docs/Content.md.
17. 'Can I reword the affiliate disclosure?' → CLAUDE.md §7, machine-pinned block.
18. 'Which doc do I read for X?' → CLAUDE.md §0 doc map — the only place the reader should have to guess.

findings.title: Proposed CLAUDE.md skeleton: 11 sections, 50,000 chars, with the arithmetic that makes it fit
findings.detail:
§0 Identity, boundary declaration, doc map — 2,000. §1 Non-negotiables (forbidden actions, file-size limits, versioning, pre-commit, owner process rules) — 2,500. §2 Repo map (compressed tree, SOURCE-vs-GENERATED rule) — 2,000. §3 Data model & graph invariants — 4,500. §4 Pipeline & commands — 6,000. §5 Neural app: current state in one page (one front-end, delivery contract, pane law, hand/EDGE headline, pair, persistence, z-ladder) each as a 3-6 line statement + pointer to docs/Neural.md — 9,000. §6 THE TRAP LIST — 14,000. §7 Content standards quick ref + CANONICAL-DISCLOSURE block — 4,000. §8 Testing, gates and what a gate is worth — 3,500. §9 Where to write what (C-UD, archive-append protocol) — 1,500. §10 Resources — 1,000. Sum = 50,000 exactly.
THE ARITHMETIC THAT MATTERS: today's non-narrative material is 15,026 (L1-294) + 27,971 (L3045-3351) = 42,997 chars. A 14,000-char trap list leaves 36,000 for it, so **the split alone does not reach 50k — the keep-material must itself shed ~7,000 chars (16%)**. The donor is identified and sufficient: the npm table is 16,723 chars because cells carry multi-paragraph prose (the `calibrate` row alone is ~1,900). Compressed to command + one line + `python3 scripts/X.py --help`, it is ~6,000 — a 10,700 saving, which funds the trap list with 3,700 to spare. Second donor: §8 RESOURCES' PostHog dashboard table belongs in docs/SEO.md (~500).
findings.evidence: awk char counts: head 15,026 / narrative 291,246 / tail 27,971; npm-scripts section L3064-3103 = 16,723 chars

findings.title: The trap list is the product: organise by TRIGGER TOKEN, not by theme, and by CLASS, not by instance
findings.detail:
Two IA rules decide whether 14,000 chars of traps actually fires at the right moment.
(1) EVERY ENTRY OPENS WITH THE SYMBOL, FILE OR API IT FIRES ON, in backticks, so `grep attachInput CLAUDE.md` lands on it. The reader's arrival state is 'I am editing attachInput', never 'I am interested in input handling'. Theme grouping is a table-of-contents affordance and this file is never browsed — it is already resident.
(2) COLLAPSE INSTANCES INTO CLASSES. The file's own highest-value compression is already written and never applied: it says 'sixth instance of this repo's recurring bug class' about `setPointerCapture`, and re-narrates the same lesson six times across v1.81.3, v1.100.2, v1.101.5, v1.104.2, v1.123.0 and the landcard corner.
