One class entry — 'a fixed overlay carrying controls must be in attachInput's pointerdown early-return list; capture retargets pointerup so the browser resolves the click to the common ancestor; `locator.click()` masks it entirely' — plus a bare instance list, is ~350 chars and strictly more useful than 6,000 chars of narrative, because it generalises to the *next* overlay.
BUDGET CHECK: I count ~52 distinct traps in the current text across six classes (input/overlay 10, canvas-geometry 5, test-honesty 11, data-join 8, persistence 3, CI-tooling 7, domain-model 5, plus the deletable registry). At 14,000 chars that is ~270 chars each — enough for rule + the symptom that made it findable + the trigger token, which is exactly what a trap needs and no more. Do not budget below 12,000; below that the symptom gets cut, and a trap without its symptom cannot be recognised from inside the bug.
findings.evidence: grep -c: 'setPointerCapture' 3, 'pointer-events' 8, 'locator.click' 4, 'mutant' 38, '_dockLandCard' 8, 'pairMid' 10 — all cross-cutting, all currently narrated per-version

findings.title: Trap class — input & overlay (the repo's single most expensive recurring class)
findings.detail: Keep inline, as ~10 one-liners keyed on their trigger token: (a) `attachInput` pointerdown calls `setPointerCapture` on the wrap → pointerup retargets → every control inside a fixed overlay is dead to the MOUSE while keyboard and `locator.click()` pass; the early-return list is the fix and every new fixed overlay with controls joins it. (b) `pointer-events:auto` is inherited and load-bearing — the overlay root disables it, the canvas hit-tests above anything that does not re-enable it. (c) `opacity:0` + `pointer-events:none` is NOT inert — hit-testing ignores opacity and children re-enable pointer-events inline; `visibility:hidden` is what removes a subtree from hit-testing. Three sibling hide-sites still write the leaky form. (d) `style.color = ""` deletes an inline declaration, it does not restore one — write the constant. (e) fixed chrome must dock off a MEASURED rect, never a constant, when the thing it clears is computed (`_dockLandCard`, `_dockLandFilm`, `_dockOptionHint`, and the still-open phone challenge-cue collision — three fixed, one open). (f) the app wrap is `position:fixed` = its own stacking context, so a deliberate screen must portal to the root plane; z bands 1-9/10-49/50-79/90-99. (g) a 44px thumb target must not set a 24px row's layout box — negative margin. (h) `_landHidden()` has FOUR holders (`_landPaneHid`, `_traySup`, `_bgDown`, `_detailCtx`); when a report says 'nothing happens but the node lights up', read the holders before the render path. (i) a CSS-border triangle computes to width 8px, not 0. (j) `scroll-snap` on a many-item tray reads to the user as 'scrolling is not supported'.

findings.title: Trap class — canvas geometry: never convert a node to a screen position from stored coordinates
findings.detail: Keep inline. This class bit four separate times (v1.114.3 hover+tap, v1.114.4 rollFromPosition, v1.125.0 in two specs) and the file says so without ever stating it once as a rule. The rule: the renderer draws at `LY(n)` / `pairMid(n)`, not `n.y`; any code — app OR spec — that turns a node into a screen point goes through `_LY`/`pairMid`, both of which are identities on an unpaired node. Companions: never assert camera behaviour by reading `camTarget` (the follow-cam rewrites it every frame) — project through `draw()`'s transform into the viewport rect; `this.now` IS the game clock, so a paused roll freezes `age` and a canvas assertion can pass against a frozen flare; anchor a label off `halfW(n)` (the drawn silhouette, widened 1.242r for a triangle, 1.18r for a diamond) rather than `n.r * scale`; measure text on a SCRATCH context because `this.ctx.font` is mid-frame state. Trigger tokens for grep: `LY`, `pairMid`, `camTarget`, `halfW`, `this.now`.

findings.title: Trap class — test honesty: the rules that stop a green suite from meaning nothing
findings.detail: Keep inline; this is the class most likely to be re-learned expensively because a violation LOOKS like success. (a) `locator.click()` scrolls into view and dispatches on the element — it cannot prove mouse reachability; `j.clickByMouse` is the only claim. (b) A probe is evidence for a commit message; only a spec is a gate — stated twice (v1.128.1 mobile framing, v1.129.1 kicker) after mutants survived. (c) NEVER assert a render by re-implementing it: the v1.126.0 audit's own probe re-declared `nodes.filter(n => n.rep && …)` and reported 'identical' about a search path that was doubling every hit. (d) A journey that leaves a gameplay `rng()` tag unrigged has bought a lottery ticket — `graph-naming` was a 7.7% coin toss for its whole life on `opp-finish`. (e) Gates can be STRUCTURALLY blind: `payload-first-hand` pins a 7-card hand so it reports identical bytes with and without the hand cap; `replay-digest` rigs a single-success-cell submission so it cannot see the outcome-kernel fix; a green run from either is not evidence about the change. (f) An assertion stricter than its own claim goes red on a CORRECT build — assert the DIFFERENTIAL, where the constant contribution cancels. (g) `test.use({reducedMotion})` leaves `matchMedia` FALSE; use `page.emulateMedia`. (h) Every port dedicated, `reuseExistingServer:false` — a shared port serves another worktree's `source/public`. (i) `npm run build` does NOT rebuild the neural bundle; a stale served `neural.js` makes neural journeys 240s-timeout and look like contention.
findings.evidence: e2e/ holds 11 playwright configs; 69 journey specs, 98 gen specs; the 240s-timeout trap currently lives ONLY in memory (project_build_excludes_neural_bundle.md)

findings.title: Trap class — id, slug and join spelling (the class that fails silently by construction)
findings.detail: Keep inline. Every member of this class produced wrong output with no exception, no warning and no red gate. (a) A node's ARRAY INDEX can never go in a URL — `rglob` + dict insertion order renumber on any content add; ordinals are permanent, append-only, retired-not-removed. (b) The `cal` join needs a three-rung key ladder (`as-is` → `slash→hyphen` → `slugify(title)`) because a layout id keeps the authored PATH while `graph.json` keys on one flat kebab token — 294 of 297 submissions shipped fabricated ~45.6% odds for months. Any emitter doing this join must refuse to write a wire below a coverage floor and PRINT the coverage. (c) `s` is `[top,bottom]` for a POSITION and `[attacker,defender]` for a TECHNIQUE — index by performer, not by side. (d) A position's `posId` is its LEAF slug; a submission's leaf (`from-mount`) is not a slug — 54 of 136 positions had an empty hand from this. (e) A non-recursive glob missed 54 nested position files, which then inherited their parent's polarity. (f) Lists hold SITES: `siteIdOf` normalises in the list LAYER (writer *and* every membership reader), not at the capture button. (g) Do NOT role-split `adj` — several readers walk it deliberately role-agnostically. (h) `cal.ev` goes on BOTH pair halves whole; filing per-member makes the answer depend on which orb you stand on.

findings.title: Trap class — persistence: a settings key can never be deleted, and a delete loses to a stale device
findings.detail: Keep inline, ~4 lines. `_pullAndMerge`'s per-key settings merge is `if (!(sk in merged) || ct > lt)` with NO tombstone, so a key deleted locally is unconditionally re-added by the first pull from any device that still carries it. The repo's answer is to stop READING the key and say so where the reader used to be — `cardOrder`, `studyOrder`, `challengePinnedTrack` are all dormant, not pruned. Companion: list reconciliation is ADD-WINS by deliberate choice (a delete loses to a stale device; deleting again is trivial, losing the class a coach already posted is not), and `srs` merge is later-`last`-wins with same-day tie → smaller ivl. Trigger tokens: `_pullAndMerge`, `ngMergeLists`, `dormant`.

findings.title: Trap class — CI and tooling: five ways a gate passed while doing nothing
findings.detail: Keep inline as one-liners; each is a general failure mode, not a fixed incident. (a) `git diff --quiet` reports NO CHANGE for an untracked file — `keepalive.yml` never committed anything, ever. (b) A bare `except Exception: return issues` swallowed a `NameError` so `check_position_type_vs_score` returned empty on every run and '0 disagreements' meant 'the check never executed'; a skip path must PRINT. (c) An ALLOW-LIST of packaged paths rots silently — package by default and `--exclude` explicitly (`e2e-full.yml` could not pass for either protected branch). (d) CI must never run a subset of the chain a human runs (`votes-refresh.yml` ran bare `regenerate_graph.py` and stripped `strength` from 4,464 of 4,465 nodes). (e) A rewrite/substitution table must THROW when a rule's `from` string is absent from the source — `build.mjs` only warned when EVERY rule missed, so two dead rules were invisible and the harness silently stopped receiving fixtures. (f) Never pipe the survey that decides a rename through `head` — the `auto_pick` retirement looked like 3 consumers and was 9. (g) A PR ratchet must not be weaker than the deploy gate it protects (baseline allowed 76 graph errors against a deploy that hard-fails on the first).

findings.title: Trap class — 'this looks deletable and is not' / 'this looks alive and is dead'
findings.detail: Keep inline as a short registry; it answers a question that is asked constantly and cannot be answered from the code. LOOKS DELETABLE, ISN'T: `AuthUI.tsx` + `scripts/authUI.inline.ts` render nothing but are the only static importer of `supabase.ts` (the `window.__bjjAuth` façade) and the only completer of a Google OAuth redirect-back — deleting either breaks signed-in users while every headless test stays green. `CategoryNav.tsx` is the site's only persistent static nav and NO GATE guards it (`check_seo_parity.py` scopes to `<article>`; `#sidebar-overlay` is a sibling of `#quartz-root`). `openListSession` has exactly one caller left (`[data-shared-drill]`) and it is the received-class study path. LOOKS ALIVE, IS DEAD: `renderDossier` and its subtree (`dossierSheetRef`, `_renderNodeQuestion`, `nodeQuestionFor`, `askFormat`, `jumpToState`) — verified, `_dossierIdx` is assigned `null` at five sites and a node index at none, so the L2636 mobile call can never fire; do not debug through it. The `#unlock-graph` / `[data-system-progress]` markup still ships on all 48 Systems pages with no script to activate it. The Forward catalog (`forward/shared/*`) is a DESIGN MOCK with no parity gate — retired rows survive there by default.
findings.evidence: grep -n '_dossierIdx\s*=' neural/src/app.src.jsx → 5 hits, all `= null`; call site at :2636 is therefore unreachable

findings.title: Keep inline: the graph topology invariants, compressed to a checkable list
findings.detail: §3 keeps what a reader can VIOLATE, and nothing else: bipartite position-role → technique → position-role; node types (role-nodes carry edges; bare hubs and `is_family:true` hubs are edgeless flashcard aggregators and are NOT navigable data nodes); the three edge types with their weight-sum rules (attempt% per role = 100, outcomes = 100, `result ∈ success|failure|counter`); `game-over` is the ONLY sink and only submissions reach it — a transition pointing at it is a misfiled finish; every `outcome.to` resolves to a role-node, a real submission, or `game-over`, never a bare hub, a family hub or a self-loop; `from_position` is origin METADATA, not a second edge; `opponentTransitions` exists nowhere and must not be reintroduced (derive in the consumer). Also keep the two-representations warning (`graph.json` role-based vs `globalGraphLayout.json` hub-collapsed) because conflating them is the standing error. Everything narrative about how these were arrived at goes to the archive; the JSON shapes and worked examples go to docs/Architecture.md, which already holds them.

findings.title: MUST NOT MOVE: the CANONICAL-DISCLOSURE block is machine-parsed by a deploy gate and an e2e spec
findings.detail: CLAUDE.md L3284-3286 carries `<!-- CANONICAL-DISCLOSURE:START -->` / `:END`. `scripts/check_affiliate_surface.py` (DOC = PROJECT_ROOT/'CLAUDE.md', L47) reads that exact block as the single source of truth for the FTC/ASA disclosure sentence and exits 1 on drift or on the block's absence; both deploy workflows call it, and `e2e/journeys/systems-surface.spec.ts:83` reads `../../CLAUDE.md` and asserts byte-identity in a real browser. Consequences for the split, all hard: the block stays in CLAUDE.md at the same path with the same markers; the surrounding §7 prose that explains WHY it lives there stays with it (~15 lines); and note that four scripts plus the spec name it as 'section 7' in their error messages, so renumbering sections silently degrades those messages — either preserve the number or update the five call sites in the same commit. This is the one place where a byte budget must lose to a legal gate.
findings.evidence: scripts/check_affiliate_surface.py:47,54-55,70; e2e/journeys/systems-surface.spec.ts:83,91,411; validate_json.py:327 cites '§7'

findings.title: The plan is short one destination: ~40-50k of live behaviour spec is neither trap nor history
findings.detail: The decided split has two buckets (condensed traps inline, narratives verbatim to the archive) and the corpus has three kinds of content. The third is CURRENT-STATE SPECIFICATION: how the app behaves today, written nowhere else. Examples that are not traps and are not history — pane law and the two body modes; the landing card's fixed read order and its three modes (`land`/`attempt`/`defense`); how a hand is dealt, ordered, frozen at deal time and clocked (`NG_DECISION_KNEE`, `NG_PREFETCH_CAP`); the EDGE model (V = p_win − λ·p_loss, B(s), the live-line `EDGE(p) = e0 + (p−p0)·c1 − Δ`, and the two honesty gaps); the derived pair (`rep`/partner, the two link kinds, `siteDeg`, the `cal` split); the share-link wire format and the four `/l/<code>` outcomes; Challenges/Game Knowledge/SRS scheduling; the sound catalog contract; the z ladder. Sending these verbatim to a CHANGELOG archive makes the app's only spec un-findable by anyone not searching by version number. RECOMMENDATION, compatible with the decision: create `docs/Neural.md` as NEWLY WRITTEN present-tense synthesis (~45k) — nothing is deleted, the narratives still go to the archive verbatim, and CLAUDE.md §5 carries a 9,000-char state summary that points into it. Without this doc, §5 is either wrong or 40k over budget.

findings.title: docs/Changelog-Archive.md: three indexes, a Status line, and a grep-first instruction
findings.detail:
250k in one file is ~62k tokens — if it is ever read whole it costs what CLAUDE.md costs today, so its structure must make partial retrieval the only reasonable behaviour.
HEADER (~1,200 chars): what it is; what it is NOT (never authoritative for current behaviour — CLAUDE.md and docs/ are); STALE BY CONSTRUCTION — every measurement is true as of its version, never re-verify a number from here without re-measuring; and the instruction 'grep this file, do not read it', with three worked grep examples.
INDEX A — VERSION (~8k): reverse-chronological, one line per entry, `[v1.129.6](#v1-129-6) — the opening flight aims at the card's band`. Newest first so the most-likely-relevant is at the top of the file.
INDEX B — SUBJECT (~10k): THE index that makes it navigable, because arrivals are 'I am touching X', not 'what happened in v1.121'. Symbol/file → versions: `attachInput` → 1.81.3, 1.100.2, 1.101.5, 1.104.2, 1.123.0; `rollCamTarget` → 1.103.2, 1.114.4, 1.128.1, 1.129.6; `_dockLandCard` → 1.81.3, 1.101.7, 1.103.1, 1.104.4. Generate it mechanically from backticked tokens; a hand-maintained one will rot.
INDEX C — DECISIONS AND THEIR REVERSALS (~3k): owner decisions with dates and their later reversals, so 'do not silently reinstate Edge' has a record (introduced v1.118.0, reversed v1.129.1) — this is the index that stops a future agent re-arguing a settled call.
BODY: entries verbatim, newest first, each `## v1.X.Y — <title>` with a stable anchor.
ONE PERMITTED EDIT TO A VERBATIM BLOCK, and it needs the owner's sign-off since 'verbatim' was decided: a `Status:` line at the top of each entry — `Current` / `Superseded by vX` / `Reversed by vX` / `Disclosed, not fixed`. Without it the archive asserts ~150 contradictory present-tense claims and a reader cannot tell which survived.
SHARDING THRESHOLD: state it now rather than discovering it — past ~300k, split by minor series (`Changelog-Archive-v1.1xx.md`) and keep Indexes A-C in the parent. Do not shard by subject; subjects cut across versions and Index B already serves that axis.

findings.title: What CLAUDE.md must declare it is NOT — and the one-sentence test that puts the boundary somewhere
findings.detail:
§0 carries an explicit negative charter, because a document that cannot say what it is not for absorbs everything, and this one demonstrably did (87% of it by mass). Declare: NOT a changelog — no 'v1.X.Y did Y'. NOT a post-mortem archive — no measurement tables, no mutation kill tables, no gate snapshots (`GATES AT vX`), no byte deltas, no test counts. NOT the API reference for `neural/src/app.src.jsx` (13,066 lines — the code is, and its comments are good). NOT a test report. NOT a design journal. NOT a duplicate of docs/Architecture.md or docs/Content.md.
THE TEST, one sentence, printed in §0 and in §9: *'If a reader could break something by not knowing it, and it will still be true after the next ten commits, it is inline; if it explains WHY the current state is what it is, it is archive.'*
FIVE MECHANICAL RULES so the test is checkable without judgement: (1) any sentence whose subject is a version number is archive; (2) any measured number describing a PAST RUN (test counts, byte deltas, 'x of N runs', 'p ≈ 0.55') is archive; (3) an owner quote is archive UNLESS the quote IS the rule, in which case keep the clause and drop the framing; (4) a mutation table is archive; the sentence 'this is gated by <spec>' is inline; (5) a trap is inline only if it names the trigger token a reader would grep for — a trap you cannot address is a story.
WHERE THE BOUNDARY GOES, concretely: the cut is BELOW the rule and ABOVE its evidence. 'A fixed overlay with controls must be in attachInput's early-return list; otherwise pointer capture retargets pointerup and the control is dead to the mouse' is inline. 'Measured: elementFromPoint returned <div data-land-foot>, 120s of Playwright retries, fifth instance' is archive.

findings.title: Move to archive: gate snapshots — point-in-time by definition, and already contradicted
findings.detail: `GATES AT v1.126.0` (L1241) and `GATES AT v1.127.0` (L1738) plus the gate paragraphs inside `WHAT IT COST` blocks record 'Core suite 384 passed / 387 passed / 398 passed', `test:units 75/75`, `e2e:gen 88 passed / 13 failed`, `triple_replay` digests, ordinal counts and per-gate OK lines. These are ~4,000 chars of assertions that were true for one commit each, and they already disagree with one another three versions apart. They belong in their entries in the archive, verbatim, where the version number that makes them meaningful is attached. What replaces them inline is one sentence in §8: 'the suite is expected green; the current known-red baseline lives in `e2e/gen/ledger.json`, and any red not listed there is yours.'

findings.title: Move to archive: byte-delta and cost accounting — ~6,000 chars that a ratchet file already owns
findings.detail: Every recent block closes with 'Bundle +1,041 raw / +383 gzip', 'browser-measured bytes-to-first-hand 380,343 → 380,403', 'neural eager 302,482 / 330,000', 'headroom 4,597 B'. There are at least eight such blocks (L1051, L1093, L1234, L1453, L1741, plus the v1.123/124 cost paragraphs). They are provenance for a decision, and the LIVE numbers live where they are enforced: `tests/artifacts/budget_site.json`, `budget_neural.json` and the two gates that read them. Inline, keep one rule: 'byte ceilings live in tests/artifacts/budget_*.json; raising one requires `--update` in its own justified commit; a green payload gate can be structurally blind, so never read it as evidence about a change it does not exercise.' That is ~300 chars replacing ~6,000.

findings.title: Move to archive: mutation-test kill tables — keep the practice, drop the ledgers
findings.detail: 'mutant' appears 38 times, mostly as tables ('Five mutants, five kills', 'six mutants, four kills — and the two that did not kill are the finding', the 11-row v1.126.0 table, the 7-row v1.127.0 table). As a record of rigour they are valuable and they are exactly what an archive is for. Inline, two sentences survive because they change future behaviour: 'a claim is not gated until a mutant that breaks it turns a named spec red' and 'a mutant that does NOT kill is a finding — record which assertion is therefore not covered, in the spec's own header, so nobody later mistakes it for coverage.' The two non-kills in `dual-pair.spec.ts` are already written into that spec's header, which is the correct home and proves the pattern.

findings.title: Move to archive: owner quotes as provenance — keep the clause where the quote IS the rule
findings.detail: 'Owner' appears 44 times and 'owner:' 17. Most are framing ('Owner: "i clicked the play from this roll in one of my last rolls sidebar and it didnt open the MC..."') and belong to the entry that explains the fix — that is Index C's material and it is why the archive must exist. A minority ARE the rule and cannot be paraphrased without losing force: 'there is never 0% to white. It's always 0% to blue'; 'do not silently reinstate Edge'; 'never the word lambda on this surface'; 'let's not assume yet that the opponent is the same level as we are'. Keep those as quoted clauses inside the relevant inline rule, dropping the surrounding incident. Rough saving: ~12,000 chars of quoted incident narration, at the cost of ~800 chars of retained clauses.

findings.title: Move to archive: measurement tables that restate a single rule at length
findings.detail: The largest single category by volume. Examples: the 272-role-hand walks with their full statistics; the λ∈{1,2,4} reach table; the three opponent models A/D/E with means; the resolve-kernel before/after TV table; the 'what the over-inclusion is made of' percentage split; the 908-prefix clip-error census; the corpus counts (1467 nodes, 1326 cards, 2662 technique members, 136/272/297/1034). Each exists to establish ONE rule that compresses to a line — 'the dial re-orders 29 hands and changes the dealt set in none'; 'the opponent mirror is what makes λ mean anything'; 'a miss must draw INSIDE its branch'. Send the tables to the archive with their entries and keep the rule. Caveat worth stating in §9: a handful of these numbers are load-bearing CONSTANTS rather than evidence (`NG_EDGE_LAM = 2`, `NG_EDGE_SAT = 15`, `NG_DECISION_KNEE = 10`, `NG_PREFETCH_CAP = 10`, `BELT_SCORE` thresholds, `REST_GLOW`, `ARRIVE_BLOOM`, `NG_LABEL_LEFT_MIN = 50`). Those go to docs/Neural.md beside the behaviour they parameterise — not to the archive, and not inline.

findings.title: Stale, verify first: the 'known 13 red' e2e:gen baseline is drifting and is in the wrong artifact
findings.detail: CLAUDE.md names 13 specs as the permanent `e2e:gen` red baseline (L~1745ff) and then, at v1.129.0, records that the count moved to 14 with `mid-timeout-question-costs-no-odds` newly red and four specs asserting a retired `auto_pick` mechanic. The repo now holds 98 gen spec files and a 179-key ledger, so '88 passed / 13 failed' cannot be reconciled from the file. A per-spec red baseline is state, it changes on most waves, and CLAUDE.md is the worst possible place for state. RECOMMENDATION: the baseline lives in `e2e/gen/ledger.json` (which already has per-test rows) or a small `e2e/gen/known-red.json` that `check_gen_specs.sh` reads and enforces; CLAUDE.md keeps one sentence pointing at it. VERIFY BEFORE MOVING: run `npm run e2e:gen` once to get the true current list — do not transcribe either the 13 or the 14 from the prose.
findings.evidence: ls e2e/gen/*.spec.ts → 98; e2e/gen/ledger.json → 179 keys; CLAUDE.md asserts 88+13=101

findings.title: Stale, verify first: the npm table documents 31 of 58 scripts and mis-states the regenerate chain
findings.detail: `package.json` defines 58 scripts; the CLAUDE.md table has 33 content rows, some of which are not npm scripts. Undocumented and non-trivial: `dev:neural`, `dev:neural:app` (the fast bundle refresh that is the fix for the 240s-timeout trap), `regenerate:neural`, `validate:headers`, `validate:curriculum`, `validate:mc`, `validate:forward`, `build:forward`, `audit:from-position`, `fix:from-position`, `migrate:ruleset`, `regenerate:explorer`, `regenerate:redirects`, `regenerate:headers`, `regenerate:llms`, `clips:report`, `regenerate:json:fast`, `e2e:headed`, `serve`. The documented `regenerate` chain omits `migrate:ruleset`, which the real script runs between `explode` and `validate:graph`. Also undocumented: `playwright.coldstart.config.ts` and `playwright.catalog.config.ts` exist with no entry, and `e2e/gallery/` is unmentioned. REBUILD THE TABLE FROM `package.json`, one line per script, and push every multi-paragraph explanation into the script's own docstring — `scripts/check_affiliate_surface.py`'s 35-line header proves the repo already writes them well, and a docstring cannot drift from its script.
findings.evidence: 58 keys in package.json scripts vs 33 documented rows; package.json:37 includes migrate:ruleset, CLAUDE.md's chain does not

findings.title: Stale, verify first: retired prototype machinery still reads as live in seven places
findings.detail: `?dual=iso` appears 7 times and `e2e/prototype` 4 times; `e2e/prototype/` no longer exists on disk and v1.126.0 retired the flag values and their payloads. The v1.114.3 and v1.114.4 blocks are still headed '(v1.114.3, `?dual` prototype)' and describe behaviour reached via a URL that is now accepted-and-ignored, while the behaviour itself SHIPPED as default in v1.125.0. findings.title: Stale, verify first: docs/Architecture.md points INTO CLAUDE.md for content that is about to move
findings.detail: The pointer graph currently runs the wrong way — the always-loaded file is the deep one and the on-demand doc defers to it. `docs/Architecture.md:79` says 'See CLAUDE.md → "Graph Topology — canonical model & invariants" for the full edge/direction/sink contract' and `:87` says 'Details and measurements: CLAUDE.md → "THE PAIR IS THE DEFAULT, AND IT IS DERIVED AT INGEST"'. `docs/DualPairMigration.md:23,32,34` carry three more. After the split, :79's target survives (the invariants stay inline) but :87 and the three DualPair references point at text that will be in the archive. FIX IN THE SAME COMMIT AS THE SPLIT: re-point them at `docs/Changelog-Archive.md#v1-125-0` / `docs/Neural.md`, and invert the general rule — CLAUDE.md points OUT, docs point at each other, nothing points INTO CLAUDE.md except the machine-parsed disclosure marker. A dangling doc pointer is worse than no pointer because it costs a read to discover.
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'CLAUDE.md' docs/ → Architecture.md:79,87; DualPairMigration.md:23,32,34

findings.title: docs/ boundary map — and two live docs that no index references
findings.detail: BOUNDARIES, one sentence each, to be printed in CLAUDE.md §0 as the doc map. `docs/Architecture.md` (36k, touched 2026-08-21): owns the pipeline and the data model IN DEPTH — JSON shapes, file organisation, Quartz config, layout zones, delivery tables. CLAUDE.md keeps only the invariants a reader can violate. OVERLAP TO RESOLVE: 'Position/Transition Playing-As Model', 'Graph Rules' and 'Neural Data Delivery (v1.80.4)' are duplicated near-verbatim in both — delete the CLAUDE.md copies, keep Architecture's. `docs/Content.md` (16k, touched 2026-07-15): owns content standards in full; CLAUDE.md §7 keeps a 10-line quick ref plus the pinned disclosure block. FLAG: five weeks stale while `migrate:ruleset` and the clips pipeline landed — verify before relying on it. `docs/SEO.md` (7k): clean boundary; absorb CLAUDE.md §8's PostHog dashboard table. `docs/Synonyms.md` (9k, touched 2026-05-28) is ORPHANED — referenced by no index, no README, no CLAUDE.md; it is content-authoring policy and should be linked from docs/Content.md and the doc map, or merged into Content.md. `docs/DualPairMigration.md` (20k, touched 2026-08-21) is ORPHANED and is a SUPERSEDED PLAN by its own admission; §§1-8 belong in the archive family, while §§9-10 (the 2.5D paradigm, 'Projection C chosen') are live design canon and should be extracted to docs/Neural.md. Note that CLAUDE.md's own §2 forbids 'Add docs without updating index' — the file violates its own rule twice.
findings.evidence: git log -1 per doc; grep -o 'docs/[A-Za-z]*\.md' over CLAUDE.md and README.md returns only Architecture, Content, SEO

findings.title: MEMORY.md boundary: promote memory-only traps into CLAUDE.md, demote canon restatements out
findings.detail: The memory index holds 36 files and its boundary with CLAUDE.md is currently undefined, which shows in both directions. PROMOTE INTO §6 — traps that live ONLY in memory and are not guaranteed loaded for a fresh agent or a human contributor: `project_build_excludes_neural_bundle.md` ('npm run build does NOT rebuild the neural bundle; a stale served neural.js makes neural journeys silently 240s-timeout and looks like contention'), `project_webgl_nav_stall_e2e.md` (never getContext-probe canvases), `project_edge_delivery_and_deploy_path.md` (CF `_headers` comma-joins duplicates so cache rules must be disjoint; `source/public/functions/` is silently dead), `project_regen_claude_inference.md` (the JSON-in-`result` gotcha), `feedback_dont_rename_nested_submission_to_short_name.md`. PROMOTE INTO §1 — owner PROCESS rules, which are repo law and not session memory: `feedback_test_locally_before_push.md` (gate `git push origin dev` on the owner's go-ahead) and `feedback_end_with_how_to_test.md` (end every delivery with the literal run command and what is blocked on the owner). DEMOTE / LEAVE: memory keeps cross-session working knowledge, owner taste and decision provenance (`project_auth_decision`, `project_open_source_strategy`, `feedback_design_taste_realistic_textures`). RULE TO PRINT IN §9: memory is per-user and may be absent; anything that a contributor could break by not knowing belongs in CLAUDE.md, and memory then points at it rather than restating it.

findings.title: Delete outright: the §1 'read three docs in order' ritual and the subagent-personality table
findings.detail: Two blocks cost tokens on every session and change no behaviour. (a) 'Step 1: Read Documentation (In Order) — 1. CLAUDE.md 2. docs/Architecture.md 3. docs/Content.md 4. docs/SEO.md' instructs a reader to consume 60k of docs before any task; it is never obeyed and cannot be, and it is the wrong shape — replace with the question-keyed routing table from finding 2, which costs about the same and actually resolves. (b) 'Step 3: Deploy Subagents' (895 chars) maps six invented engineering personalities to task types; no workflow, script or gate references it, and the model does not need permission to parallelise. (c) 'Step 2: Ask Critical Questions' (337 chars) is generic advice. Together ~1,500 chars, replaced by ~600 chars of routing table plus the plan-TL;DR rule, which IS load-bearing and stays. This is the only DELETE I would make without archiving, because there is no provenance to preserve — nothing was learned here and nothing was measured.
findings.evidence: grep -rl 'Systematic Migrator\|Ruthless Editor\|Paranoid Tester' across scripts/ .github/ e2e/ → no hits

findings.title: Enforce the budget the way this repo enforces every other one: a byte ratchet plus an append rule
findings.detail: The split will not hold on discipline — the file grew to 337,351 chars one honest post-mortem at a time, and every one of those authors believed their block was the exception. This repo's own answer to exactly this failure mode is a ratchet (`check_payload_budget.py`: shrinking always passes, raising a ceiling needs `--update` in its own justified commit). Mirror it: `scripts/check_claudemd_budget.py` with a 52,000-char ceiling in `tests/artifacts/budget_docs.json`, wired into `ci-validate.yml` beside `validate:ordinals`. Two companion rules for §9, which is where the commit protocol lives: (1) shipping a change means APPENDING its narrative to `docs/Changelog-Archive.md` — the version-bump step already exists in the pre-commit checklist, so this rides it; (2) a change may add to §6 only by adding a TRAP (trigger token + rule + symptom), never a story, and if §6 is at budget the author must merge two instances into a class before adding — which is the compression that should have been happening all along. Set the ceiling at 52,000 not 50,000: a ratchet with zero headroom fails on the first legitimate trap and gets disabled.
findings.evidence: scripts/check_payload_budget.py + tests/artifacts/budget_site.json establish the pattern; CLAUDE.md was edited on 5 of the last 5 commits

findings.title: votes-refresh.yml does NOT run the `regenerate:graph` umbrella — the v1.104.6 fix was reverted in v1.106.8
findings.detail: CLAUDE.md's CI block asserts: "`votes-refresh.yml` committed a `graph.json` with the strength pass skipped ... It ran bare `regenerate_graph.py`; it now runs the `npm run regenerate:graph` umbrella (graph-base → layout → ordinals → strength). CI must never run a subset of the chain a human runs." findings.title: RELOCATION #1 (highest leverage): the 13-red e2e:gen baseline has no machine home — ledger.json has 179 entries, all status 'accepted'
findings.detail: CLAUDE.md confesses the defect itself: 'Four versions of gates blocks have said "the same 13 names" without ever writing them down, which makes the phrase uncheckable.' Measured: e2e/gen/ledger.json contains 179 entries and the ONLY status value present is 'accepted' — no known-red concept exists. Durable home: add "status": "known-red" plus a reason to those 13 rows, and make scripts/check_gen_specs.sh assert SET EQUALITY between the observed red set and the ledger's known-red set. That converts a four-times-repeated unverifiable English sentence into a gate that fails in both directions (a new red, or a fixed one left stale), deletes ~1,400 chars of prose, and gives v1.129.0's '13 -> 14, and the +1 is honest' a machine-checked place to live.

contexteng.headline: The lessons this file exists to preserve are already written — better and at the point of use — in 1,097,752 chars of code comments, spec headers and script docstrings that the build strips to zero bytes, so ~87% of CLAUDE.md is an always-paid second copy of a free corpus; the genuinely orphaned lesson is the 13-red e2e:gen baseline, which CLAUDE.md admits is 'uncheckable' and which ledger.json (179 entries, every one status 'accepted') has no field to hold.

findings.title: app.src.jsx already carries half the narrative — 315,521 chars of comments, 52% token overlap
findings.detail: The biggest duplication axis is not inside CLAUDE.md at all. `neural/src/app.src.jsx` is 13,066 lines of which 4,107 are comment lines = 315,521 chars, almost exactly the size of CLAUDE.md's version narrative (293,624). I extracted every distinctive token from L295-3044 (identifiers >=6 chars in backticks, plus measured numbers >=4 digits) and grepped the comment corpus: 473 of 913 (52%) are already there — 286/511 identifiers, 48/168 measured numbers. Spot-checked side by side, the duplication is near-verbatim: the `_deriveDualPairs` header comment (app.src.jsx:734-760) restates CLAUDE.md L928-1000 including `2,471,947 raw / 199,358 gzip`, `546,746 / 90,492`, `0 of 1467 collide`, `1466 of 1467 resolve`, `rSite = sqrt(deg_a+deg_b-2)`, `1467/1467 sites recover`, `272 hands`, `1326 dealt options`. The `cardOrder` retirement comment (app.src.jsx:11433-11455) restates CLAUDE.md L2370-2400 including the literal array `[-6,-20,+6,+8,-2,+14,+17,+19]` and `211 of 270`, `16 of 270`, `223 re-ordered`. Even the owner quotes are duplicated — 149 'owner' mentions in the comments. SINGLE HOME: the code comment, for anything that names a function, a constant or a measurement of that function's behaviour. CLAUDE.md should keep only the rule a reader needs BEFORE they open the file.

findings.title: `n.y` where the renderer draws at `LY(n)` — one trap, stated four times across four versions
findings.detail: This is the single most repeated engineering lesson in the dual-pair material and it is genuinely a trap worth keeping. It appears at L1020-1025 (v1.125.0, headed 'for the third time', naming v1.114.3's hover and tap and v1.114.4's rollFromPosition), L1438 (v1.129.0, the `this._LY = LY` pattern), L1700-1710 (v1.127.0, twice inside the mutant table), and L1828-1841 plus L1865-1887 (v1.114.3/v1.114.4, the original statement). Four statements, four sets of supporting numbers, one rule: 'any code that converts a node to a screen position must go through `_LY`/`pairMid`; both are identities on an unpaired node.' KEEP that one sentence plus the identity clause inline as a trap. Everything else — the 644->0 pixel mutant, the 11.900 world-unit swing, the ~37px lift arithmetic — is evidence that belongs in the archive and in dual-pair.spec.ts.

findings.title: EDGE material is 60,066 chars and re-argues the same four points across five versions
findings.detail: v1.104.3+v1.118.0 L1892-2152 = 26,344; the model block L2153-2278 = 10,221; v1.121.0 L2279-2412 = 11,221; v1.124.0 L2413-2532 = 12,280. Total 60,066 (17.8% of the file). Four facts are restated version after version: (a) '`movePotential` survives only as the ESCAPE tray's corner value, because an escape's options are POSITIONS which the EDGE table cannot value' — L994, L1906, L2082, L2375, L2379, five times; (b) 'THE ORDER IS FROZEN AT DEAL TIME' — L1959 and L2473, twice, with L2477 cross-referencing; (c) 'in 98 of 272 hands the best-EDGE card is not the best-odds card' — twice verbatim (it is one of only 68 repeated 8-word shingles in the whole narrative); (d) EDGE's own definition, 'how much better or worse this move is than the ORDINARY choice from where you are standing', stated twice verbatim at L1908ish and L2155ish. SINGLE HOME: one EDGE canon block with the formula, the three-marks/two-channels rule, the frozen-order rule and the escape-tray exception.

findings.title: 'replay-digest is unchanged and that is NOT the evidence' — one methodological rule, said four times
findings.detail: L1727 (v1.127.0, 'MUST NOT MOVE HERE'), L2322 (v1.121.0, 'DID NOT MOVE, AND THAT WAS EXPECTED TO BE THE OTHER WAY ROUND'), L2402 (v1.122.0, 'is UNCHANGED and that is not the evidence'), L2478 (v1.124.0, verbatim the same sentence with a different digest). Plus supporting mentions at L1214, L1241, L1739, L2016. The rule underneath is one sentence and it is a real trap: 'a green replay-digest is only evidence about a change the scripted roll can structurally reach; if the spec rigs past your code path, the digest proves nothing.' The same rule is re-derived in fresh prose each time, with fresh supporting measurements, so the copies are individually well-written and only collectively wasteful. It also means the copies have NOT yet drifted much inside CLAUDE.md (the drift is all cross-file, with README, Architecture.md and MEMORY.md) — the risk is ahead of the file, not behind it. findings.title: HARD ESTIMATE: ~228,000 of 337,351 chars (68%) is pure restatement
findings.detail: Partition, non-overlapping. Cross-check against the 50,000 target: what remains is ~35,000-45,000 chars of durable trap (I counted 77 rule-shaped bold spans containing never/must/cannot/only, and roughly 120 distinct rules in total, at 250-400 chars each once stripped to rule-plus-why-plus-one-number) plus ~15,000-20,000 chars of trimmed head and tail after deferring to docs/ — 50,000 to 65,000, landing on the target. The ~65,000-char remainder is unique history with no duplicate anywhere, and that is the material the verbatim archive exists for.
findings.evidence: Section char counts by awk; token overlap 473/913 against 315,521 chars of app.src.jsx comments; 97,908 chars of spec headers; nine gate-snapshot ranges = 6,573; deleted inventory 7,821 less 1,939 survivors; 77 rule-shaped bold spans matching never/must/cannot/only.

dry.headline: The dominant duplication is not inside CLAUDE.md but between CLAUDE.md and the code: app.src.jsx carries 315,521 chars of comments holding 52% of the narrative's distinctive facts (473 of 913 tokens) — including the owner quotes and the exact measurements — with e2e spec headers a third copy at 97,908 chars, so the version narratives are largely a prose mirror of comments that sit beside the code they describe.

findings.title: The single most consequential rule has no code home: generated .md files carry no banner
findings.detail: CLAUDE.md L63 forbids editing generated `.md` in `content/`. This is the rule whose violation silently destroys work — and it is the ONE major rule with zero reinforcement in the repo. `head -6 'content/Transitions/100% Sweep.md'` shows frontmatter beginning `title: "100% Sweep | BJJ Technique | BJJ Graph"` and nothing else. No DO-NOT-EDIT comment, no generator stamp. An agent opening any of ~1,500 generated files sees an ordinary markdown file. Edit it, run `npm run regenerate`, work is gone with no error. Contrast every other trap in this document, which is duplicated at its point of use. KEEP INLINE, at the top, in the shortest possible form, and state the correct target: `content/*.json` for data, `templates/` for structure.
findings.evidence: grep of generated .md frontmatter shows only `title:`; no generator banner anywhere in content/*.md

findings.title: MISSING: `npm run build` does not rebuild the neural bundle — the top time-waster, absent from CLAUDE.md
findings.detail: `grep -n 'dev:neural\|regenerate:neural' CLAUDE.md` returns NOTHING. The `build` script is quartz build + redirects + headers + llms + build:forward + build:share-shell + validate:payload — no `neural/build/build.mjs`. So after editing app.src.jsx, `npm run build && npm test` grades the PREVIOUSLY built `neural.js`, and neural journeys time out at 240s looking exactly like flake or contention. The three commands that fix it (`dev:neural`, `dev:neural:app`, `regenerate:neural`) are the ONLY package.json scripts touching the app, and all three are absent from CLAUDE.md's §5 command table. The deploy workflows know (deploy.yaml:84 runs `npm run regenerate:neural` under the comment 'deploy does NOT run root npm run build') but that is the converse case. This fact currently lives only in the user's private MEMORY.md, which a fresh clone or another engineer does not have.
findings.evidence: package.json `build` chain has no neural step; deploy.yaml:84 + deploy-dev.yaml:77 run regenerate:neural explicitly; CLAUDE.md grep for dev:neural = 0 hits

findings.title: The 13 known-red `e2e:gen` specs exist ONLY in CLAUDE.md, and the ledger actively contradicts them
findings.detail: CLAUDE.md L1739-1752 names the 13 permanently-failing gen specs. `e2e/gen/ledger.json` holds 179 test entries and every single one has `"status": "accepted"` — Counter({'accepted': 179}). `grep -rln 'known-13|known red|expected failures'` outside CLAUDE.md hits only playwright.quarantine.config.ts (a different mechanism). So there is no machine-readable baseline. Delete this list and the next agent running `npm run e2e:gen` sees 13 failures and either rewrites specs that correctly assert retired behaviour (e.g. `auto_pick`, retired v1.129.0) or blames their own change. Two of the 13 burn 4.0m each on timeout, so the run also looks broken. This is the clearest Category-1 keep in the whole file — and the honest fix is to move the list into the ledger as a status value, at which point it can leave CLAUDE.md.
findings.evidence: python3 Counter over e2e/gen/ledger.json tests[] → {'accepted': 179}; grep for the 13 names outside CLAUDE.md hits only ledger.json (marked accepted)

findings.title: MISSING: `neural/src/*` is gitignored with an allow-list — a new build input is silently dropped from CI
findings.detail: .gitignore:87-94 is `neural/src/*` followed by `!*.src.js`, `!*.src.jsx`, `!*.css`, `!xdc-template.html`, `!helmet.html`, `!props.json`, `!technique-content.js`. Add `neural/src/foo.js` and it is invisible to git; CI checks out without it; `node neural/build/build.mjs` either throws or ships a bundle missing the feature — green locally, broken in production. The .gitignore's own comment says exactly this, but nobody reads .gitignore before creating a source file. Proof it bites: `neural/src/support.js` (1,658 lines) is untracked and ignored right now. CLAUDE.md spends 87% of itself on this directory and never mentions the rule. One line: any new neural/src build input must carry the `.src.` infix or be `.css`; verify with `git check-ignore -v`.
findings.evidence: git check-ignore: neural/src/support.js tracked=NO ignored=YES; .gitignore:87-94 allow-list

findings.title: MISLEADING: the Position and Transition JSON schema examples are wrong in both key name and value shape
findings.detail: CLAUDE.md L189-210 shows `{"name": "Armbar from Mount", "attempt_probability": 25}` and rules 'attempt_probability values MUST sum to 100% per role'. Real (content/Positions/Mount.json): `{"transition": "Mount to Armbar", "attempt_probability": {"gi": 6, "nogi": 7}}` — the key is `transition`, not `name`, and the value is a per-ruleset map. L242-265 shows `"probability": 55` and `"success_rate"` scalar; real (content/Transitions/100% Sweep.json): `"probability": {"gi": 50, "nogi": 50}` and `"success_rate": {"gi": 50, "nogi": 50}`. The document contradicts ITSELF — its own Q3-occurrence entry in §5 correctly describes `{gi,nogi}` maps summing to 100 per frame. An agent authoring or repairing content from §4 writes files that fail validation, and worse may write scalars a downstream reader mis-parses. These two blocks are the most-copied part of the file; fix them before anything else.
findings.evidence: content/Positions/Mount.json top.transitions[0] = {transition, attempt_probability:{gi:6,nogi:7}}; content/Transitions/100% Sweep.json outcomes[].probability = {gi,nogi}

findings.title: MISLEADING: "Attacker/Defender sections are generated by templates, not stored in the source JSON" — they ARE in the JSON
findings.detail: Asserted twice (L240 and L264). content/Transitions/100% Sweep.json has top-level `attacker` and `defender` objects carrying overview, key_principles, setup_requirements, execution_steps, common_counters, common_errors, training_progressions, flashcards, safety_considerations, clips (and recognition_cues / defensive_options / favorable_outcomes on defender). The templates RENDER those fields; they do not author them. Combined with the (correct) rule 'never edit generated .md', an agent asked to add a defender's recognition cue has been told the content is not in the JSON and the .md is off-limits — leaving `templates/Transitions/TEMPLATE-DEFENDER.md.jinja2` as the only apparent target, which would change all 1,034 transitions. Reword to: the .md SECTIONS are template-rendered from the `attacker`/`defender` blocks in the source JSON.
findings.evidence: json keys of content/Transitions/100% Sweep.json include 'attacker','defender' with 12 and 11 authored subkeys respectively

findings.title: MISLEADING: §7's tri-level success-rate format has ZERO instances in a 1,500-file corpus
findings.detail: §7 (L3211-3220) gives 'Format: (Success Rate: Beginner X%, Intermediate Y%, Advanced Z%)' with 'Rules: Beginner <= Intermediate <= Advanced (strictly enforced)'. `grep -rl 'Success Rate: Beginner' content/` returns 0 files. The real rendered format is `**Success Rate**: 27%` (templates/Transitions.md.jinja2:105, `{{success_rate}}%`) — a single folded no-gi value — and the source is a `{gi,nogi}` map. No validator enforces the ordering (no 'Beginner' in validate_json.py or validate_graph_integrity.py). Worse, docs/Content.md L15-34 says the same thing, so the two authoritative documents corroborate each other and both disagree with the corpus. This is the most dangerous class of stale: mutually confirming and wrong. Verify then rewrite in BOTH files or delete from both.
findings.evidence: grep -rl 'Success Rate: Beginner' content/ → 0; templates/Transitions.md.jinja2:105 `**Success Rate**: {{success_rate}}%`; docs/Content.md:20 repeats the dead format

findings.title: MISLEADING: the mandatory Pre-Commit Checklist would fire a Claude-API content rewrite for a one-line app fix
findings.detail: L3167-3175 mandates `npm run regenerate:build` before every commit, and the FORBIDDEN table (L64) repeats it as the remedy for 'skip validation before commits'. That expands to `regenerate` = issues → `regenerate:json --interval 600` (the Claude API pass, 600s between calls) → explode → migrate:ruleset → validate:graph → md → hubs → votes → graph → explorer, THEN an ~11-minute build. Nobody does this: the last 40 commits are neural-app changes. And it omits the one step that actually matters for those commits (`dev:neural:app`). A rule this expensive is ignored, and an ignored rule trains agents to ignore the section it lives in. Split it: content commits get the regenerate path; app commits get `dev:neural:app` + `npm run test:curated` + `check_no_raw_random.sh`. Note also the documented pipeline order omits `migrate:ruleset`, which package.json runs between explode and validate:graph.
findings.evidence: package.json regenerate chain includes regenerate:json --interval 600 and migrate:ruleset; last 40 commits are all v1.1xx app work

findings.title: MISLEADING: FORBIDDEN says "files >1000 lines" is never allowed; 11 tracked files break it, led by the app at 13,066
findings.detail: L69 forbids creating files >1000 lines ('Unmaintainable → Split into focused modules') and L74 sets 'Code files: <500 preferred, <1000 max'. Measured on tracked source: app.src.jsx 13,066 · sequence-registry.js 3,283 · regenerate_content_json.py 2,256 · validate_graph_integrity.py 1,516 · regenerate_graph.py 1,441 · calibrate_probabilities.py 1,433 · validate_json.py 1,422 · screen-registry.js 1,152 · regenerate_neural_data.py 1,148 · share-lists.spec.ts 1,048 · challenge-ui.src.js 1,041. CLAUDE.md itself states elsewhere (L808) that 'the runtime remains ONE imperative component in neural/src/app.src.jsx' — a deliberate design choice. So the document simultaneously forbids and mandates the same structure, and an agent following the rule could reasonably start splitting the app. Also self-violating: 'Documentation: <300 lines preferred' against its own 3,338. Either restate as a default-with-named-exceptions or drop it.
findings.evidence: git ls-files | wc -l on source extensions: 11 files >1000 lines; CLAUDE.md L808 declares the monolith deliberate

findings.title: MISLEADING: PROJECT STRUCTURE omits the directory the rest of the document is about
findings.detail: The tree (L80-134) lists content/, templates/, docs/, scripts/ (10 of 90 files), branding/, source/, tests/artifacts/, and one workflow. It does NOT list `neural/` — where the app lives — nor `e2e/`, `functions/`, `forward/`, `workers/`, `supabase/`, or `node_ordinals.json`. An agent asked 'where is the front-end?' reads a tree whose only code directory is `source/quartz/`, which CLAUDE.md elsewhere says is just the SSG shell. Counts are also stale: '85+ positions' (real 136), '150+ submissions' (real 360, a 2.4x understatement), '1000+ transitions' (real 1,034, fine). And `tests/` shows only `artifacts/`, hiding the five `*.test.mjs` files that `npm run test:units` runs. Replace the partial file listing with a 12-line directory-purpose map that includes neural/ and e2e/.
findings.evidence: find counts: Positions 136, Transitions 1034, Submissions 360, Systems 47; ls shows neural/ e2e/ functions/ forward/ workers/ supabase/ all absent from the tree

findings.title: The version narratives are a second copy of comments that already live at their point of use — archive is safe
findings.detail: This is the load-bearing test's actual answer, and it is measurable. app.src.jsx carries 3,323 comment lines, 558 of them substantive prose blocks. Spot-checked, the CLAUDE.md narrative and the code comment are near-verbatim twins: `_deriveDualPairs` (app.src.jsx:733-760) reproduces the entire v1.125.0 section including 'THE HUB KEEPS ITS ID' and 'ONE FOR ONE is not tidiness: rSite recovers sqrt(deg_a+deg_b-2)'; NG_EDGE_LAM / NG_LOSS_PRESETS / NG_EDGE_SAT / NG_DECISION_KNEE / NG_PREFETCH_CAP / NG_LAND_WARM_CEILING_MS / NG_SRS_IVLS / NG_LAND_MORE_COL each carry their own measured rationale at the definition; every playwright.*.config.ts header explains its own port and the cross-worktree hazard; e2e/dsl.ts explains late payloads; share-camera.spec.ts's header IS the camera-ownership block; scripts/regenerate_node_ordinals.py's docstring IS the ordinal section; tests/artifacts/graph_validation_baseline.json's `note` field IS the ratchet paragraph. The point-of-use copy is strictly better — adjacent, unmissable when editing, and harder to drift. Moving the narratives out costs almost nothing.
findings.evidence: 3,323 comment lines in app.src.jsx; verbatim twins confirmed for _deriveDualPairs, 8 NG_* constants, 9 playwright configs, dsl.ts, share-camera.spec.ts, regenerate_node_ordinals.py, graph_validation_baseline.json

findings.title: No standing rule = the file is back to 337k within two weeks; the trim must ship with the rule
findings.detail: Measured growth: 284,708 chars at aea25bfa1 (v1.126.0, 2026-08-21) → 337,351 at c897d19de (v1.129.6, 2026-08-22). That is +52,643 chars across 12 commits in 2 days — one whole target-sized CLAUDE.md every 48 hours, ~4,400 chars per commit. A one-time cut to 50k without changing the writing habit is undone in under a fortnight, and the next person will conclude the trim 'didn't work'. The rule that follows from finding 11: a shipped change writes its post-mortem AT THE CODE (constant, function, spec header, config header, gitignore, baseline JSON `note`) and gets a CLAUDE.md line only if the fact has NO code home. Add that as a §0 rule with a stated char budget, or nothing else here matters.
findings.evidence: git show <rev>:CLAUDE.md | wc -c across 12 revisions: 284,708 → 337,351 in 2 days

findings.title: KEEP: the two graph representations — role-node data layer vs hub-collapsed visual layer
findings.detail: L166-188 and L276-294. This is the #1 conflation available here and it is genuinely counterintuitive: `graph.json` carries `Mount/Top` and `Mount/Bottom` as the edge-bearing states PLUS a bare edgeless `Mount` hub, while `globalGraphLayout.json` collapses them to one node. A competent engineer reasoning from either artifact alone builds the wrong mental model and then mis-files edges, mis-counts nodes, or 'fixes' the edgeless hub. It is compounded by the derived pair (finding 14) where the rep member IS the hub id. docs/Architecture.md L46-127 covers it too, but this is the fact you must hold BEFORE you open anything, which is the definition of inline. Condense the two sections into ~15 lines; drop the worked file-tree examples.
findings.evidence: docs/Architecture.md:68 'Graph Rules (two representations — don't conflate)' duplicates it; graph.json positions has 409 keys of which 272 are role-states

findings.title: KEEP: `s` is two different pairs — position [top,bottom] vs technique [attacker,defender]
findings.detail: From v1.103.0 (L1902+ and the role-correctness block). `roleIdx()` returns 0/1 from playerRole; `valIdx(node)` picks by PERFORMER for techniques and by side for positions. Indexing a technique's `s` with a top/bottom index is silently wrong, not crashy — it cost a bottom player ALL 297 submissions and 144 of 596 bottom-authored techniques. Both functions exist (app.src.jsx:1388-1395) but the code cannot tell you why two nearly-identical accessors exist; the failure mode is a plausible-looking hand with the wrong cards. Also keep the companion rule: the PERFORMER is read from `fromRole`, never inferred from which side the score favours, and a fallback may relax ORIGIN but never ROLE.
findings.evidence: app.src.jsx:1388 roleIdx(), :1390 valIdx(node) — two accessors, 6 and 5 call sites

findings.title: KEEP: the pair is derived at ingest, the rep IS the hub, and `adj` must NOT be role-split
findings.detail: v1.125.0/v1.126.0, condensed to ~12 lines. Three facts that are wrong under first-principles reasoning: (1) both roles are two orbs on screen but ONE node id — the rep carries the hub id, its ordinal and its URL, so nothing was migrated; (2) the partner mints `<hub>/Bottom` with `o: null`, which is why lists must normalise through `siteIdOf` (see finding 16); (3) site adjacency is deliberately NOT role-split, because `opponentDefend`, `_mcPool` and `_posIdx` walk `adj[currentPos]` with no role filter on purpose — role-splitting it handed the opponent YOUR hand and reddened content-capstone. The 'do not role-split adj' line is the one an optimiser reaches for first. Archive the measurement tables (1467/1467, 272/272, byte deltas) — they are proof, not guidance.
findings.evidence: app.src.jsx:761 _deriveDualPairs with its own 28-line docstring; :1035 comment on the one-way site tie; siteIdOf at :5452 with 9 call sites

findings.title: KEEP: lists store SITES — `siteIdOf` normalisation, because only a hub carries an ordinal
findings.detail: v1.126.0's worst find, and it stays worst: a `+` pressed while standing on the lower orb filed a partner id with `o: null`, so the technique was dropped from the share code with NO error and a one-item list encoded to the empty string. 136 of 272 position landings and 172 of 400 technique seats stand on a partner — i.e. every time the coach is playing bottom. The rule 'normalise in the LIST LAYER, not at the capture button, and normalise the READERS too (activeListHas, nodeInAnyList, listsWith) not just the writer' is the part that is not deducible: normalising only the write makes a captured technique show `+` instead of `✓` on the very orb you captured it from. `siteIdOf` exists in code with a one-line comment; the blast radius does not.
findings.evidence: app.src.jsx:5452 siteIdOf, :5465 activeListHas uses it, :5508 'a list holds SITES'

findings.title: KEEP, and merge four copies into one: `replay-digest` is structurally blind — an unchanged digest is not evidence
findings.detail: CLAUDE.md states this four separate times (v1.121.0, v1.122.0, v1.123.0, v1.124.0), each time discovering it afresh. The general rule is the keeper: the digest rigs one scripted roll, so a change that does not alter THAT roll's beats cannot move it — cardOrder was never set by any digest spec, lossAversion defaults to the tested value, and the outcome-kernel fix could not reach it because the rigged node authors exactly one success cell. `scripts/triple_replay.sh` compares runs to EACH OTHER, so no fixture holds the expected digest at all; the value `0390cc44ee7f40e5` appears nowhere in the repo but CLAUDE.md. Keep one paragraph: what the digest does and does not prove, plus 'if your change should have moved it and did not, that is the finding.' Archive the four per-version instances.
findings.evidence: grep for 0390cc44ee7f40e5 outside CLAUDE.md → 0 hits; triple_replay.sh hashes runs against each other, not a baseline

findings.title: KEEP: the latch audit — a built, correct card can be invisible because one of four holders is stuck
findings.detail: v1.129.5. `_landHidden()` asks `_landPaneHid`, `_traySup`, `_bgDown`, `_detailCtx`; any one stuck leaves a fully populated landing card invisible while everything else behaves. The v1.129.5 bug was `_bgRestore()` having exactly ONE caller (`setPaused(false)`), so a background tap could only be undone by the play button — pre-existing, and it presents as 'nothing happens when I click, but the node lights up'. The diagnostic instruction is the value: when a report says a surface did not appear, read the holders before reading the render path. Two lines. Archive the rest of the section.
findings.evidence: app.src.jsx: _landHidden 2 refs, _suppressLand 13 refs, _bgRestore 4 refs, _standDown 3 refs

findings.title: KEEP: `attachInput`'s setPointerCapture retargets clicks — six instances, and the list is a checklist
findings.detail: The wrap's pointerdown calls `setPointerCapture`, which retargets later pointer events so the browser resolves the click to the down/up common ancestor. Every fixed overlay that owns controls must be in the early-return list or its buttons are dead to the MOUSE while `locator.click()` masks it completely. Six recorded instances (in-node dossier, landing card corner +, .ng-seemore, option sheet, film strip, mobile pane). The code comment at app.src.jsx:12147-12152 explains the mechanism at the site — keep only the OPERATIONAL rule inline: any new fixed overlay with controls goes in that list, and prove reachability with `j.clickByMouse`, never `locator.click()`. Related and equally keep-worthy: `pointer-events:auto` is inherited-and-load-bearing on fixed overlays, and `opacity:0` does not remove a subtree from hit-testing — `visibility:hidden` does.
findings.evidence: app.src.jsx:12146-12152 comment block; e2e/dsl.ts:673 clickByMouse with ancestor-interception failure text at :703-713

findings.title: KEEP: an unrigged `rng()` tag is a lottery ticket that only prints when it loses
findings.detail: v1.127.2, and it generalises past its spec. `graph-naming` left `rng("opp-finish")` live, so the opponent could submit you and end the round before the journey's second landing — measured 6/78 failures un-rigged vs 0/30 rigged, invisible across four consecutive green full suites (P(4 green) ≈ 0.73 at 7.7%). The app has 12 rng tags (start-pos, role, outcome, resolve, max-moves, ai-skill, opp-sub-pick, opp-pick, opp-finish, mc-shuffle, escape, checkpoint-pick) plus surface-scoped variants built dynamically at app.src.jsx:8081-8107. Rule to keep: when a journey's subject is what happens AFTER an exchange, rig every draw that can end the exchange early. Also keep the determinism seam itself — every draw goes through `rng(tag)`, gated by scripts/check_no_raw_random.sh which allows exactly 1 Math.random in app.src.jsx and 0 in sound.src.js.
findings.evidence: 12 static rng tags enumerated; dynamic tPick/tShuf at app.src.jsx:8081-8107; check_no_raw_random.sh enforces the 1/0 counts

findings.title: KEEP as one testing-canon block: measure the rendered result, never re-implement it
findings.detail: The same lesson appears at least six times under different names and collapses to four rules. (1) Never assert camera behaviour by reading `camTarget` — nine writers, and the follow-cam re-aims it every frame; project the node through draw()'s transform into the viewport rect. (2) Never assert a render by re-implementing its filter — the v1.126.0 audit's own probe re-implemented `nodes.filter(n => n.rep && …)` and reported 'identical' about a search path that was doubling every hit. (3) A probe is not a gate — v1.128.1's mobile framing and v1.129.1's kicker both had probes and both survived their mutants until a journey pinned them. (4) When geometry lives in a draw-local closure, read the strings/values the frame PUBLISHED (`_lastPairLabel`, `_lastRichLabel`, `this._LY`) — that is the render's output, not a re-implementation. share-camera.spec.ts's header carries (1) verbatim; the other three have no single home. ~8 lines inline, everything else archived.
findings.evidence: e2e/journeys/share-camera.spec.ts:6-25 header; app.src.jsx publishes _lastPairLabel (4 refs) and _lastRichLabel (2 refs) per frame

findings.title: KEEP: EDGE honesty gap 1 — the shipped opponent is not the opponent the number was computed against
findings.detail: Everything else about EDGE (formula, solver, wire shape, saturation, freeze-at-deal-time) is documented at the constants and in scripts/solve_edge_values.py. This one is not, and it is the fact that decides whether any EDGE number may be quoted to a user: `opponentDefend` iterates undirected hub-collapsed adjacency with NO role filter and NO origin filter and never reads `attemptProbability` — 10,662 candidate cells vs the model's 1,246, so only 11.7% of what the shipped opponent may pick is a move the model's opponent would consider, and 87.6% of the shipped pool is wrong on role, origin or both. Keep 3 lines plus the reproduction command (`tests/artifacts/_opponent_gap_measure.py`). Also keep the meta-lesson attached to it — the retired 9.1/23.2% figure was measuring the wrong set and understated the gap by half, so a canon number nobody can reproduce is worse than no number.
findings.evidence: scripts/solve_edge_values.py exists with solve/verify/mutants modes; the gap measurement script is named in CLAUDE.md and lives in tests/artifacts/

findings.title: KEEP: ordinals are permanent and a node's array index must never reach a URL
findings.detail: L296-330 condensed to ~5 lines. Counterintuitive because the obvious wire encoding (array index) is corrupting for a non-obvious reason: regenerate_graph.py iterates unsorted `rglob('*.json')` and the layout derives its node list from dict insertion order seeded by that, so adding ONE content file renumbers pre-existing entries and an already-posted `/l/<code>` silently opens a DIFFERENT class with no error anywhere. scripts/regenerate_node_ordinals.py's docstring says all of this well, so keep only the operational half inline: ordinals are append-only, never renumbered, never reused, retired-not-deleted; `regenerate:ordinals` runs inside the `regenerate:graph` umbrella after graph-layout; `validate:ordinals` is a hard gate in ci-validate and both deploys. Archive the codec's byte-level format, the URL-length tables and the clip-classifier measurements — lists-codec.src.js and its 19-test suite own those.
findings.evidence: scripts/regenerate_node_ordinals.py:1-35 docstring is a verbatim twin; node_ordinals.json committed; validate:ordinals in ci-validate.yml:77 and both deploy workflows

findings.title: KEEP: pane law and the one-front-end fact; ARCHIVE the UI archaeology attached to them
findings.detail: Two rules survive from the ~35k-char pane/landing/challenges region: (a) the pane is manual-only — open pauses the roll, close resumes it only if the pane is what paused it, latched in applyDeckVisibility via _paneAutoPaused, and nothing in the roll loop may open or close it; (b) the Neural app is the ONE front-end, `?variant=legacy` is accepted-and-ignored, and the deleted modules must not be restored or implied to exist. Both are decisions a first-principles reader would violate (auto-opening the pane on a save nudge is the obvious product instinct; restoring a deleted component from git history is the obvious fix). Everything else in that region — which tab shows which subtitle, where the account chip sits, the .ng-drilltab deletion history, list-row padding at 22px vs 38px — is present-tense UI state that the CSS, the JSX and the specs state more accurately, and it is the single largest archive win in the file.
findings.evidence: L806-927 measures 34,888 chars; pane-law.spec.ts + legacy-gone.spec.ts + docs/Architecture.md:331 all carry the two rules

findings.title: ARCHIVE: the v1.104.6 CI narratives — every fix landed and each carries its own comment
findings.detail: Verified all four: e2e-full.yml:54 is now `tar -czf complete-e2e-site.tgz -C source public`; keepalive.yml:40 uses `git status --porcelain` under a comment explaining why `git diff --quiet` never reported an untracked file; tests/artifacts/graph_validation_baseline.json has `max_errors: 0` with a `note` field reproducing CLAUDE.md's paragraph; node-version is "22" in all four build/test workflows. These are ~4,000 chars of post-mortem for defects that no longer exist in artifacts that now document themselves. The one line worth keeping is forward-looking and currently buried: 'if the e2e-full tarball ever gets too big, use --exclude — a new emitted path must be packaged by default, because an allow-list rots silently.'

findings.title: MISSING: owner workflow constraints live in private MEMORY.md, not in the project file
findings.detail: Three facts govern how work is delivered here and none is in CLAUDE.md: (1) the owner tests locally before dev pushes, so committing locally is fine but `git push origin dev` is gated on their go-ahead (feedback_test_locally_before_push); (2) every delivery ends with the literal run command and what is blocked on the owner (feedback_end_with_how_to_test); (3) `npm run build` does not rebuild the neural bundle (finding 2). All three are in the user's auto-memory, which is user-scoped — a fresh clone, a CI agent, or a second engineer does not have it, and the memory file itself flags #3 as 'looks like contention/regression but isn't'. These belong in CLAUDE.md precisely because they are cheap and their absence produces a confidently wrong action.
