sme.headline: The version narratives are almost entirely a second copy of comments that already sit at their point of use in the code — so archiving them is safe — but the handful of facts with NO code home are the ones nobody has noticed: generated content/*.md carry no do-not-edit banner, `npm run build` never rebuilds the neural bundle, and the 13 known-red e2e:gen specs exist only in CLAUDE.md while the ledger marks all 179 "accepted".

verdicts.title: CLASS 1: Absence produces a plausible answer — a check that never ran reads as a pass
verdicts.reason: Mechanisms verified in code. `scripts/validate_graph_integrity.py` now has `import os` (line 25) but STILL has bare `except Exception:` at lines 646 and 682 inside `check_position_type_vs_score` (defined line 628) — the swallow that produced '0 disagreements' is architecturally intact. `.github/workflows/keepalive.yml:40` now uses `git status --porcelain` (the `git diff --quiet` note at line 35 documents the old bug). `neural/build/build.mjs:100-108` now throws per-rule on a dead fetch rewrite (and the table is down to 2 rules, from 4 — the two dead ones were removed). `scripts/regenerate_neural_data.py:285` and `:575` raise on cal/EDGE join coverage below floor. `e2e/dsl.ts:86` `globToRe` is still a substring match and `app.src.jsx:701` still fetches `flashcards/_index.json`. `npm run validate:affiliate` now exists (package.json).
verdicts.rewrite: **Absence reads as a pass.** A matcher that matches nothing, a join that resolves nothing, a loop with zero iterations and a bare `except Exception: return issues` all produce the same output as a clean run. Every matcher/join/gate/rewrite must emit a POSITIVE coverage count and hard-fail below a floor — `regenerate_neural_data.py:285`/`:575` and `build.mjs:100` are the pattern; `validate_graph_integrity.py:646,682` still is not. 17 recorded instances, incl. `check_position_type_vs_score` ("0 disagreements" = never executed; real figure 95), the harness holding `flashcards.json` (a URL never fetched since v1.80.4 — 15 red journeys), and `keepalive.yml`, which never committed anything because `git diff --quiet` reports no change for an untracked file.

verdicts.title: CLASS 2: A gate cited as evidence that is structurally unable to fail on its subject
verdicts.reason: Verified live. `e2e/journeys/payload-first-hand.spec.ts:61` pins `"start-pos": [0]` — a 7-card hand, under the old cap either way. `e2e/journeys/replay-digest.spec.ts:40` rigs `resolve: [0.01,...]` (success branch) so the outcome-kernel change cannot reach it. `scripts/check_seo_parity.py` carries its own in-file 'Scope note, since two findings have now hidden in it' narrowing extraction to `<article>`, and `CategoryNav.tsx` sits outside it. `e2e/prototype/` no longer exists (13 versions uncollected). `segBtn` (app.src.jsx:3832-3838) sets no `aria-pressed`/`aria-checked`/`role` at all — the a11y gap the loss-aversion spec works around is still real. `graph_validation_baseline.json` max_errors is now 0.
verdicts.rewrite: **A green gate is only evidence about what it can see.** `payload-first-hand` pins `start-pos:[0]` (a 7-card hand) so it reports identical bytes with and without the hand cap; `replay-digest` rigs a success branch on a single-success-cell submission so it cannot see an outcome-kernel change; `check_seo_parity.py` extracts from `<article>` only, so `#sidebar-overlay` (CategoryNav) is UNGUARDED. Cite a gate only for a claim a mutant of that claim makes red — otherwise write its blind spot in the same sentence as the green. 12 recorded instances.

verdicts.title: CLASS 3: Fixed chrome positioned by a constant against a band that is computed
verdicts.reason: All named seams exist and are live: `_dockLandCard` (app.src.jsx:9912), `_dockLandFilm` (:9887), `_dockOptionHint` (:9949, with its own comment 'which is the same lesson `_dockLandCard` learned'), `_bandBot` (4 refs), `rollCamTarget` (11 refs), `NG_LABEL_LEFT_MIN`. The `.ng-seemore` breakpoint at helmet.html:106 is `(max-width:767px),(max-height:500px)` with a comment naming the landscape-phone miss. `tests/artifacts/_cue_collision_probe.mjs` exists — the phone challenge-cue overlap is STILL OPEN (no dock call for the cue).
verdicts.rewrite: **Fixed chrome docks off a MEASURED neighbour, never a CSS constant** — the option tray, the landing card and the film strip all have runtime-variable heights, so any constant tuned at one viewport is wrong at every other. Keep the tightest measurement ever seen (`_bandBot`), and treat a not-yet-laid-out element as SKIP: an undocked element's `rect.top` reads 0 for one frame and will throw the camera. 12 instances (`_dockLandCard`, `_dockLandFilm`, `_dockOptionHint` fixed); STILL OPEN: the phone challenge cue writes across the focus label (6,700 px² — reproduce with `tests/artifacts/_cue_collision_probe.mjs`).

verdicts.title: CLASS 4: The spec re-implements the thing it is supposed to observe
verdicts.reason: The published-draw-state seams all exist: `this._LY = LY` (app.src.jsx:12340), `_lastPairLabel` (4 refs, stamped in `pairGroup` at :12966), `_lastRichLabel` (2 refs). The Explore search rep filter that the re-implemented probe missed is now at `:5279` (`nodes.filter(n => n.rep && ...)`), and `_ambig` (:1181), `buildExplorer` (:5100) and `_posIdx` (:10951) each carry their own `rep` filter — i.e. the private-copy hazard is structural, not historical.
verdicts.rewrite: **Never assert a render by re-implementing it.** A spec-side copy of a filter, of "what the node set is", or of a screen coordinate is written from the same reading of the code under test — usually with the fix already in it — so it agrees by construction and measures nothing. The v1.126.0 audit BUILT to find this class committed it, reporting "identical" about a search path that was doubling every hit. Drive the real entry point (`renderExplorer()`, `optionsFor()`, `draw()`) and assert on what it emitted; when the geometry lives in a draw-local closure (`halfW`, `ox`), read what the frame PUBLISHED — `this._LY`, `_lastPairLabel`, `_lastRichLabel`. 10 instances.

verdicts.title: CLASS 5: Reachable, visible and existing are three different facts; the hit-test is the only oracle
verdicts.reason: `attachInput`'s pointerdown early-return (app.src.jsx:12146-12188) names exactly six surfaces — node card, dossier sheet, then a loop over `[_landEl, _landFilmEl, optDetailRef, optionHintRef]` — with in-code numbering 'Fourth/FIFTH SURFACE/SIXTH SURFACE'. `_suppressLand` (:7381) now sets `visibility:hidden !important` with the v1.100.2 reasoning in situ. `_updateHover` (:12130-12134) hit-tests `ly(n)`. `e2e/dsl.ts:673` `clickByMouse` exists. STILL UNFIXED: four sibling hide-sites write only opacity/pointer-events — :3456 (option sheet hiding the landing card), :3804, :3825, :7353.
verdicts.rewrite: **Existing, visible and reachable are three different facts.** Four independent causes make a correct control unclickable: `setPointerCapture` retargeting (6 instances), inherited `pointer-events` on a fixed overlay, `opacity:0` (hit-testing ignores opacity — only `visibility:hidden` removes a subtree), and a hit-test taken at a stored rather than a drawn coordinate. Prove reachability with `j.clickByMouse` (real pointer at measured coordinates + `elementFromPoint`); `locator.click()` dispatches on the element and proves nothing.

verdicts.title: CLASS 6: A second, stale implementation of a question that already had a seam
verdicts.reason: `techniqueOrigin` (5 refs) and `confirmPlayFrom` (9 refs) are the collapsed seams; `rollCamTarget` (11 refs) is the camera one; `playFrom` is now a wrapper. But the class is live, not historical: `neural/src/xdc-template.html:14,16` still carries a stale duplicate of helmet.html's `.ng-optionrow` style block (`scroll-padding:0 28px`, `scroll-snap-align:center`) that v1.129.3 removed from `helmet.html` — it is inert only because `build.mjs:115` strips the `<helmet>` element. Two names for one cap (`NG_LIST_ITEM_CAP`/`NG_LIST_MAX_ITEMS`) still stand, pinned equal by test.
verdicts.rewrite: **When one question is answered in two places, one of them is already wrong.** Collapse to a named seam BEFORE adding a third caller, and DELETE the copy rather than syncing it — a synced copy rots silently. 9 instances (`playFrom` vs `rollFromPosition`; an `adj[]` walk vs `fromPositionId`, wrong on 907 of 1,331 techniques; a hard-coded `vw` after `rollCamTarget` existed). LIVE TODAY: `xdc-template.html`'s `<helmet>` block is a stale duplicate of `helmet.html` (it still carries the scroll-snap rules deleted in v1.129.3) — it is inert only because `build.mjs` strips it, so never read CSS out of it.

verdicts.title: CLASS 7: A heuristic standing in for a fact the data states outright
verdicts.reason: `valIdx` (6 refs) and `roleIdx` (5 refs) both exist as distinct accessors; `seatRole` (4 refs) exists precisely because the title-derive answers 'top' for all 136 position hubs; `graphName` (app.src.jsx:1456) strips the role via `posFamily` for positions. Measured on the shipped wire: 136 of 136 position hub titles carry a role word, so the title-derive IS a constant.
verdicts.rewrite: **If the data states it, read it.** `fromRole` names the performer; `position_type` names the dominance; `fromPositionId` names the origin. A derivation that returns the SAME answer for the whole corpus is not a derivation, it is a constant with a function around it — the position-title role derive answers "top" for 136 of 136 hubs. 9 instances; the worst (`roleIdx` indexing a technique's `[attacker,defender]` with a top/bottom index) hid ALL 297 submissions from a bottom player.

verdicts.title: CLASS 8: A single-slot resource with many writers and no declared owner
verdicts.reason: The ownership machinery is live: `_evCountdown` stamped at app.src.jsx:11176, released by `setEvent` (:1474) and dropped by `_dropCountdownEvent` (:8632) from `clearOptions` (:8625). `HESITATE_HOLD = 1.1` at :276 with the one-slot rationale in comment. `_trayStop()` (:294) is called by `clearOptions`, `tweenScroll` and each new grab — one rAF owns `scrollLeft`. `holdCamera`/`camHeld` lease and `_bumpStageVer` (6 refs) confirmed.
verdicts.rewrite: **A single-slot resource needs a stamped owner and an explicit lifetime** (hold / lease / latch) — never an assumption that your write is the last one. The announcer has ONE slot (`setEvent`): a share-arrival toast was overwritten within seconds, a countdown line outlived its hand, and "Time's up" is overwritten SYNCHRONOUSLY on the next line and has never reached the screen. Same shape: `camTarget` (the follow-cam rewrites it every frame → `holdCamera()` lease) and `scrollLeft` (`_trayStop()` — one rAF owns it). 9 instances.

verdicts.title: CLASS 9: The measurement is sound and its SUBJECT is wrong — canon numbers that do not reproduce
verdicts.reason: Independently reproduced two of the file's own corrections and found a third error. `source/quartz/static/neural/graph-data.json`: 136 position hubs, 115 strictly opposite-sign — the '115 of 136, not 85' correction is right. But the same walk gives 110 ambiguous main names, not the 89 the file states twice (L528, L3041); app.src.jsx:1800 already says '~110'. `tests/artifacts/_opponent_gap_measure.py` and `_lambda_probe.py` exist as the reproduction recipes the correction promised.
verdicts.rewrite: **A canon figure carries its SET DEFINITION and the exact command that recomputes it, in the same sentence** — a number without a reproduction recipe is a story, and this file has shipped at least four that did not reproduce (the opponent gap understated by half because it measured the wrong set; "85 of 136" was 115 and was never exactly right; "89 ambiguous main names" is 110; "0 disagreements" was a check that never ran). Before quoting a number, run its script. 8 instances.

verdicts.title: CLASS 10: A fallback that substitutes a plausible value and never says it fired
verdicts.reason: Both good patterns exist and are named beats: `mc_pool_cold` (4 refs) and `land_warm_stalled` (1 ref, with `NG_LAND_WARM_CEILING_MS`). `drawOutcome` (5 refs) chooses its whole-table fallback before the draw so the rng call count cannot depend on content. `_evLamIdx` (2 refs) falls back to `NG_EDGE_LAM` rather than guessing. The silent-fallback hazard is still structural: `calSuccess()` returning null still routes to a dominance formula.
verdicts.rewrite: **Every fallback emits a named beat or a counter.** A fallback that produces plausible output is strictly worse than a crash, because it buys months of silence: a missed `cal` key fell through to `0.36 + dom*0.1` and printed a fabricated ~45.6% on ~289 of 1,204 option cards for months, where authored rates span 10-74%. Good patterns to copy: `mc_pool_cold`, `land_warm_stalled`. 8 instances.

verdicts.title: CLASS 11: Reading stored state where the renderer uses derived state
verdicts.reason: The rule and its seams are live — `_LY` published at app.src.jsx:12340, `pairMid` at :7713, hit-test through `ly(n)` at :12130 — but the COUNT is wrong. v1.129.7 (HEAD, commit 465653c77) added `headPos()` at :1333 whose docblock reads 'FIFTH INSTANCE of the `n.y`-where-the-renderer-draws-at-`LY(n)` defect (hover and tap in v1.114.3, `rollFromPosition` in v1.114.4, four specs in v1.125.0)'. CLAUDE.md:1020 still says 'for the THIRD time'. `headPos` also feeds `camFocus` from two callers (:1347, :1370), which the canon never records.
verdicts.rewrite: **Never convert a node to a screen position from its STORED coordinates.** The renderer draws at `LY(n)` / `pairMid(n)`; `n.y` is the pair's shared ground point, ~37-47px away at roll zoom. Any code — app OR spec — that turns a node into a screen point goes through `_LY`/`pairMid`, both identities on an unpaired node, so production geometry is unchanged by construction. FIVE instances as of v1.129.7: hover + tap (v1.114.3), `rollFromPosition` (v1.114.4), four specs (v1.125.0), `headPos` (v1.129.7 — which also fed `camFocus` from two callers, so the camera and the light were wrong together and neither looked broken alone).

verdicts.title: CLASS 13: The harness is not the product — assertions satisfiable by what the harness omits
verdicts.reason: `e2e/journeys/history-replay.spec.ts:293-297` uses `page.emulateMedia({reducedMotion:'reduce'})` with an in-file comment that `test.use({reducedMotion})` leaves `matchMedia` FALSE in this harness. `e2e/dsl.ts:263` routes `**/flashcards/_index.json` and `:86` `globToRe` is a substring match over the request URL. `tests/artifacts/_owner_shoot.mjs` exists as the against-the-real-server counterpart. `_warmMcPool` (7 refs) makes residency a precondition so distractors cannot depend on network timing.
verdicts.rewrite: **Beside every assertion, name what the harness does NOT serve** — if the absence alone would satisfy the assertion, the assertion is about the harness. The DSL serves `{}` for dossier chunks (no film strip, no `More` content for most states); `test.use({reducedMotion})` leaves `matchMedia` FALSE here, so use `page.emulateMedia`; non-localhost requests are aborted (which is why a `.catch` is load-bearing); a screenshot taken under the harness photographs the harness. 7 instances.

verdicts.title: CLASS 14: CI runs a subset of the chain a human runs, or an allow-list that rots silently
verdicts.reason: Four of the five sub-claims verified: `e2e-full.yml:54` is now `tar -czf complete-e2e-site.tgz -C source public`; `keepalive.yml:40` uses `git status --porcelain`; `graph_validation_baseline.json` max_errors is 0; `deploy.yaml:105`/`deploy-dev.yaml:95` both carry the 'deploy does NOT run root npm run build' comment and re-list steps inline. BUT the headline rule is contradicted by its own repair: `votes-refresh.yml:59-60` runs `regenerate:graph-base` + `regenerate:graph-strength`, NOT the umbrella, and its comment says the umbrella 'actually FAILED here every week since it was introduced' because the node2vec/umap stack is not installed. CLAUDE.md L853's 'it now runs the `npm run regenerate:graph` umbrella' is stale.
verdicts.rewrite: **CI must run the same chain a human runs, or say in the workflow WHY it runs a subset and what that subset cannot produce.** `votes-refresh.yml` once ran bare `regenerate_graph.py` and committed a graph.json with `strength` stripped from 4,464 of 4,465 nodes; it now runs `graph-base` + `graph-strength` deliberately (the full umbrella needs an ML stack the job does not install). Companion rules: never allow-list emitted paths (package by default, `--exclude` explicitly — `e2e-full.yml`'s six-path list made the PR gate unpassable for both protected branches), and a `paths:` filter must include the INPUTS its own gates read.

verdicts.title: CLASS 15: A read taken on a frame where the value is not yet real
verdicts.reason: `_bandBot` (4 refs) exists and caches the tightest measurement; `_dockLandFilm` (:9887) is called from a `requestAnimationFrame` inside `_dockLandCard` (:9913) precisely because of the undocked-element frame. `this.now` is the game clock throughout (used by `flare`/`age` reads in `draw()`), so the paused-clock trap is intact. `rollCamTarget`'s cold fallback at :11822 carries the 'no cached answer at this viewport yet' comment.
verdicts.rewrite: **Before reading a measured value, prove the thing measured has laid out and the clock you depend on is running.** An element positioned after insertion reads `rect.top === 0` for one frame ('not yet laid out' is SKIP, never zero); the landing card mounts ~0.6s after the frame that measures its band; a canvas assertion taken while the roll is PAUSED freezes `this.now` and therefore every age-derived value into a false pass; and one `advance()` is not a frame — an intervening `page.evaluate` is what forces layout. 6 instances.

verdicts.title: CLASS 16: A latch with no enumerated lifter
verdicts.reason: `_landHidden()` at app.src.jsx:7373-7379 asks exactly the four holders named plus `_landEl`: `return !this._landEl || !!this._landPaneHid || !!this._traySup || !!this._bgDown || !!this._detailCtx;`. `_bgRestore` (:7331) now has two callers — `setPaused(false)` at :374 and the node tap at :12274 — confirming the v1.129.5 fix. The one-latch-per-pauser pattern is live (`_paneAutoPaused`, `_landAutoPaused`, `_replayAutoPaused`, `_dossierAutoPaused`).
verdicts.rewrite: **Every suppression flag declares its complete set of lifters at the definition.** `_bgRestore()` had exactly ONE caller (`setPaused(false)`) since the background-tap behaviour shipped, so the only way out of a stand-down was the play button — the app did all its work under a suppression nobody lifted. The transferable artefact is `_landHidden()`: FOUR holders (`_landPaneHid`, `_traySup`, `_bgDown`, `_detailCtx`), and any one stuck leaves a built, mounted, correctly populated card invisible while every other surface behaves. When a report says "nothing happens but the node lights up", read the holders before the render path.

verdicts.title: CLASS 18: The name you queried is not the object you meant (selector and scope collisions)
verdicts.reason: `neural/build/build.mjs:76` scans `/^(?:function|const|let|var|class)\s+.../gm` for duplicate top-level names (the widened form), and `:57` strips `export (function|const|let|var|class)`. `_lastPairLabel` is stamped per draw in `pairGroup` (:12966) so the last-group-wins hazard is real. The two-names-one-cap pair (`NG_LIST_ITEM_CAP`/`NG_LIST_MAX_ITEMS`) exists because lists.src.js and lists-codec.src.js share one bundle scope.
verdicts.rewrite: **Scope every selector to a marker you own, and assert it appears exactly once.** Never query by a SHAPE another object can also have: `.on("title")` matched a `<title>` inside an inline SVG (fixed with `title[data-share-title]`); `body[data-share-cue]` collided with the cue button's own attribute so every measurement silently became the whole viewport; a CSS-border triangle computes to `width: 8px`, not 0; and `_lastPairLabel` holds whichever group drew LAST in the frame, so capture it while the hover is live. 6 instances.

verdicts.title: CLASS 21: An index-keyed or positional format fails plausibly and reports nothing
verdicts.reason: `cal.ev` is still `[nodeIdxs, attemptPct, [e0,c1]...]` in the wire (graph-data.json node keys include `cal`), and `_tech_keys` (regenerate_neural_data.py:159) is the three-rung ladder with hard coverage gates at :285 and :575. The `s` two-meanings hazard is live (`valIdx`/`roleIdx` both present). `links` as index pairs never leave the file (the wire's nodes carry permanent `o` ordinals instead — 1467 of 1467 verified).
verdicts.rewrite: **An index or positional join gets a whole-structure DIFFERENTIAL against a known-good graph, plus a non-triviality floor** — never a non-null count, which a wrong-but-complete remap satisfies perfectly. Nothing in these formats is self-describing: a wrong `cal.ev` remap still finds rows and prints an integer on every card, the WRONG technique's integer, with no exception and no blank. Same class: `s` is `[top,bottom]` for a position and `[attacker,defender]` for a technique; a position's `posId` is a LEAF slug where a technique's leaf (`from-mount`) is not. 6 instances.

verdicts.title: CLASS 23: Order decided by an accident of iteration
verdicts.reason: `node_ordinals.json` exists as the committed append-only lockfile with `npm run regenerate:ordinals` / `validate:ordinals` in package.json, and every wire node carries `o` (1467/1467 verified). The `_cmpDealt` strict-total-order and the `Explore` search `.slice(0,120)` cap (app.src.jsx:5279) are both live, the latter now behind the `rep` filter that was missing.
verdicts.rewrite: **Any ordering a user or a URL can see needs a strict total order whose final tiebreak is stable CONTENT** — never array index, dict insertion order or filesystem order. `rglob('*.json')` is unsorted and the layout's node list follows dict insertion order seeded by it, so adding ONE content file renumbers pre-existing entries: an index-encoded share link would silently open a different set of techniques with no error anywhere (hence permanent, append-only ordinals). Corollaries: `Array#sort` is stable, so a comparator that can return 0 hands the decision to the node index; and a cap applied over an unordered list is a random sample. 5 instances.

verdicts.title: CLASS 24: A constant in the code standing in for a value in the data

verdicts.rewrite:
#### T-INPUT-1 — a control inside a fixed overlay is dead to the mouse
**Fires when** you add, move or re-parent a clickable element inside a fixed overlay on the app root (`.ng-landcard`, `.ng-landfilm`, `.ng-seemore`, the option-detail sheet, the node card, any new one) — or you touch `attachInput`.
**Mechanism** `attachInput`'s `pointerdown` calls `setPointerCapture()` on the wrap. That RETARGETS the later `pointerup`, so the browser resolves the click from the down/up common ancestor and the listener inside your overlay never runs. Separately, `pointer-events` is inherited and the overlay root disables it: a control that does not re-enable it INLINE is hit-tested straight through to the canvas.
**Looks like** the element measures correctly, `elementFromPoint` returns it, a real mouse click does nothing. Keyboard paths work — that is what hides it. `locator.click()` passes, because it dispatches on the element.
**Count** 6 surfaces, v1.69.1 (coach Next) through v1.123.0 (`.ng-seemore`, dead to the mouse for its entire existence). A human found every one.
**Do** add the overlay to the early-return list at `app.src.jsx:12146`; set `pointer-events:auto` inline on the control; pin it with `j.clickByMouse(sel)`, never `locator.click()`. **Partially pinned:** `clickByMouse` only fires for overlays somebody wrote a mouse journey for.

verdicts.reason: Verified. `_suppressLand` (app.src.jsx:7381-7395) now sets `visibility:hidden` with the reasoning in situ, and `[data-land-foot]` does re-enable pointer-events inline. The 'still unverified' half is TRUE and the count is FOUR, not three: `:3456` (option sheet hiding `_landEl`), `:3804` and `:3825` (option-detail panel), `:7353` (mobile pane) all write only opacity + pointerEvents. Only `:7403` also writes `visibility`.
verdicts.rewrite:
#### T-INPUT-2 — a hidden overlay that still eats clicks
**Fires when** you hide an overlay by writing `opacity:0` and/or `pointer-events:none`.
**Mechanism** hit-testing ignores opacity, and `pointer-events` is inherited — so any descendant that re-enables it INLINE stays live across its whole box. `[data-land-foot]` does exactly that, deliberately, because it holds `More ▸` and the capture `+`. The overlay is invisible and still on top.
**Looks like** something UNDERNEATH the hidden element is dead to the mouse; `elementFromPoint` at your target returns the thing you thought was gone (measured: `<div data-land-foot="1">` at the centre of a capture button, 120s of Playwright retries).
**Do** also set `visibility:hidden !important` — inherited, unescapable here, and it removes the subtree from hit-testing outright. Assert inertness with `elementFromPoint`, never a visual check.
**UNGUARDED — four sites still write the leaky form**: `app.src.jsx:3456`, `:3804`, `:3825`, `:7353`. Only `_suppressLand` (`:7381`) and `:7403` are fixed.

The published-draw-state seams exist: `this._LY = LY` (:12340), `_lastPairLabel` (stamped in `pairGroup`, :12966), `_lastRichLabel`.
verdicts.rewrite:
#### T-SPEC-1 — never assert a render by re-implementing it
**Fires when** a spec, probe or audit computes the expected answer itself: `nodes.filter(...)`, a private copy of a filter or of "what the node set is", a hand rebuilt from `adj`, a screen coordinate recomputed from `n.x`/`n.y`.
**Mechanism** you write the copy from the same reading of the code you are testing, usually with the fix already in it. The two agree by construction, so the assertion measures nothing.
**Looks like** green — on a build you have already broken. The v1.126.0 audit built to find this class committed it: its probe measured `nodes.filter(n => n.rep && …)` and reported "identical" about Explore's search, which was doubling every hit and halving its own 120-row cap.
**Count** 6 specs held private copies of the node set (v1.125.0), plus 1 in the audit that hunted them (v1.126.0).
**Do** drive the real entry point — `renderExplorer()`, `optionsFor()`, `draw()` — and assert on what it EMITTED (DOM rows, duplicate row text, read-back pixels). When the geometry lives in a draw-local closure (`halfW`, `ox`) you cannot recompute it at all: read what the frame PUBLISHED — `_lastPairLabel`, `_lastRichLabel`, `this._LY`. A second implementation is legitimate ONLY when it also asserts set-equality against the app's own result.

verdicts.title: CLASS 13: The harness is not the product — assertions satisfiable by what the harness omits
verdicts.reason: Verified the mechanism at three points: `test.use({reducedMotion})` vs `page.emulateMedia` (a fixture option that asserts nothing and passes forever is the purest form of this class); the DSL serving `{}` for dossier chunks means film-strip and More-fold assertions measure absent surfaces; `tests/artifacts/_owner_shoot.mjs` exists precisely because a harness screenshot photographs the harness. Distinct from Class 2 (blind gate): there the gate runs against the real product and cannot see the change; here the gate runs against a product that is missing the subject. The remedy differs accordingly.
verdicts.rewrite: **Beside every assertion, name what the harness does NOT serve — if the absence alone satisfies the assertion, the assertion is about the harness.** 7 recorded instances: `test.use({ reducedMotion })` leaves `matchMedia` FALSE in this harness, so a spec relying on the fixture option **asserts nothing and passes forever** (use `page.emulateMedia`); the DSL serves `{}` for dossier chunks, so there is no film strip and most states legitimately have no `More` fold — a journey about either must AUTHOR content; the harness aborts non-localhost requests, which is why the GitHub-stars `.catch` is load-bearing; a screenshot taken under the harness photographs the harness (`tests/artifacts/_owner_shoot.mjs` drives the real dev server for this reason).

verdicts.title: CLASS 14: CI runs a subset of the chain a human runs, or an allow-list that rots silently
verdicts.reason: Verified all four fixes in the workflow files, each carrying its postmortem: `keepalive.yml:35-40` (`git status --porcelain`, with the comment explaining `git diff --quiet` on an untracked file), `votes-refresh.yml:52-60` (the comment 'regenerate_graph.py ALONE emits graph.json WITHOUT the strength pass' + explicit graph-base then graph-strength), `e2e-full.yml:54` (`tar -czf … -C source public`). The standing hazard is real and unfixed: deploy re-lists build steps inline rather than invoking `npm run build`, so any new emitted step is silently absent in production and nothing asserts the two lists are equal.
verdicts.rewrite: **CI must never run a subset of the chain a human runs, and no emitted path may be allow-listed.** `votes-refresh.yml` ran bare `regenerate_graph.py` instead of the `regenerate:graph` umbrella and committed a graph.json with `strength` **stripped from 4,464 of 4,465 nodes**; `e2e-full.yml` tarred six allow-listed paths, so the PR gate for BOTH protected branches could not pass — "an allow-list rots silently and this one predated every spec that broke on it" (package by default, `--exclude` explicitly). 7 recorded instances, incl. a `paths` filter omitting the very input its own gate reads. **STANDING HAZARD: deploy does not run root `npm run build` — both workflows re-list the steps inline, so a new build step is absent in production by default and no gate compares the two lists.**

verdicts.title: CLASS 15: A read taken on a frame where the value is not yet real
verdicts.reason: Distinct from Class 3 despite sharing the `_bandBot` instance: Class 3 is about WHERE chrome is anchored, this is about WHEN a value may be read, and its other instances are independent (the double-`advance()` layout trap, `this.now` freezing `age` on a paused roll so a canvas floor assertion passed against a build with the glow deleted, Chrome dispatching blur-from-detach while `isConnected` still reads TRUE, a touch reading taken 450ms after touchend measuring a state the app had already reset). Each cost a separate debugging loop and none is deducible from the code at the read site.
verdicts.rewrite: **Before reading a measured value, prove the thing measured has laid out and the clock it depends on is running.** 6 recorded instances: a camera read taken inside one `advance()` describes nothing (the card's top was 588 on that frame and 376 on the next — a second bare `advance` is not enough, an intervening `page.evaluate` is what forces layout); `parkOn` pauses and **`this.now` IS the game clock**, so a paused roll freezes every `age`-derived value and a canvas floor assertion passed against a build with the glow deleted; Chrome dispatches a blur from DETACH while `isConnected` still reads TRUE, so a commit decision must be deferred one real tick; a reading taken 450ms after `touchend` measured a state the app had already reset, which invalidated the premise a whole feature rested on. **"Not yet laid out" is SKIP, never zero.**

verdicts.title: CLASS 16: A latch with no enumerated lifter
verdicts.reason: Verified the audit artefact exists and is exactly as described: `_landHidden()` at app.src.jsx:7373 returns `!this._landEl || !!this._landPaneHid || !!this._traySup || !!this._bgDown || !!this._detailCtx` — four holders — with its own comment 'ASK THE HOLDERS, NOT THE PIXELS'. `_bgRestore` now has two callers (:374 via setPaused, :12274 via the node tap) where it had one. The per-pauser latch discipline (`_landAutoPaused`, `_paneAutoPaused`, `_replayAutoPaused`) is the good pattern and is real. The diagnostic instruction ('read the holders before the render path') is the transferable part and appears nowhere else.
verdicts.rewrite: **Every suppression flag declares its complete set of lifters at its definition.** `_bgRestore()` had exactly ONE caller (`setPaused(false)`), so a background tap could only be undone by the PLAY BUTTON — the app did all its work underneath a suppression nobody lifted, and it presents as "nothing happens when I click, but the node lights up". 6 recorded instances, incl. `userActiveNow()` measuring the GAME clock so one click on a paused board latched "user is active" forever. **Diagnostic: `_landHidden()` (app.src.jsx:7373) asks FOUR holders — `_landPaneHid`, `_traySup`, `_bgDown`, `_detailCtx`. Any one stuck leaves a built, mounted, correctly populated card invisible while every other surface behaves. Read the holders before reading the render path.** Good pattern: one latch per pauser (`_landAutoPaused` / `_paneAutoPaused` / `_replayAutoPaused`) so releasing gives back only the pause you took.

verdicts.title: CLASS 18: The name you queried is not the object you meant (selector and scope collisions)
verdicts.reason: Verified two mechanisms that cannot be deduced: the `title` element-name collision (a shell carries a second `<title>` inside an inline SVG, so `HTMLRewriter.on("title")` hits the wrong one — fixed with a `data-share-title` marker asserted exactly once), and the shared-bundle scope collision (`lists-codec.src.js` and `lists.src.js` are concatenated into one IIFE by build.mjs, so `NG_LIST_ITEM_CAP`/`NG_LIST_MAX_ITEMS` are deliberately different names for one cap). The `body[data-share-cue]` case is the most instructive: a selector that silently returns `<body>` turns every geometric measurement into the whole viewport, which reads as a plausible answer. Distinct from Class 9 (wrong SET) — here the query itself resolves to the wrong OBJECT.
verdicts.rewrite: **Scope every selector to a marker you own and assert it appears exactly once.** A query that resolves to the wrong object returns plausible data, not an error: `body[data-share-cue]` collided with the cue BUTTON's own attribute, so `querySelector` returned `<body>` and every "where is the cue" measurement silently became the whole 390x844 viewport (three journeys red); `HTMLRewriter.on("title", …)` matches by element NAME and the shell carries a second `<title>` inside an inline SVG. 6 recorded instances. **Never query by a shape another object can also have** — element name, a bare attribute, or a computed dimension (a CSS-border triangle computes to `width: 8px`, not 0). Bundle corollary: `lists-codec.src.js` and `lists.src.js` share ONE scope in the IIFE, so no top-level name may collide; `build.mjs` throws on duplicates (its scan used to cover only `function|const`, so a colliding `let` walked past the guard into the SyntaxError it exists to prevent).

verdicts.title: CLASS 21: An index-keyed or positional format fails plausibly and reports nothing
verdicts.reason: Survives, but must be rewritten NARROWER than proposed — four of its six cited instances are borrowed (the `s` two-pairs case is Class 7, the cal key spelling is Class 1/10, `deg` vs `siteDeg` is Class 11, `links`-as-index-pairs is Class 23). What is unique and not stated anywhere else is the `cal.ev` join and, critically, its GATE SHAPE: a wrong remap finds rows, prints integers on every card and prints the wrong technique's number on each, so a non-null count passes perfectly — the assertion must be a whole-structure differential plus a non-triviality floor (>1200 cards carrying a real mark) so it cannot pass on a build where both sides came back empty. That remedy is worth its own entry.
verdicts.rewrite: **A positional/index join fails by printing the wrong right-looking answer.** `cal.ev` is keyed `<position node index>/<role>` with `blk[0]` a list of TECHNIQUE node indexes — nothing in the format is self-describing, so a wrong remap still finds rows, still prints an integer on every card, and prints the WRONG technique's number on each: no exception, no warning, no blank. **Gate it with a whole-structure DIFFERENTIAL against a known-good graph PLUS a non-triviality floor** (assert >1200 cards carry a real mark, so it cannot pass on a build where both sides came back empty and every comparison was trivially equal) — never a non-null count, which a wrong-but-complete remap satisfies perfectly. Same shape wherever indices are the key; they are safe only when they never leave the file that defines them.

verdicts.title: CLASS 23: Order decided by an accident of iteration
verdicts.reason: The founding case is load-bearing and permanent: `rglob('*.json')` is unsorted, the layout derives its node list from adjacency dict-insertion order seeded by that iteration, so adding one content file renumbers pre-existing entries — which is why `node_ordinals.json` exists as an append-only lockfile with a hard gate. The `Array#sort` stability case is a genuinely different mechanism reaching the same failure (21 pairs tie on EDGE, odds AND attempt%, so the name tiebreak is the only thing between the user and node index deciding the tray order). The `movePotential` constant-key case shows a cap over an effectively-unordered list is a random sample. Three user-visible instances; not obvious from any single call site.
verdicts.rewrite: **Any ordering a user or a URL can see needs a strict total order whose final tiebreak is stable CONTENT — never array index, dict insertion order or filesystem order.** `rglob` is unsorted and the layout's node list follows adjacency dict-insertion order seeded by it, so adding ONE content file renumbers pre-existing entries — an index-encoded share link would silently open a different set of techniques with no error anywhere (hence `node_ordinals.json`: permanent, append-only, retired-not-removed, hard-gated). `Array#sort` is stable, so **a comparator that can return 0 hands the decision to the node index** — 21 dealt pairs tie on EDGE, odds AND attempt%, and only the name separates them. 5 recorded instances. **A cap over an unordered list is a random sample**: `movePotential` returned a constant 1 for all 297 submissions, so the 10-cap dealt them alphabetically and truncated the state's most-attempted move.

verdicts.title: CLASS 24: A constant in the code standing in for a value in the data
verdicts.reason: Survives on its unique instances and its unique DETECTION method, though it overlaps Class 10 on the dominance-fallback example. `movePotential`'s `if (n.ty === "submissions") return 1` and `get("dailyGoal",30)+"+"` are neither fallbacks nor missing checks — they are plain hardcoded constants displayed as measurements, and both were invisible for versions. What no other class supplies is the audit heuristic: where printed values are bit-identical, assert the underlying source rows are identical too (42 of 42), and count the distinct values a field actually produces (the dominance fallback prices the whole submission corpus at 2 distinct values against an authored 37).
verdicts.rewrite: **A value identical across a whole category on screen is a constant until proven otherwise.** `movePotential` returned `1` for every submission, so the sort key was constant across all 297; "30+ weak spots" printed `get("dailyGoal",30)+"+"` and read the same for a player with 3 gaps and one with 700; the dominance fallback priced the entire submission corpus at **2 distinct values** where 37 are authored. 4 recorded instances. **Detection, cheap and general: count the DISTINCT values a field actually produces, and where two printed values are bit-identical assert the underlying source rows are identical too** (42 of 42 is the passing shape) — an exact tie on screen must be a tie in the data, never a constant in the code.

verdicts.title: CLASS 26: Shared mutable environment — the run measured someone else's artifact
verdicts.reason: Verified the fix is in place across configs: core :8133, gen :8127, share :8129, replay :8151, catalog :8131, chrome/private/coldstart all `reuseExistingServer: false`; only `playwright.observe.config.ts` keeps true, deliberately. Each config's header carries the postmortem. Also verified the project-memory instance is real and independent (`npm run build` does not rebuild the neural bundle — `dev:neural:app` exists precisely as the sub-second fix). The measured evidence (a run served a 343,153-byte neural.js from a sibling worktree against its own 364,190) makes this falsifiable rather than folklore.
verdicts.rewrite: **A result taken while another process could write the tree under test is not a result.** A config with `reuseExistingServer: true` on a shared port means whichever WORKTREE started it owns it, and every later run tests THAT worktree's `source/public` — measured: a run was served a 343,153-byte `neural.js` from a sibling where its own was 364,190. Every suite therefore owns a dedicated port with `reuseExistingServer:false` (core :8133, gen :8127, share :8129, replay :8151, catalog :8131; only `observe` reuses, deliberately). Two companions: **cache keys name the RESOLVED artifact version, never a file that changes every commit** (the Playwright cache was keyed on package-lock in a repo that bumps the version every commit — the key missed every run while still uploading 261 MiB); and **`npm run build` does NOT rebuild the neural bundle**, so a stale served `neural.js` makes neural journeys 240s-timeout and looks like contention (`npm run dev:neural:app`, <1s).

verdicts.title: CLASS 28: A truncated or narrowed survey before a rename, deletion or retirement
verdicts.reason: Independently verified the blast radius: `grep -rn auto_pick e2e/gen/*.spec.ts` returns 7 distinct spec files today, against the 3 consumers the truncated survey reported. The app has completed the retirement (`fx("hesitated", …)` at app.src.jsx:11205, `auto_pick` gone). The class is the cheapest of all to avoid and the one most likely to be repeated by an agent under time pressure — it is a method trap with no code site, so it cannot live anywhere but here. The hand-maintained-enumeration variant (`attachInput`'s early-return list, no gate deriving it) is a real second instance.
verdicts.rewrite: **Never pipe the survey that decides a rename or deletion through `head`.** The `auto_pick` retirement was scoped from a truncated grep showing 3 consumers; the real list was **7 gen specs + 2 core specs**, and the core one only surfaced when the full suite went red. **Count in full (`| wc -l` first, then read all).** Second form of the same trap: where the enumeration is hand-maintained rather than derived, a new member is missing by default — `attachInput`'s overlay early-return list has no gate deriving it, and `.ng-seemore` was absent from it for its entire existence, dead to the mouse the whole time.

verdicts.title: CLASS 29: The inner gate is weaker than the outer gate it is supposed to protect
verdicts.reason: Both halves verified. `tests/artifacts/graph_validation_baseline.json` now reads `max_errors: 0` with a note stating it was 76 while both deploys hard-fail on the first — so a PR could land 76 errors and still deploy-fail. And the unenumerated-baseline half is worse than described: `e2e/gen/ledger.json` holds 179 tests, ALL with `status: "accepted"`, and no known-red list exists in any config, script or workflow — the 13 names live only in CLAUDE.md prose, so the phrase "the same 13 names" was uncheckable for four versions and the count has since moved to 14.
verdicts.rewrite: **A tolerance baseline must be at least as strict as the gate downstream of it, and must ENUMERATE what it tolerates by name.** The PR ratchet allowed 76 graph errors while both deploys hard-fail on the first, so a PR could land 76 and still deploy-fail (now 0). The `e2e:gen` red baseline is worse: it exists ONLY as prose — `e2e/gen/ledger.json` marks all 179 tests `accepted` and no config, script or workflow carries a known-red list — so "the same 13 names" was unfalsifiable across four versions and has since drifted to 14. **An aggregate count is unfalsifiable and rots into permanent noise; put the baseline where the runner reads it, not where the reader reads it.**

verdicts.title: CLAUDE.md is one version behind HEAD and its running count of the `n.y`-vs-`LY(n)` bug class is already wrong (three vs five)
verdicts.reason: Verified exactly. HEAD is 465653c77 / package.json 1.129.7; CLAUDE.md's newest narrative is v1.129.6 and the file was last touched by c897d19de. HEAD's commit body says verbatim "FIFTH INSTANCE of the `n.y`-where-the-renderer-draws-at-`LY(n)` defect (hover and tap in v1.114.3, rollFromPosition in v1.114.4, four specs in v1.125.0)" while CLAUDE.md L1020 still says "for the third time". `headPos()` is at app.src.jsx:1333 and feeds `camFocus` at :1347 and :1370 — the two callers the canon never records. Separately, HEAD also CORRECTS a canon line the rewrite would otherwise carry forward: the v1.125.0 claim that `adj[<either member>]` is "byte-for-byte today's `adj[<hub>]`, in the same order" is measured false in 136/136 (the pair tie, and order legitimately differs).
verdicts.rewrite: Fold into the Class-11 entry above (which states five instances). Two additional corrections that must land in the same pass: **`headPos()` feeds `camFocus` through two callers, so a wrong ground point makes the camera and the light wrong TOGETHER — which is why neither looked broken alone**; and the v1.125.0 line "`adj[<either member>]` is byte-for-byte `adj[<hub>]`, in the same order" is **false as written** — measured over 136/136 hubs the two members differ by exactly the pair tie and the order legitimately differs (a kind-2 site link is pushed one-way). The design claim holds; a spec written against the literal wording goes red on a correct build.

verdicts.title: "89 main names are ambiguous" measures 110 today — stated twice, and the surrounding facts are exact
verdicts.reason: Re-measured against the shipped wire `source/quartz/static/neural/graph-data.json` with the app's own splitName regex: 1467 nodes ✓, 648 qualified ✓, Kimura 35 ✓, Americana 16 ✓ — and ambiguous main names = **110**, with **561** nodes that would render qualified. Every neighbouring figure reproduces exactly, which makes the one that does not more dangerous, not less: a reader has no signal to distrust it. (Note: my first measurement returned 157/974/1899 because I read `neural/src/graph-data.json`, a Jul-12 stale copy — see the separate .dc.html/stale-copy finding.)
verdicts.rewrite: **Render the FULL authored name on every list, share and option surface — never `splitName().main` alone.** Measured on the shipped wire (`source/quartz/static/neural/graph-data.json`, 1467 nodes): **648 carry a `from <position>` qualifier, 110 main names are shared, and 561 nodes would render qualified**. "Kimura" is 35 different techniques here, "Americana" 16 — the qualifier IS the disambiguator, and dropping it destroys the point of a shared class. Same rule for add/remove toasts and the `l-manifest.json` og preview.

verdicts.title: UNDOCUMENTED VERIFICATION TRAP: `neural/src/Neural Graph.dc.html` is a 288KB non-built copy of the whole app that grep-hits every symbol the canon calls deleted
verdicts.reason: Verified and stronger than stated. `neural/build/build.mjs` reads only app.src.jsx, xdc-template.html, props.json, helmet.html, sound/challenge/lists sources and the CSS — the .dc.html files are not inputs. `Neural Graph.dc.html` is 288,327 bytes, modified Aug 22 12:22 (same day as HEAD), and carries LIVE code for every symbol the canon calls deleted (e.g. `bar.style.animation = "ngCount " + decisionSec` at :3059). Correction to the claim: the app.src.jsx and xdc-template.html hits for those symbols are COMMENTS documenting the deletion, so every real code hit is in the .dc.html. All these files are gitignored by the `neural/src/*` allow-list, so they never reach CI — they only poison greps. I hit this class myself during verification, reading the stale `neural/src/graph-data.json` (Jul 12) and getting 1899 nodes.
verdicts.rewrite: **`neural/src/` contains non-build design dumps that grep exactly like the app.** `Neural Graph.dc.html` (288KB, touched as recently as HEAD), the other `*.dc.html`, `support.js`, `flashcards.json` and `graph-data.json` are NOT build inputs — `neural/build/build.mjs` reads only `app.src.jsx`, `xdc-template.html`, `helmet.html`, `props.json`, `technique-content.js` and the `*.src.js` / `*.css` files — and all of them are gitignored. So every symbol the canon calls deleted (`movePopularity`, `_hash01`, `_freqMap`, `.ng-drilltab`, the `ngCount` animation) still grep-hits, with live-looking code, and the stale `graph-data.json` reports 1899 nodes where the shipped wire has 1467. **Scope any grep or measurement to the build inputs, and read the shipped wire from `source/quartz/static/neural/`.**

verdicts.title: The setPointerCapture / hidden-overlay instance counters are internally out of order
verdicts.reason: Verified: CLAUDE.md L2840 (v1.101.5) says "Fourth instance" of setPointerCapture; L2853 (v1.100.2 — an EARLIER version, printed after it in the file) says "Fifth instance of this repo's recurring bug class" about the opacity/hit-test defect; L2064 (v1.123.0) says "SIXTH INSTANCE OF THE setPointerCapture BUG CLASS". Two mechanisms with two different fixes (early-return list vs `visibility:hidden`) are counted against one informal register, so the sequence reads 5, 4, 6. The code is the arbiter and is self-consistent: `attachInput` numbers its own list Fourth/FIFTH/SIXTH SURFACE and holds exactly six entries. A reader who conflates the two classes applies the wrong fix.

Split into the two entries already written above (Class 5's mechanisms 1 and 3) and count each separately: **pointer-capture retargeting = 6 surfaces**, the list being `attachInput`'s own early-return (node card, dossier sheet, landing card, film strip, option-detail sheet, see-more hint); **hit-testing through a transparent overlay = a separate class with a separate fix (`visibility:hidden`), at least one site still leaky (`app.src.jsx:3456`)**. State each count as "N recorded instances as of v1.129.7" so a future reader can tell drift from disagreement.

verdicts.title: UNSETTLED: the graph-integrity headline ("Errors: 0, Warnings: 7, 345 info of which 295 attempt_negligible", "now 49") could not be re-measured read-only
verdicts.reason: Confirmed only the mechanical half: `import os` is present at scripts/validate_graph_integrity.py:25 so the check can execute, the in-code comment at :648-651 records the swallowed NameError verbatim, and tests/artifacts/graph_validation_baseline.json really is max_errors 0. The `from_position_role_mismatch` "all 65" and the `e2e:gen` "88 passed / 13 failed" split are likewise unverified — I confirmed all 13 named spec files plus the 14th exist, and that `auto_pick` is now referenced by 7 gen specs while the app emits `hesitated` instead.

verdicts.title: The trap list is the product: organise by TRIGGER TOKEN, not by theme, and by CLASS, not by instance
verdicts.reason: The supporting facts check out and are the argument. The file re-narrates one overlay lesson across v1.69.1, v1.81.3, v1.100.2, v1.101.5, v1.104.2 and v1.123.0 while `attachInput`'s own comment block already compresses it to six numbered surfaces plus 'the list is the cure' — the compression exists in code and was never applied to the prose. The ~270 chars/trap budget is consistent with what a trap needs (rule + recognisable symptom + token) — every entry I wrote above lands in that range.
verdicts.rewrite: Structural directive, not a trap entry. Apply as: (1) every entry OPENS with the symbol/file/API in backticks so `grep attachInput CLAUDE.md` lands on it; (2) one entry per CLASS with a bare instance list, never one per incident; (3) budget 12,000–14,000 chars — below 12,000 the symptom gets cut, and a trap without its symptom cannot be recognised from inside the bug.

verdicts.title: Trap class — input & overlay (the repo's single most expensive recurring class)
verdicts.reason: Verified every sub-item that is checkable: the `attachInput` guard and its six-surface list (app.src.jsx:12146-12191); `pointer-events:auto` inline on `[data-land-foot]` (:9565); `visibility:hidden !important` in `_suppressLand` (:7403) and its ABSENCE at the still-leaky :3456; `NG_LAND_MORE_COL` as the written-not-cleared resting colour; the three dock seams; the z-ladder banding in helmet.html; `_landHidden()`'s four holders (:7373); the CSS-border triangle note; the scroll-snap removal (`scroll-snap-type` gone from xdc-template.html, only the inert `scroll-snap-align` remains). Ten sub-rules, four distinct physical mechanisms, one still-open bug — this is the correct grouping.
verdicts.rewrite: Ship as the entries already written for Class 5 (mechanisms 1-4 + `j.clickByMouse`), Class 3 (docking), Class 16 (`_landHidden` holders), plus three Tier-2 one-liners: **`style.color = ""` DELETES an inline declaration, it does not restore one — write the constant (`NG_LAND_MORE_COL`)**; **the app wrap is `position:fixed` = its own stacking context, so a deliberate screen must portal to the root plane; pick a z BAND (1-9 ambient / 10-49 fx / 50-79 coaching / 90-99 deliberate screens), never a loose number**; **a 44px thumb target must not set a 24px row's layout box — shrink the box with a negative margin, keep the hit area.**

verdicts.reason: Verified the seams: `pairMid()` at app.src.jsx:7713, `this._LY = LY` at :12340 with the 'ONE definition' comment, `NG_LABEL_LEFT_MIN` at :328 applied to the drawn silhouette at :11907, and `share-camera.spec.ts:11-25` carrying the camTarget rule with 'camTarget has nine writers'. verdicts.title: Trap class — test honesty: the rules that stop a green suite from meaning nothing
verdicts.reason: Verified the checkable sub-items: `j.clickByMouse` is documented as refusing to scroll and failing on an intercepting ancestor; every config's `reuseExistingServer:false` and dedicated port; `dev:neural:app` exists as the stale-bundle fix; `check_no_raw_random.sh` enforces exactly 1 `Math.random()` in app.src.jsx and 0 in sound.src.js; 13 static `rng()` tags. This is the class most likely to be re-learned expensively because every violation LOOKS like success, and it is entirely method — no code site owns it.
verdicts.rewrite: Ship as the entries already written for Class 4 (T-SPEC-1), Class 2 (blind gates), Class 13 (harness omissions) and Class 26 (shared environment), plus two Tier-1 one-liners that have no other home: **a probe is evidence for a commit message; only a spec is a gate** — two consecutive versions shipped a fix whose mutant then survived, because it had been probed and never pinned; and **a journey that leaves a gameplay `rng()` tag unrigged has bought a lottery ticket that only prints when it loses** — `graph-naming` left `rng("opp-finish")` live and was a 7.7% coin toss for its whole life, hidden by four consecutive green full suites (P ≈ 0.73). verdicts.title: FINISHED COPY (a): T-INPUT-1 — a control inside a fixed overlay is dead to the mouse
verdicts.reason: Copy is accurate against the code. `attachInput`'s guard at app.src.jsx:12146-12191 names exactly the six surfaces and its own comment ends 'Sixth time; the list is the cure' and 'Every fixed overlay that owns its own controls needs to be named here; the alternative is finding it once per surface, by hand, forever'. verdicts.rewrite:
#### T-INPUT-1 — a control inside a fixed overlay is dead to the mouse
**Fires when** you add, move or re-parent a clickable element inside a fixed overlay on the app root (`.ng-landcard`, `.ng-landfilm`, `.ng-seemore`, the option-detail sheet, the node card, any new one) — or you touch `attachInput`.
**Mechanism** `attachInput`'s `pointerdown` calls `setPointerCapture()` on the wrap. That RETARGETS the later `pointerup` to the wrap, so the browser resolves the click from the down/up common ancestor and the listener inside your overlay never runs. Separately, `pointer-events` is inherited and the overlay root disables it: a control that does not re-enable it INLINE is hit-tested straight through to the canvas.
**Looks like** the element measures correctly, `elementFromPoint` returns it, a real mouse click does nothing. Keyboard paths work — that is what hides it. `locator.click()` passes, because it dispatches on the element.
**Count** 6 surfaces in the guard (`app.src.jsx:12146-12191`, numbered Fourth/FIFTH/SIXTH in code), plus the deleted coach button in v1.69.1. `.ng-seemore` was dead to the mouse for its entire existence. A human found every one.
**Do** add the overlay to `attachInput`'s early-return list; set `pointer-events:auto` inline on the control; pin it with `j.clickByMouse(sel)` — never `locator.click()`. **Partially pinned: the list is hand-maintained and no gate derives it.**

But the 'three sites unverified' figure is now wrong in BOTH directions and needs re-measuring before it ships: the mobile-pane pair has since been routed through `_suppressLand` (applyDeckVisibility, ~:2076-2083) and is FIXED, while `expandOption` at :3456 still writes `opacity="0"; pointerEvents="none"` on `_landEl` with no visibility — that is the v1.100.2 defect, live at HEAD. So the entry should name one confirmed-leaky site rather than three unverified ones, which makes it the most actionable line in the section instead of scaremongering.
verdicts.rewrite:
#### T-INPUT-2 — a hidden overlay that still eats clicks
**Fires when** you hide an overlay by writing `opacity:0` and/or `pointer-events:none`.
**Mechanism** hit-testing ignores opacity, and `pointer-events` is inherited — so any descendant that re-enables it INLINE stays live across its whole box. `[data-land-foot]` does exactly that, deliberately, because it holds `More ▸` and the capture `+` (`app.src.jsx:9565`). The overlay is invisible and still on top.
**Looks like** something UNDERNEATH the hidden element is dead to the mouse. `elementFromPoint` at your target returns the thing you thought was gone — measured: `<div data-land-foot="1">` at the centre of a capture button, 120s of Playwright retries.
**Count** 5 instances by v1.100.2. **STILL LEAKY AT HEAD: `app.src.jsx:3456`** — `expandOption` stands the landing card down with opacity + pointer-events only. The mobile-pane pair now routes through `_suppressLand` and is fixed.
**Do** also set `visibility:hidden !important` (inherited, nothing here escapes it with `visible`, removes the subtree from hit-testing) — `_suppressLand` at `:7403` is the reference. Assert inertness with `elementFromPoint`, never with a visual check. **UNGUARDED — no gate enumerates the hide-sites.**

verdicts.reason: Copy is accurate and every named seam exists: `_lastPairLabel` (app.src.jsx:12972, cleared each frame at :12983), `_lastRichLabel` (:12835), `this._LY = LY` (:12340). The self-indicting instance is the strongest sentence in the entry and is verifiable from the file's own text. The final clause — that a second implementation is legitimate only when it also asserts set-equality — is the right escape hatch and matches `option-hand`'s actual design. Ship as written.
verdicts.rewrite:
#### T-SPEC-1 — never assert a render by re-implementing it
**Fires when** a spec, probe or audit computes the expected answer itself: `nodes.filter(...)`, a private copy of a filter or of "what the node set is", a hand rebuilt from `adj`, a screen coordinate recomputed from `n.x`/`n.y`.
**Mechanism** you write the copy from the same reading of the code you are testing, usually with the fix already in it. The two agree by construction, so the assertion measures nothing.
**Looks like** green — on a build you have already broken. The v1.126.0 audit built to find this class committed it: its probe measured `nodes.filter(n => n.rep && …)` and reported "identical" about Explore's search, which was doubling every hit and halving its own 120-row cap.
**Count** 6 specs held private copies of the node set (v1.125.0), plus 1 in the audit that hunted them (v1.126.0), plus three pixel oracles that could not kill their mutant because the geometry lived in a draw-local closure.
**Do** drive the real entry point — `renderExplorer()`, `optionsFor()`, `draw()` — and assert on what it EMITTED: DOM rows, duplicate row text, read-back pixels. When the geometry lives in a closure (`halfW`, `ox`) you cannot recompute it at all: PUBLISH it (`_lastPairLabel`, `_lastRichLabel`, `this._LY = LY`) and read the published value. A second implementation is legitimate ONLY when it also asserts set-equality against the app's own result.

verdicts.title: MISLEADING: the Position and Transition JSON schema examples are wrong in both key name and value shape
verdicts.reason: Verified against the corpus. `content/Positions/Mount.json` has `{"transition": "Mount to Armbar", "attempt_probability": {"gi": 6, "nogi": 7}}` — the key is `transition`, not `name`, and the value is a per-ruleset map. `content/Transitions/100% Sweep.json` has `"success_rate": {"gi": 50, "nogi": 50}` and outcome `"probability": {"gi": 50, "nogi": 50}`. CLAUDE.md §4 shows `"name"` with scalar 25 and scalar 55. The document contradicts itself — its own Q3-occurrence row in §5 correctly describes `{gi,nogi}` maps summing to 100 per frame. §4 is the most-copied block in the file and an agent authoring from it writes files that fail validation, or worse writes scalars a divergence-tolerant reader mis-parses.
verdicts.rewrite: Not a trap entry — fix the examples before anything else, they are the most-copied block in the file. **A position's transition entry is `{"transition": "<name>", "attempt_probability": {"gi": N, "nogi": M}}` — the key is `transition`, not `name`, and the value is a per-ruleset MAP that must sum to 100 PER FRAME.** **A transition's `success_rate` and every outcome `probability` are `{gi, nogi}` maps too**, not scalars; the scalar `successRate` in `graph.json` is the FOLDED no-gi default, with the pair carried alongside as `successRateByRuleset`. Both blocks currently contradict §5's own Q3-occurrence description.

verdicts.title: MISLEADING: "Attacker/Defender sections are generated by templates, not stored in the source JSON" — they ARE in the JSON
verdicts.reason: Verified: `content/Transitions/100% Sweep.json` has top-level `attacker` and `defender` objects. Attacker carries overview, key_principles, setup_requirements, execution_steps, common_counters, common_errors, training_progressions, flashcards, safety_considerations, clips, description, name; defender additionally carries recognition_cues, defensive_options, favorable_outcomes. The templates render those fields; they do not author them. CLAUDE.md asserts the opposite twice (§4, both the file-structure block and the Transition Schema rules). Combined with the correct rule 'never edit generated .md', an agent asked to fix one technique's defender copy is told the content is not in the JSON and the .md is off-limits, leaving the shared Jinja2 template as the only apparent target — which would change all 1,034 transitions.
verdicts.rewrite: Not a trap entry — a correction with a real blast radius. **Reword §4: the attacker/defender SECTIONS of the generated `.md` are template-rendered FROM the `attacker` and `defender` blocks that live in the source JSON.** As written ("generated by templates, not stored in the source JSON") plus the correct "never edit generated `.md`" rule, an agent fixing one technique's defender copy is left with the shared `TEMPLATE-DEFENDER.md.jinja2` as the only apparent target — a one-file edit that rewrites all 1,034 transitions.

verdicts.title: KEEP: the pair is derived at ingest, the rep IS the hub, and `adj` must NOT be role-split
verdicts.reason: The three facts are right and each is counter-intuitive: two orbs but ONE node id (so nothing was migrated), the partner mints `<hub>/Bottom` with `o: null` (which is why `siteIdOf` exists), and `adj` must stay role-agnostic (verified `pairMid` and the derivation exist; the content-capstone failure is the evidence). But one supporting line must NOT be carried forward: HEAD (v1.129.7) measured the v1.125.0 claim that `adj[<either member>]` is "byte-for-byte `adj[<hub>]`, in the same order" and found it false in 136 of 136 — the members differ by exactly the pair tie, and order legitimately differs because a kind-2 site link is pushed one-way. The design claim survives; the wording does not, and a spec written against the literal wording goes red on a correct build.
verdicts.rewrite: **The pair is DERIVED at ingest, and the rep member IS the hub** — same id, same share ordinal, same URL, so `node_ordinals.json` was never touched and every `/l/<code>` still resolves. The partner mints `<hub>/Bottom` / `<hub>/Defender` with **`o: null`**, which is why lists must normalise through `siteIdOf`. **DO NOT ROLE-SPLIT `adj`:** `opponentDefend`, `_mcPool` and `_posIdx` walk `adj[currentPos]` with no role filter deliberately — they are asking about the EXCHANGE, not your hand — and splitting it handed the opponent YOUR hand and reddened `content-capstone`. Each member therefore carries the technique set of its site. **Do not repeat the retired wording "byte-for-byte, in the same order": measured 136/136, the two members' `adj` differ by exactly the pair tie and the order differs (a site link is pushed one-way).** `?dual=legacy` is the escape hatch; the geometry claims and byte deltas belong in the archive.

verdicts.title: KEEP: lists store SITES — `siteIdOf` normalisation, because only a hub carries an ordinal
verdicts.reason: Verified in code: `siteIdOf` at app.src.jsx:5452 with nine call sites, and critically it is applied to the READERS as well as the writer — `activeListHas` (:5465), `addToList` (:5508), `removeFromList` (:5528), the id-index lookup (:5790), `listItemName` (:5822), `nodeInAnyList`/`listsWith` (:6029, :6036), `openListPicker` (:6096, commented "the picker's ✓ must read the id the list will hold"). The non-deducible part is exactly the part the code cannot state: normalising only the WRITE makes a captured technique show `+` instead of `✓` on the very orb you captured it from, and the reachability figures (136 of 272 position landings, 172 of 400 technique seats stand on a partner) are what turn this from an edge case into "every time the coach is playing bottom".
verdicts.rewrite: **A list holds SITES, so `siteIdOf` normalises in the LIST LAYER — in the writer AND in every membership reader.** Only a hub carries a share ordinal; the pair's partner mints `<hub>/Bottom` with `o: null`, so a `+` pressed while standing on the lower orb filed an id that `ngListEncodeIds` reports as `missing` — the technique is **dropped from the share code with no error**, and a one-item list of it encodes to the empty string. Not an edge case: **136 of 272 position landings and 172 of 400 technique seats stand on a partner**, i.e. every time you are playing bottom. Normalising only the write is the tempting half-fix and is wrong — it makes a captured technique show `+` instead of `✓` on the very orb you captured it from. Identity on any unpaired node, so `?dual=legacy` is untouched.

verdicts.title: KEEP: an unrigged `rng()` tag is a lottery ticket that only prints when it loses
verdicts.reason: The trap is CONFIRMED and generalises well beyond its spec — the deductive argument (rig `opp-finish` and the branch becomes unreachable) is stronger than the statistics, and the file says so, which is itself the model for how to report a flake. The determinism seam is verified: `scripts/check_no_raw_random.sh` allows exactly 1 `Math.random()` in app.src.jsx and 0 in sound.src.js, and it fails loudly with line numbers. One correction: the tag list is **13** static tags, not 12 — the claim omits `mc-pick`. Full list measured: start-pos, role, outcome, resolve, max-moves, ai-skill, opp-pick, opp-sub-pick, opp-finish, mc-pick, mc-shuffle, escape, checkpoint-pick, plus the surface-scoped variants built dynamically (`land-mc-pick`, `land-mc-shuffle`).
verdicts.rewrite: **A journey that leaves a gameplay `rng()` tag unrigged has not chosen a branch, it has bought a lottery ticket — and the ticket only prints when it loses.** `graph-naming` left `rng("opp-finish")` live, so the opponent could submit you and end the round before the journey's second landing: measured **6 failures in 78 un-rigged runs (7.7%) vs 0 in 30 rigged**, and P(four consecutive green full suites) ≈ 0.73, so three earlier clean reports were never evidence of absence. **When a journey's subject is what happens AFTER an exchange, rig every draw that can end the exchange early.** The 13 static tags: `start-pos, role, outcome, resolve, max-moves, ai-skill, opp-pick, opp-sub-pick, opp-finish, mc-pick, mc-shuffle, escape, checkpoint-pick` (plus surface-scoped `land-mc-*`). The seam is gated: `scripts/check_no_raw_random.sh` allows exactly 1 `Math.random()` in `app.src.jsx` (the `rng()` passthrough) and 0 in `sound.src.js`.

verdicts.title: KEEP: EDGE honesty gap 1 — the shipped opponent is not the opponent the number was computed against
verdicts.reason: Survives on the ground the claim itself names: everything else about EDGE is documented at the constants and in `scripts/solve_edge_values.py`, but this one fact decides whether an EDGE integer may be shown to a user, and it is a disagreement BETWEEN two code paths, so neither file can state it alone. All eleven instances are present in CLAUDE.md.
verdicts.rewrite:
**A CHECK THAT NEVER RAN READS EXACTLY LIKE A CHECK THAT PASSED — 17 recorded instances.** A bare `except: return []`, a zero-length comparison loop, a matcher whose pattern matches nothing, a `git diff --quiet` on an untracked file, a join that misses every key: each emits a plausible negative result. `check_position_type_vs_score` reported "0 disagreements" for months because a missing `import os` raised `NameError` into a bare `except` (real figure 95); the harness held `"flashcards.json"`, a URL the app has not fetched since v1.80.4, so every cold-start assertion measured a warm boot (15 red journeys).
**Do:** every matcher, join, rewrite table and gate emits a POSITIVE coverage count and hard-fails below a floor; a skip path PRINTS; a rule whose `from` string is absent from the source THROWS (`build.mjs`), and a check whose loop had nothing to iterate is an error, not a pass (`check_headers_cache.py` check 6a).

verdicts.title: CLASS 2: A gate cited as evidence that is structurally unable to fail on its subject
verdicts.reason: `grep -c` on CLAUDE.md: 'Treat it as unguarded' 1 (CategoryNav), 'Treat the catalog as unguarded' 1, 'structurally blind' 2, 'STRUCTURALLY unable' 2, 'structurally incapable' 1, 'do not read a green payload gate' 1 — five separate vocabularies, never joined. Verified downstream: `scripts/check_seo_parity.py:138-140` narrows to `<article>` and its own scope note at :54-58 says two findings have hidden there and names CategoryNav; `source/quartz/components/CategoryNav.tsx` exists and no gate references it. `scripts/check_forward_catalog.mjs:1-3` is an 'Offline smoke check … fails on a throw, an empty render, a nested <button>' — no parity gate against `renderSettings`, and `forward/shared/fixtures.js:494` records the retired rows surviving there. `e2e/prototype/` does not exist and `prototype` appears in no config's `testDir` (all nine configs checked). `tests/artifacts/graph_validation_baseline.json` max_errors is 0.
verdicts.rewrite:
**A GREEN GATE IS EVIDENCE ONLY ABOUT WHAT IT CAN SEE — 12 recorded instances of citing one that could not fail.** `payload-first-hand` pins a 7-card hand, so it reports identical bytes with and without the hand cap. `replay-digest` rigs a single-success-cell submission, so the outcome-kernel fix, the `cardOrder` retirement and the loss-aversion dial were all invisible to it. `check_seo_parity.py` scopes to `<article>`, so `CategoryNav.tsx` — the site's only persistent static nav — is UNGUARDED; so is the Forward catalog mock; so was `e2e/prototype/`, which no config's `testDir` has ever collected, through 13 versions including the one that made its subject the default.
**Do:** cite a gate only for a claim a mutant of that claim makes red. Otherwise write its blind spot in the same sentence as the green, in the words 'this gate cannot see X'.

verdicts.title: CLASS 3: Fixed chrome positioned by a constant against a band that is computed
verdicts.reason: All seams exist in `neural/src/app.src.jsx`: `_dockLandCard` (8 mentions in CLAUDE.md), `_dockOptionHint` (2), `_dockLandFilm` (3), `_placeListPicker` (1), `_bandBot` (4 occurrences in app.src.jsx), 'UNDOCKED element is not a constraint' (1).
