The self-count 'third instance' appears once (L1804) against 12 distinct instances in the text — the undercount the claim alleges.
verdicts.rewrite:
**FIXED CHROME MUST DOCK OFF A MEASURED RECT, NEVER A CONSTANT COPIED FROM A NEIGHBOUR'S CURRENT SIZE — 12 instances, self-counted as "the third", still recurring at v1.129.6.** The option tray has no fixed height and grows upward; a width-only breakpoint misses a landscape phone (844px WIDE); a 44px pixel threshold fires for nothing when the thing it measures is radius-anchored (2.2x spread in one frame); the cold fallback `H - 240` is not a band, it is nearly the whole screen. Fixed: `_dockLandCard`, `_dockLandFilm`, `_dockOptionHint`, `_placeListPicker`, `_bandBot`. **STILL OPEN: the phone challenge cue writes across the focus label (6,700 px²) — reproduce with `node tests/artifacts/_cue_collision_probe.mjs`.**
**Do:** measure at runtime, keep the TIGHTEST measurement ever taken at this viewport (a per-landing reset hands the loose answer back on the first frame), and treat a not-yet-laid-out element as SKIP — its `rect.top` reads 0 for one frame and that zero will throw your camera.

verdicts.title: CLASS 4: The spec re-implements the thing it is supposed to observe
verdicts.reason: CLAUDE.md L1151 carries 'Never assert a render by re-implementing it' verbatim (the grep -c missed it only because the sentence wraps mid-phrase). `e2e/journeys/share-camera.spec.ts:11-25` is a header that states the camTarget canon in full: 'frameNodes does not move the camera. It writes camTarget … camTarget has nine [writers] … A test that asserts camTarget'. The published-draw-state seams exist in CLAUDE.md (`_lastPairLabel` 3, `_lastRichLabel` 1, `this._LY = LY` 2) and `option-hand.spec.ts` exists. The v1.126.0 self-indictment (the audit tool committing the defect it hunted) is present at L1148-1153.
verdicts.rewrite:
**NEVER ASSERT A RENDER BY RE-IMPLEMENTING IT — 10 instances, one of them committed by the audit built to find the other six.** You write the copy from the same reading of the code you are testing, usually with the fix already in it, so the two agree by construction and the assertion measures nothing. The v1.126.0 probe measured `nodes.filter(n => n.rep && …)` and reported "identical" about Explore's search, which was doubling every hit.
**Do:** drive the real entry point (`renderExplorer()`, `optionsFor()`, `draw()`) and assert on what it EMITTED — DOM rows, duplicate row text, read-back pixels. When the geometry lives in a draw-local closure (`halfW`, `ox`), you cannot recompute it: PUBLISH it (`this._LY = LY`, `_lastPairLabel`, `_lastRichLabel`) and read the published value — that is the render's output, not a second implementation. Never assert the camera from `camTarget`: the follow-cam rewrites it every frame; project through `draw()`'s transform into the viewport rect (`share-camera.spec.ts` header). A second implementation is legitimate ONLY when it also asserts SET EQUALITY against the app's own result.

verdicts.title: CLASS 5: Reachable, visible and existing are three different facts; the hit-test is the only oracle
verdicts.reason: `neural/src/app.src.jsx:12146-12186` — the `attachInput` pointerdown early-return names exactly six surfaces (node card, dossier sheet, then the loop over `_landEl`, `_landFilmEl`, `optDetailRef`, `optionHintRef`) with in-code numbering 'Fourth surface', 'FIFTH SURFACE (v1.102.1)', 'SIXTH SURFACE (v1.123.0): the "see more" hint … has NEVER been in this list … dead to the mouse for as long as it has existed'. `_suppressLand` at :7403 now writes `visibility:hidden !important`. `j.clickByMouse` exists at `e2e/dsl.ts:673`. AND THE CLASS IS STILL LIVE: `expandOption` at :3456 still hides `_landEl` with `style.opacity="0"` + `pointerEvents="none"` ONLY, while `[data-land-foot]` at :9565 sets `pointer-events:auto` inline in its cssText — the exact leaky pair v1.100.2 fixed elsewhere.
verdicts.rewrite:
**A CONTROL CAN MEASURE CORRECTLY, HIT-TEST CORRECTLY AND STILL BE DEAD TO THE MOUSE — 10+ instances, four different physical causes.** (1) `attachInput`'s pointerdown calls `setPointerCapture()` on the wrap, which RETARGETS pointerup, so the browser resolves the click to the down/up common ancestor and your listener never runs — every fixed overlay owning controls must be in that early-return list (6 surfaces today; `.ng-seemore` went its whole life without one). (2) `pointer-events` is INHERITED and the overlay root disables it — re-enable it inline or the canvas hit-tests through. (3) Hit-testing IGNORES opacity: `opacity:0` + `pointer-events:none` leaves an invisible strip live wherever a child re-enables pointer-events inline. **`visibility:hidden !important` is what removes a subtree from hit-testing — and `expandOption` (app.src.jsx:3456) still writes the leaky form over `[data-land-foot]`, which sets `pointer-events:auto` inline. UNFIXED.** (4) A z-index inside the `position:fixed` wrap is trapped at plane 0.
**Do:** prove reachability with `j.clickByMouse(sel)` — a real pointer at measured coordinates plus `elementFromPoint`. `locator.click()` dispatches on the element and therefore proves nothing; it masked every one of these.

verdicts.title: CLASS 6: A second, stale implementation of a question that already had a seam
verdicts.reason: All nine instances present in CLAUDE.md with their symbols intact ('SECOND, STALE' 1 hit, 'second stale implementation' 1 hit, `NG_LIST_ITEM_CAP` and `NG_LIST_MAX_ITEMS` 1 each, `opponentDefend` 10, `movePotential` 7). The `_dockLandFilm`/`NG_LAND_MORE_COL` pair is verified in code — `NG_LAND_MORE_COL` is a real constant at app.src.jsx:4 (the two-writer fix). The `techniqueOrigin` seam exists in app.src.jsx.
verdicts.rewrite:
**WHEN ONE QUESTION IS ANSWERED IN TWO PLACES, ONE OF THEM IS ALREADY WRONG — 9 instances, self-named once as "one level down".** `playFrom` was a whole stale copy of `rollFromPosition` (hard-coded camera, no archive, no state reset). `rollFromPosition` then walked `adj[]` for a technique's origin while `confirmPlayFrom` had read `fromPositionId` all along — measured wrong on 907 of 1,331 techniques, with the technique you just tapped absent from the hand you were dealt 68.4% of the time. The same function still aimed at `{n.x, n.y}` a version after `rollCamTarget` existed: "same defect, missed once".
**Do:** collapse to ONE named seam (`rollCamTarget`, `techniqueOrigin`, `captureNode`, `siteIdOf`) BEFORE adding a third caller, and DELETE the copy rather than syncing it. Where two names for one value must coexist (`NG_LIST_ITEM_CAP` / `NG_LIST_MAX_ITEMS`, one scope), a test pins them equal.

verdicts.title: CLASS 7: A heuristic standing in for a fact the data states outright
verdicts.reason: All nine instances present in CLAUDE.md (`valIdx` 2, `fromRole` 4, `seatRole` 2, `withDeck` 1). Verified in code: `this._ambig` is built at app.src.jsx:1179-1183 and read at :1442, i.e. the ambiguity fact is computed from the data rather than guessed; `scripts/regenerate_graph.py:206` uses `positions_dir.rglob('*.json')` (recursive, the fixed form). The v1.103.0 defect is internally coherent with `graph-data.json`, which I re-read directly.
verdicts.rewrite:
**IF THE DATA STATES IT, READ IT — 9 instances of a heuristic standing in for an authored fact.** `optionsFor` inferred the performer from `myVal < oppVal - 0.05` while every technique carries `fromRole`; `roleIdx()` indexed both meanings of `s` with a top/bottom index and a bottom player was shown ZERO of the 297 submissions. **`s` is TWO DIFFERENT PAIRS: `[top,bottom]` for a POSITION, `[attacker,defender]` for a TECHNIQUE — index by PERFORMER (`valIdx`), never by side.** A fallback may relax ORIGIN; it must never relax ROLE.
**Do:** a derivation that returns the SAME answer for the whole corpus is not a derivation, it is a constant with a function around it — all 136 position titles end "… Top", which is why `seatRole` exists for the 596 bottom-authored techniques and why you must never derive a role from a node title.

verdicts.title: CLASS 8: A single-slot resource with many writers and no declared owner
verdicts.reason: All nine instances present in CLAUDE.md, and the fix seams are real code: `HESITATE_HOLD` (1 mention), `holdCamera` (2), 'ONE rAF OWNS' (1), `_bumpStageVer` (2), and in app.src.jsx `_trayStop()` at :294 is called by `_trayFling` at :314 and by a new grab at :489 — exactly the 'one rAF owns scrollLeft' contract. The still-unfixed 'Time's up never reaches the screen' disclosure is present and explicitly marked pre-existing and not fixed.
verdicts.rewrite:
**A SINGLE-SLOT RESOURCE NEEDS A STAMPED OWNER AND AN EXPLICIT LIFETIME — 9 instances, always found as "the thing I wrote is not there any more".** `setEvent` has ONE announcer slot: a share-arrival toast never reached a real recipient (overwritten within seconds), "Decide 1…" got stuck, and "Time's up" is STILL never seen because `enterAttempt` overwrites it synchronously on the next line. `camTarget` has nine writers and the follow-cam rewrites it every frame, so every selection flight was eaten within one frame until `holdCamera()` gave it a 7s LEASE.
**Do:** hold (`_announceArrival` defers to the next landing), lease (`holdCamera`/`releaseCamera`, released by any real pan/pinch/wheel), stamp (`_evCountdown`, released by every other `setEvent`), or own the rAF (`_trayStop` before any glide, fling, tween or teardown). Never assume your write is the last one.

verdicts.title: CLASS 9: The measurement is sound and its SUBJECT is wrong — canon numbers that do not reproduce
verdicts.reason: Independently re-measured two of the eight and both confirm the class. (1) The v1.127.1 correction is CURRENT: over `source/quartz/static/neural/graph-data.json`, position nodes = 136 and strictly-opposite-sign `s` = 115 — exactly the corrected figure, and the '85 of 136' it replaced is the stale one. (2) The ambiguity figure is ITSELF now stale in the same way — see the dedicated verdict below (110, not 89). `tests/artifacts/_opponent_gap_measure.py` exists on disk, so the class's own remedy (ship the recompute command with the number) is already practised in one place. 'A canon number nobody can reproduce is worse than no number' is present verbatim.
verdicts.rewrite:
**A NUMBER WITHOUT A REPRODUCTION RECIPE IS A STORY — 8 instances where the measurement was sound and its SUBJECT was wrong.** The opponent-gap figure (9.1 / 23.2% / 2476) measured a set the model never holds and understated the gap by half; the position-colour figure was quoted as 85 of 136 and re-measures at 115; a tray-drag premise rested on a reading taken 450ms after touchend, by which time the app had already reset; a 340px canvas sweep read OTHER nodes' labels; a raw-innerHTML jargon check hits `class="paceVal"` and reports a leak that is not on screen.
**Do:** every canon figure carries its SET DEFINITION and the exact command that recomputes it, in the same sentence (`tests/artifacts/_opponent_gap_measure.py` is the pattern). Before quoting a figure, re-derive it — the file's own corrections show at least three drifted once already.

verdicts.title: CLASS 10: A fallback that substitutes a plausible value and never says it fired
verdicts.reason: All eight instances present in CLAUDE.md, and the two GOOD patterns it names are real named beats: `mc_pool_cold` (1) and `land_warm_stalled` (1). The emitter-side remedy is verified downstream by CLASS 21's evidence — `_tech_keys` plus a coverage floor that refuses to write a wire below 95% per type. `withDeck` (the no-op filter) appears once.
verdicts.rewrite:
**A FALLBACK THAT PRODUCES PLAUSIBLE OUTPUT IS STRICTLY WORSE THAN A CRASH — it buys months of silence. 8 instances.** A missing `cal` made `calSuccess()` return null and `moveChance` fall back to `0.36 + dom*0.1`, so ~289 of 1,204 dealt cards printed a fabricated ~45.6% against an authored range of 10–74%, for months, with nothing red anywhere. `posIdx` falling back to the technique itself staged a roll ON A TECHNIQUE NODE for 1,331 of 2,934 nodes. 54 of 136 positions ran entirely on the no-candidates fallback.
**Do:** every fallback emits a NAMED BEAT or increments a counter — `mc_pool_cold` and `land_warm_stalled` are the two that do it right. Choose the fallback BEFORE the draw so the rng call count cannot depend on content, and never let a fallback relax ROLE.

verdicts.title: CLASS 11: Reading stored state where the renderer uses derived state
verdicts.reason: CONFIRMED as a class and the count in CLAUDE.md is already wrong. `git log -1 --format=%B 465653c77` (HEAD, v1.129.7) states: 'FIFTH INSTANCE of the `n.y`-where-the-renderer-draws-at-`LY(n)` defect (hover and tap in v1.114.3, rollFromPosition in v1.114.4, four specs in v1.125.0)' and fixes `headPos()`, which 'also feeds `camFocus` via two callers'. CLAUDE.md L1020 still reads 'for the third time'. `pairMid` appears 10 times and `this._LY = LY` twice in CLAUDE.md; both seams are real.
verdicts.rewrite:
**NEVER CONVERT A NODE TO A SCREEN POSITION FROM ITS STORED COORDINATE — the renderer draws at `LY(n)` / `pairMid(n)`, not `n.y`. FIVE recorded instances (v1.114.3 hover AND tap, v1.114.4 `rollFromPosition`, four specs in v1.125.0, `headPos()` in v1.129.7).** The lift is ~37px at roll zoom against a 28px pick radius, so clicking a VISIBLE orb matched nothing; a spec sampling at `n.y` reported "no ring is drawn" about a ring that was drawn; `headPos` fed `camFocus` through two callers, so the camera and the light were wrong TOGETHER and neither looked broken alone.
**Do:** publish the derivation (`this._LY = LY`, stamped every frame) and make `_LY`/`pairMid` the ONLY conversion any consumer or spec may use — both are the identity on an unpaired node, so production geometry is unchanged by construction. Same shape in a different quantity: `deg` is GEOMETRY (split per member), `siteDeg` is the STATE (whole) — reading the split number in `movePotential` halves a value the escape tray prints.

verdicts.title: CLASS 13: The harness is not the product — assertions satisfiable by what the harness omits
verdicts.reason: All seven instances present in CLAUDE.md. Verified against the harness itself: `e2e/dsl.ts:84` documents payload globs as substring matches, :263 routes `**/flashcards/_index.json`, :379-382 documents that 'A spec that holds flashcards.json back cannot ALSO be made to wait for it'. `tests/artifacts/_owner_shoot.mjs` exists — the committed acknowledgement that a screenshot under the harness photographs the harness. `e2e/playwright.coldstart.config.ts` exists as a real alternate config over `./journeys`.
verdicts.rewrite:
**NAME WHAT THE HARNESS DOES NOT SERVE, BESIDE EVERY ASSERTION — if the absence alone would satisfy it, the assertion is about the harness. 7 instances.** The DSL serves `{}` for dossier chunks, so there is no film strip and most states legitimately have no `More` fold; `test.use({reducedMotion})` leaves `matchMedia` FALSE here (use `page.emulateMedia`), so a spec relying on the fixture option asserts nothing and passes forever; the harness aborts non-localhost requests, which is why a `.catch` is load-bearing; MC distractors must not depend on deck residency or network timing picks the options.
**Do:** for a claim about the PRODUCT's look, drive the real dev server with real wall-clock time (`tests/artifacts/_owner_shoot.mjs`), not the harness.

verdicts.title: CLASS 14: CI runs a subset of the chain a human runs, or an allow-list that rots silently
verdicts.reason: Six of seven confirmed, ONE IS NOW FALSE AND ITS RULE IS CONTRADICTED BY THE CODE. Confirmed: `.github/workflows/e2e-full.yml:54` is now `tar -czf complete-e2e-site.tgz -C source public`; `ci-validate.yml` paths include `source/quartz/static/globalGraphLayout.json` and `neural/src/**` with the explanatory comments; `keepalive.yml:40` uses `git status --porcelain`; `serve` is a real devDependency; `graph_validation_baseline.json` max_errors is 0. **STALE: CLAUDE.md says votes-refresh.yml 'now runs the `npm run regenerate:graph` umbrella (graph-base → layout → ordinals → strength). CI must never run a subset of the chain a human runs.' The workflow at lines 50-60 does NOT run the umbrella — it runs `regenerate:graph-base` + `regenerate:graph-strength`, and its own comment says the umbrella 'actually FAILED here every week since it was introduced' because the node2vec/umap-learn stack is not installed, and that it would rewrite files the PR step never stages.** So both the stated fix and the stated rule are contradicted by the current, deliberate implementation.
verdicts.rewrite:
**CI MUST NOT SILENTLY RUN A SUBSET OF THE CHAIN A HUMAN RUNS, AND AN ALLOW-LIST OF EMITTED PATHS ROTS — 7 instances, all found in one pass (v1.104.6).** `votes-refresh.yml` ran bare `regenerate_graph.py` and committed a graph.json with `strength` stripped from 4,464 of 4,465 nodes. `e2e-full.yml` tarred six allow-listed paths, so the PR gate for BOTH protected branches could not pass — package by default and `--exclude` explicitly. `ci-validate.yml`'s paths filter omitted `globalGraphLayout.json`, the INPUT its own ordinal gate reads. `git diff --quiet` reports NO CHANGE for an UNTRACKED file, so `keepalive.yml` never committed anything, ever.
**CORRECTION, verify before quoting:** `votes-refresh.yml` deliberately runs `regenerate:graph-base` + `regenerate:graph-strength` and NOT the umbrella — the umbrella failed there every week (no node2vec/umap stack) and rewrites files the PR step never stages. The rule is therefore "a partial chain must be justified AT THE CALL SITE and must include every step that mutates the artifact it commits", not "always run the umbrella".
**Standing hazard:** deploy does NOT run root `npm run build`; both workflows re-list steps inline, so any new build step is silently absent in production unless added there too.

verdicts.title: CLASS 15: A read taken on a frame where the value is not yet real
verdicts.reason: All six instances present in CLAUDE.md, and the code seam exists: `_bandBot` occurs 4 times in `neural/src/app.src.jsx` (the cached tightest-measurement fix). The paused-clock trap is structurally verifiable — `this.now` is the game clock and `parkOn` pauses, so an age-derived canvas assertion freezes; `graph-naming.spec.ts` exists and is the spec named. The 'blur from DETACH is not a decision' seam is pinned by `e2e/journeys/lists-rename.spec.ts`, which exists.
verdicts.rewrite:
**BEFORE READING A MEASURED VALUE, PROVE THE THING MEASURED HAS LAID OUT AND THE CLOCK YOU DEPEND ON IS RUNNING — 6 instances.** A camera read taken inside one `advance()` describes nothing (the card's top was 588 on one frame and 376 on the next — a second bare `advance` is NOT enough; an intervening `page.evaluate` is what forces layout). An UNDOCKED element's `rect.top` reads 0 for a frame and is not a constraint — SKIP it, never treat it as zero. `parkOn` pauses and `this.now` IS the game clock, so a paused roll freezes every age-derived assertion into a FALSE PASS (a glow floor passed against a build with the glow deleted). A blur from DETACH is not a decision — Chrome dispatches it while `isConnected` still reads TRUE, so defer the commit one real tick.
**Do:** keep the TIGHTEST measurement ever taken at this viewport (`_bandBot`); a per-landing reset hands the loose answer straight back.

verdicts.title: CLASS 16: A latch with no enumerated lifter
verdicts.reason: `neural/src/app.src.jsx:7373-7380` — `_landHidden()` returns `!this._landEl || !!this._landPaneHid || !!this._traySup || !!this._bgDown || !!this._detailCtx`, exactly the four holders named, with an in-code comment 'ASK THE HOLDERS, NOT THE PIXELS'. `_bgRestore` now has TWO callers (`:374` inside `setPaused(false)` and `:12274` on the node tap) — the v1.129.5 fix landed, confirming the one-caller history. The one-latch-per-pauser good pattern is real (`_landAutoPaused`, `_paneAutoPaused`, `_replayAutoPaused`, `_dossierAutoPaused`, `_bgDown` all in CLAUDE.md).
verdicts.rewrite:
**EVERY SUPPRESSION FLAG DECLARES ITS COMPLETE SET OF LIFTERS AT THE DEFINITION — 6 instances of a latch nobody could release. `_bgRestore()` had exactly ONE caller (`setPaused(false)`), so a background tap could only be undone by the PLAY BUTTON: the app dealt the hand, built the card and flew the camera underneath a suppression nobody lifted.**
**Do:** give every multi-holder surface an audit function that names which holder is standing — `_landHidden()` asks FOUR (`_landPaneHid`, `_traySup`, `_bgDown`, `_detailCtx`), and any one stuck leaves a built, mounted, correctly populated card invisible while every other surface behaves. **When a report says "nothing happens but the node lights up", read the holders before the render path.** One latch per pauser (`_landAutoPaused`, `_paneAutoPaused`, `_replayAutoPaused`) so releasing gives back only the pause you took; and never gate on `userActiveNow()`, which measures the GAME clock and latches forever on a paused board.

verdicts.title: CLASS 18: The name you queried is not the object you meant (selector and scope collisions)
verdicts.reason: All six instances present in CLAUDE.md, with two verified downstream: `data-share-title` (the scoped HTMLRewriter marker) appears once and `scripts/build_share_shell.mjs` is a real, wired build step in package.json; `NG_LIST_ITEM_CAP` and `NG_LIST_MAX_ITEMS` appear once each (the deliberate two-names-one-scope pair). `_lastPairLabel` appears 3 times, consistent with the 'holds whichever group drew LAST in the frame' trap.
verdicts.rewrite: **SCOPE EVERY SELECTOR TO A MARKER YOU OWN AND ASSERT IT APPEARS EXACTLY ONCE — 6 instances of querying by a shape another object also has.** `body[data-share-cue]` collided with the cue BUTTON's own attribute, so `querySelector` returned `<body>` and every "where is the cue" measurement silently became the whole 390x844 viewport (three journeys red). `HTMLRewriter.on("title", …)` matches by element NAME and the shell carries a second `<title>` inside an inline SVG — the Function targets `title[data-share-title]`, a marker the builder writes and asserts once. A duplicate-top-level-name guard that scanned only `function|const` let a colliding `let` walk into the SyntaxError it exists to prevent. `_lastPairLabel` holds whichever group drew LAST in the frame — capture it once, while the hover is live. A CSS-border triangle's computed `width` is 8px, not 0.

verdicts.title: CLASS 21: An index-keyed or positional format fails plausibly and reports nothing
verdicts.reason: All six instances present in CLAUDE.md; `_tech_keys` (2 mentions) is the named three-rung ladder, and `e2e/journeys/dual-consumers.spec.ts` exists on disk as the differential gate. The `s`-is-two-pairs and `posId`-vs-`fromPositionId` instances are corroborated by CLASS 7's code evidence (`_ambig`/`valIdx` in app.src.jsx). The graph-data.json `links`-as-index-pairs shape is real — I read the file directly (1467 nodes).
verdicts.rewrite:
**AN INDEX OR POSITIONAL JOIN FAILS PLAUSIBLY AND REPORTS NOTHING — 6 instances. "Nothing in the format is self-describing: a wrong remap still finds rows, still prints integers on every card, and prints the WRONG technique's number on each — no exception, no warning, no blank."** The `cal` key's flat-kebab spelling missed all 297 submissions; `posId` was a PATH where `fromPositionId` is a SLUG, so 54 of 136 positions had an empty hand; `s` is `[top,bottom]` for a position and `[attacker,defender]` for a technique behind one shape.
**Do:** gate an index join with a whole-structure DIFFERENTIAL against a known-good graph PLUS a non-triviality floor — never a non-null count, which a wrong-but-complete remap satisfies perfectly (`dual-consumers.spec.ts` asserts >1200 cards carry a real mark so it cannot pass on a build where both sides came back empty). Any emitter doing a spelling-sensitive join must PRINT its coverage and refuse to write below a floor (`_tech_keys`, 95% per type). An index is safe only when it never leaves the file it indexes.

verdicts.title: CLASS 23: Order decided by an accident of iteration
verdicts.reason: `scripts/regenerate_graph.py:182` is `for json_file in directory.rglob('*.json'):` — unsorted, exactly the founding case. `node_ordinals.json` exists at repo root with `format_version`, `next_ordinal` 1467 and `count_assigned`, i.e. the append-only lockfile that exists BECAUSE of it, and `validate:ordinals` is a real script in package.json. All five instances present in CLAUDE.md.
verdicts.rewrite: **ANY ORDERING A USER OR A URL CAN SEE NEEDS A STRICT TOTAL ORDER WHOSE FINAL TIEBREAK IS STABLE CONTENT — never array index, dict insertion order or filesystem order. 5 instances.** `regenerate_graph.py` walks an unsorted `rglob('*.json')` and the layout derives its node list from that insertion order, so adding ONE content file renumbers pre-existing entries — an index-encoded share link would silently open a DIFFERENT set of techniques with no error anywhere (hence `node_ordinals.json`: permanent, append-only, retired-not-removed, minted in sorted-id order). `Array#sort` is STABLE, so a comparator that can return 0 hands the decision to the node index — 21 option pairs tie on EDGE, odds AND attempt%, so the name tiebreak is load-bearing. A constant sort key made the cap deal the first ten ALPHABETICALLY. **A cap over an unordered list is a random sample.**

verdicts.title: CLASS 24: A constant in the code standing in for a value in the data
verdicts.reason: All four instances present in CLAUDE.md and the tell is stated verbatim ('AN EXACT TIE ON SCREEN IS A TIE IN THE DATA, NEVER A CONSTANT IN THE CODE'). Corroborated by direct measurement: `graph-data.json` really does carry per-technique authored rates (I read the wire), and `withDeck` appears once as the no-op filter. The gate shape (42 of 42 bit-identical printed values traced to identical wire rows) is pinned by `e2e/journeys/option-hand.spec.ts`, which exists.
verdicts.rewrite:
**A VALUE THAT IS IDENTICAL ACROSS A WHOLE CATEGORY ON SCREEN IS A CONSTANT UNTIL PROVEN OTHERWISE — 4 instances.** `if (n.ty === "submissions") return 1` made the sort key constant across all 297 submissions; the dominance fallback priced the entire corpus at TWO distinct values where the authored range is 10–74%; "30+ weak spots" was `get("dailyGoal",30)+"+"`, so it read the same for a player with 3 gaps and one with 700; the `withDeck` filter was a no-op.
**Do:** count the DISTINCT values a field actually produces, and where printed values are bit-identical, assert the underlying wire rows are identical too.

verdicts.title: CLASS 26: Shared mutable environment — the run measured someone else's artifact
verdicts.reason: Verified every port config: `playwright.config.ts:7` header says 'DEDICATED PORT :8133, reuseExistingServer:false (v1.81.3)' and :32 sets it false; gen (:37), share (:35), replay (:30) all false with explanatory headers; observe (:26) and quarantine (:21) are deliberately true. `share.config.ts:5-10` states the cross-worktree mechanism verbatim. The stale-bundle variant is corroborated by package.json: `npm run build` does not invoke `neural/build/build.mjs`, while `dev:neural:app` exists precisely as the fast refresh.
verdicts.rewrite:
**A RESULT TAKEN WHILE ANOTHER PROCESS COULD WRITE THE TREE UNDER TEST IS NOT A RESULT — 5 instances.** A config with `reuseExistingServer:true` on a shared port means whichever WORKTREE started it owns it and every later run tests THAT worktree's `source/public` — measured, a run was served a 343,153-byte `neural.js` where its own was 364,190. A Playwright browser cache keyed on the package-lock hash missed every run (this repo bumps the version every commit) while still uploading 261 MiB. **`npm run build` does NOT rebuild the neural bundle — a stale served `neural.js` makes neural journeys 240s-timeout and looks exactly like contention or a regression; refresh with `npm run dev:neural:app`.**
**Do:** every suite owns a dedicated port with `reuseExistingServer:false` (core :8133, gen :8127, share :8129, replay :8151; observe/quarantine reuse deliberately). Cache keys name the RESOLVED artifact version. A flake seen while a bundle was rebuilding is measured with a matched pair, not waved away.

verdicts.title: CLASS 28: A truncated or narrowed survey before a rename, deletion or retirement
verdicts.reason: 'A TRUNCATED GREP' present once in CLAUDE.md with the full account. Corroborated: all 14 named gen specs exist on disk (`ready-test-expiry-autopick-burns-move`, `mid-timeout-question-costs-no-odds`, etc.), so the real consumer list really was larger than the `| head` survey showed. The hand-maintained enumeration it names is real and still hand-maintained: `attachInput`'s early-return list at app.src.jsx:12186 is a literal array with no gate deriving it.
verdicts.rewrite:
**COUNT THE SURVEY IN FULL BEFORE A RENAME OR DELETION — `| head` is how you miss a consumer.** The `auto_pick` retirement was scoped with `grep -rn auto_pick … | head`, which showed the sound catalog, the app and ONE gen spec, so the change looked cheap. verdicts.title: Trap class — test honesty: the rules that stop a green suite from meaning nothing
verdicts.reason: Every rule has a verified anchor. (a) `j.clickByMouse` at `e2e/dsl.ts:673`. (b) 'a probe is not a gate' and 'A probe is evidence' both present in CLAUDE.md. (c) 'Never assert a render by re-implementing it' at L1151. (d) `graph-naming.spec.ts` exists; the app has 13 `rng("…")` tags (`start-pos, role, outcome, resolve, max-moves, ai-skill, opp-sub-pick, opp-pick, opp-finish, mc-pick, mc-shuffle, escape, checkpoint-pick`) and `scripts/check_no_raw_random.sh` enforces exactly 1 `Math.random()` in app.src.jsx and 0 in sound.src.js. (e) 'do not read a green payload gate' present; neither replay digest hash appears anywhere in the repo outside CLAUDE.md, confirming no fixture holds it. (g) verified as a real Playwright behaviour claim. (h) all four gate configs set `reuseExistingServer:false` with headers explaining why. (i) `npm run build` does not invoke `neural/build/build.mjs`; `dev:neural:app` exists as the fix.
verdicts.rewrite:
**TEST HONESTY — the rules that stop a green suite from meaning nothing. A violation here LOOKS like success.**
- `locator.click()` scrolls into view and dispatches ON the element — it cannot prove mouse reachability. `j.clickByMouse` (`e2e/dsl.ts:673`) is the only claim.
- **A probe is evidence for a commit message; only a spec is a gate.** Said twice after mutants survived (v1.128.1 mobile framing, v1.129.1 kicker).
- **Never assert a render by re-implementing it** — the v1.126.0 audit's own probe re-declared the filter and reported "identical" about a broken search path.
- **An unrigged gameplay `rng()` tag is a lottery ticket that only prints when it loses.** `graph-naming` was a 7.7% coin toss on `opp-finish` for its whole life; four consecutive green suites hid it (P ≈ 0.73). When a journey's subject is what happens AFTER an exchange, rig every draw that can END the exchange early. Tags: `start-pos role outcome resolve max-moves ai-skill opp-sub-pick opp-pick opp-finish mc-pick mc-shuffle escape checkpoint-pick` (+ surface-scoped variants). `scripts/check_no_raw_random.sh` pins the seam.
- **A gate can be STRUCTURALLY blind to your change**: `payload-first-hand` pins a 7-card hand (identical bytes with and without the hand cap); `replay-digest` rigs a single-success-cell submission (no fixture holds the digest — the spec compares runs to each other). A green run from either is not evidence about your change. **If your change SHOULD have moved the digest and did not, that is the finding.**
- An assertion stricter than its own claim goes red on a CORRECT build — assert the DIFFERENTIAL, where the constant contribution cancels.
- `test.use({reducedMotion})` leaves `matchMedia` FALSE here; use `page.emulateMedia`.
- Every suite owns a dedicated port with `reuseExistingServer:false`. **`npm run build` does NOT rebuild the neural bundle — use `npm run dev:neural:app`; a stale `neural.js` 240s-timeouts and looks like contention.**

verdicts.title: Trap class — CI and tooling: five ways a gate passed while doing nothing
verdicts.reason: Six of seven verified in the workflows themselves (see CLASS 14). (a) `keepalive.yml:40` `git status --porcelain` with the diff --quiet explanation. (b) `validate_graph_integrity.py:25` `import os`, :648 the comment, :646 the bare except. (c) `e2e-full.yml:54` `tar -czf … -C source public`. (e) `build.mjs:91-103` throws per rule. verdicts.rewrite:
**CI AND TOOLING — five ways a gate passed while doing nothing.**
- **`git diff --quiet` reports NO CHANGE for an UNTRACKED file** — `keepalive.yml` never committed anything, ever. Use `git status --porcelain`.
- **A bare `except Exception: return issues` swallowed a `NameError`**, so `check_position_type_vs_score` returned empty on every run and "0 disagreements" meant "the check never executed". A skip path must PRINT.

- **A rewrite/substitution table must THROW when a rule's `from` string is absent from the source.** `build.mjs` only warned when EVERY rule missed, so two dead rules were invisible and the harness silently stopped receiving fixtures.

- **A partial chain must be justified AT THE CALL SITE and must include every step that mutates the artifact it commits.** `votes-refresh.yml` once ran bare `regenerate_graph.py` and stripped `strength` from 4,464 of 4,465 nodes. It runs `graph-base` + `graph-strength` today and deliberately NOT the umbrella (the layout/ordinal steps need an ML stack this job does not install and would rewrite files it never stages) — the reason is in the workflow comment. **Do not "fix" it to the umbrella.**

verdicts.title: FINISHED COPY (a): T-INPUT-1 — a control inside a fixed overlay is dead to the mouse

verdicts.rewrite:
#### T-INPUT-1 — a control inside a fixed overlay is dead to the mouse
**Fires when** you add, move or re-parent a clickable element inside a fixed overlay on the app root (`.ng-landcard`, `.ng-landfilm`, `.ng-seemore`, the option-detail sheet, the node card, any new one) — or you touch `attachInput`.
**Mechanism** `attachInput`'s `pointerdown` calls `setPointerCapture()` on the wrap. That RETARGETS the later `pointerup` to the wrap, so the browser resolves the click from the down/up common ancestor and the listener inside your overlay never runs. Separately, `pointer-events` is inherited and the overlay root disables it: a control that does not re-enable it INLINE is hit-tested straight through to the canvas.
**Looks like** the element measures correctly, `elementFromPoint` returns it, a real mouse click does nothing. Keyboard paths work — that is what hides it. `locator.click()` passes, because it dispatches on the element.
**Count** 6 surfaces in the early-return list as of v1.129.7, numbered in code; v1.69.1 (coach Next button) through v1.123.0 (`.ng-seemore`, dead to the mouse for its entire existence). A human found every one.
**Do** add the overlay to `attachInput`'s early-return list (`app.src.jsx:12186`) so a gesture starting inside it returns before capture; set `pointer-events:auto` inline on the control; pin it with `j.clickByMouse(sel)` — never `locator.click()`.
**Partially pinned:** `j.clickByMouse` exists, but only fires for overlays someone wrote a mouse journey for. **The early-return list is hand-maintained with no gate deriving it.**

#### T-INPUT-2 — a hidden overlay that still eats clicks
**Fires when** you hide an overlay by writing `opacity:0` and/or `pointer-events:none` — `_suppressLand`, `applyDeckVisibility`, `expandOption`, the mobile-pane pair, or any new hide-site.
**Mechanism** hit-testing ignores opacity, and `pointer-events` is inherited — so any descendant that re-enables it INLINE stays live across its whole box. `[data-land-foot]` (`app.src.jsx:9565`) does exactly that, deliberately, because it holds `More ▸` and the capture `+`. The overlay is invisible and still on top.
**Looks like** something UNDERNEATH the hidden element is dead to the mouse. `elementFromPoint` at your target returns the thing you thought was gone — measured: `<div data-land-foot="1">` at the centre of a capture button, 120s of Playwright retries.

**Do** also set `visibility:hidden !important`. It is inherited, nothing in this subtree escapes it with `visible`, and it removes the subtree from hit-testing outright. Assert inertness with `elementFromPoint`, not with a visual check.

verdicts.rewrite:
#### T-SPEC-1 — never assert a render by re-implementing it
**Fires when** a spec, probe or audit computes the expected answer itself: `nodes.filter(...)`, a private copy of a filter or of "what the node set is", a hand rebuilt from `adj`, a screen coordinate recomputed from `n.x`/`n.y`.
**Mechanism** you write the copy from the same reading of the code you are testing, usually with the fix already in it. The two agree by construction, so the assertion measures nothing.
**Looks like** green — on a build you have already broken. The v1.126.0 audit built to find this class committed it: its probe measured `nodes.filter(n => n.rep && …)` and reported "identical" about Explore's search, which was doubling every hit and halving its own 120-row cap.
**Count** 6 specs held private copies of the node set (v1.125.0), plus 1 in the audit that hunted them (v1.126.0), plus three pixel oracles that could not kill a label mutant (v1.129.0).
**Do** drive the real entry point — `renderExplorer()`, `optionsFor()`, `draw()` — and assert on what it EMITTED: DOM rows, duplicate row text, read-back pixels. When the geometry lives in a draw-local closure (`halfW`, `ox`) you cannot recompute it at all: PUBLISH it (`_lastPairLabel`, `_lastRichLabel`, `this._LY = LY`) and read the published value. Reading the strings a frame passed to `fillText` is the render's output, not a second implementation. A second implementation is legitimate ONLY when it also asserts set-equality against the app's own result, so a disagreement fails loudly (`option-hand.spec.ts`).

verdicts.title: KEEP: the pair is derived at ingest, the rep IS the hub, and `adj` must NOT be role-split

verdicts.rewrite:
**THE PAIR IS DERIVED AT INGEST AND THE REP *IS* THE HUB.** Both orbs are one node id: the rep carries the hub id, its ordinal and its URL, so **zero ordinals were minted and zero retired — nothing was migrated**. The partner mints `<hub>/Bottom` / `<hub>/Defender` with **`o: null`**, which is why lists must normalise through `siteIdOf`. `graph-data.json` is byte-for-byte unchanged; the cost is CPU, not bytes. `?dual=legacy` is the escape hatch.

Splitting it handed the opponent YOUR hand and reddened `content-capstone`. Site adjacency (link kind 2) is one-way and never drawn.
**PRECISION, corrected v1.129.7 — do not restate the old wording:** `adj[<member>]` is **not** "byte-for-byte" `adj[<hub>]`. Measured, the two members differ in 136 of 136; the difference is ONLY the pair tie (each holds the other), the technique sets are identical 136/136 once the partner is stripped, and order legitimately differs. A spec written against the literal old wording goes red on a correct build.

verdicts.title: KEEP: lists store SITES — `siteIdOf` normalisation, because only a hub carries an ordinal
verdicts.reason: `siteIdOf` occurs 9 times in `neural/src/app.src.jsx` — consistent with normalisation at the writer AND the membership readers, which is the non-deducible half of the rule. The ordinal premise is verified independently: `node_ordinals.json` has `next_ordinal` 1467 against 1467 wire nodes, so the derived partners carry none. CLAUDE.md mentions `siteIdOf` 3 times. The blast-radius framing (half of jiu-jitsu) follows from the 136-of-272 / 172-of-400 seat figures, which are internally consistent with the 136 position hubs I counted in `graph-data.json`.
verdicts.rewrite:
**LISTS HOLD SITES, NOT MEMBERS — `siteIdOf` normalises in the LIST LAYER, and the READERS matter as much as the writer.** Only a hub carries a share ordinal; a derived partner mints `<hub>/Bottom` / `<hub>/Defender` with `o: null` (**0 of 1467 partners carry one**). So a `+` pressed while standing on the LOWER orb filed an id the encoder reports as `missing`: **the technique was dropped from the share code with no error, and a one-item list encoded to the empty string.** Not an edge case — 136 of 272 position landings and 172 of 400 technique seats stand on a partner, i.e. every time the coach is playing bottom.
**Do:** normalise in `addToList`, `removeFromList`, `removeListItem` AND `activeListHas`, `nodeInAnyList`, `listsWith`, `listItemName`, `openListPicker` — it is the layer's own invariant, so a surface added later cannot bypass it. **Normalising only the WRITE makes a captured technique show `+` instead of `✓` on the very orb you captured it from** (mutant, killed).

verdicts.title: KEEP: an unrigged `rng()` tag is a lottery ticket that only prints when it loses
verdicts.reason: The determinism seam is verified end to end. `grep -o 'rng("[a-z-]*"' neural/src/app.src.jsx | sort -u` yields 13 base tags: `ai-skill checkpoint-pick escape max-moves mc-pick mc-shuffle opp-finish opp-pick opp-sub-pick outcome resolve role start-pos` (the claim listed 12 and omitted `mc-pick`), plus the surface-scoped variants built dynamically. `scripts/check_no_raw_random.sh` exists and enforces exactly 1 `Math.random()` in app.src.jsx (the rng passthrough) and 0 in sound.src.js, failing loudly with line numbers. `e2e/journeys/graph-naming.spec.ts` exists. verdicts.rewrite:
**A JOURNEY THAT LEAVES A GAMEPLAY `rng()` TAG UNRIGGED HAS BOUGHT A LOTTERY TICKET, AND THE TICKET ONLY PRINTS WHEN IT LOSES.** `graph-naming` left `rng("opp-finish")` live, so the opponent could submit you and END the round before the journey's second landing — measured 6 failures in 78 un-rigged runs (7.7%) against 0 in 30 rigged, invisible across four consecutive green full suites (P(4 green) ≈ 0.73). The proof is that rigging makes the branch UNREACHABLE; the counts only corroborate.
**Do:** when a journey's subject is what happens AFTER an exchange, rig every draw that can END the exchange early. Tags: `start-pos role outcome resolve max-moves ai-skill opp-sub-pick opp-pick opp-finish mc-pick mc-shuffle escape checkpoint-pick`, plus surface-scoped variants (`land-mc-pick`, `land-mc-shuffle`) built dynamically so a landing card can never eat the sidebar's rigged queue. `scripts/check_no_raw_random.sh` pins the seam: exactly 1 `Math.random()` in `app.src.jsx`, 0 in `sound.src.js`.

verdicts.title: KEEP: EDGE honesty gap 1 — the shipped opponent is not the opponent the number was computed against
verdicts.reason: The reproduction command exists on disk: `tests/artifacts/_opponent_gap_measure.py`. CLAUDE.md mentions `opponentDefend` 10 times and states both set definitions (SHIPPED = the hub's undirected adjacency filtered to non-positions and deduped by title, 10,662 cells; MODEL = the paired role-node's own dealt hand, 1,246 cells) alongside the meta-lesson that the retired 9.1/23.2%/2476 figure measured the wrong set and understated the gap by half. This is the one canon number in the file that ships with both its set definition and its recompute command — the pattern CLASS 9 prescribes.
verdicts.rewrite:
**EDGE HONESTY GAP — THE SHIPPED OPPONENT IS NOT THE OPPONENT THE NUMBER WAS COMPUTED AGAINST, and this decides whether an EDGE figure may be quoted to a user.** `opponentDefend` iterates UNDIRECTED, HUB-COLLAPSED adjacency with **no role filter and no origin filter** and never reads `attemptProbability`: **10,662 candidate cells over 272 role-states (39.2 each) against the model's 1,246 (4.58 each) — only 11.7% of what the shipped opponent may pick is a move the model's opponent would consider, and 87.6% of the shipped pool is wrong on role, origin or both.** The modelled set is a strict SUBSET in 272 of 272 states, so this is pure over-inclusion. **EDGE therefore describes a better-behaved opponent than the one you face; that sentence belongs in any copy explaining EDGE.**
**Reproduce:** `python3 tests/artifacts/_opponent_gap_measure.py`.
**Meta-lesson attached, and it is why the command is here:** the retired figure (9.1 / 23.2% / 2476) measured the opponent's role-filtered moves BEFORE origin narrowing — a sound measurement of the wrong set, disclosing the gap at roughly HALF its real size. **A canon number nobody can reproduce is worse than no number.**

traps.group: 1. Before you add, move or hide a fixed overlay (or touch `attachInput`)
traps.entry:
**`attachInput` · `setPointerCapture` — a control inside a fixed overlay is dead to the MOUSE.** `attachInput`'s `pointerdown` captures on the wrap, which retargets the later `pointerup`, so the browser resolves the click from the down/up common ancestor and your listener never runs. It measures correctly, `elementFromPoint` returns it, keyboard works, and `locator.click()` passes because it dispatches on the element.
**Do:** name the overlay in `attachInput`'s pointerdown early-return list (`app.src.jsx:12146-12188` — 6 surfaces, numbered in code: node card, dossier sheet, landing card, film strip, option-detail sheet, see-more hint), set `pointer-events:auto` INLINE on the control, and prove it with `j.clickByMouse(sel)` (`e2e/dsl.ts:673`).
**Partially pinned:** `clickByMouse` only fires for overlays somebody wrote a mouse journey for, and the list is hand-maintained with no gate deriving it — that is how `.ng-seemore` stayed dead to the mouse for its entire existence.
traps.instances: 6 surfaces (v1.69.1 → v1.123.0), all found by hand

traps.group: 1. Before you add, move or hide a fixed overlay (or touch `attachInput`)
traps.entry:
**`opacity:0` IS NOT HIDDEN — an invisible overlay still eats clicks.** Hit-testing ignores opacity, and `pointer-events` is inherited, so any descendant that re-enables it inline stays live across its whole box — `[data-land-foot]` does exactly that on purpose (`app.src.jsx:9565`), because it holds `More ▸` and the capture `+`. Symptom: something UNDERNEATH is dead to the mouse and `elementFromPoint` returns the thing you thought was gone (measured: `<div data-land-foot="1">` at the centre of a capture button, 120s of Playwright retries).
**Do:** also write `visibility:hidden !important` — inherited, unescapable here, removes the subtree from hit-testing. `_suppressLand` (`app.src.jsx:7385-7403`) is the reference. Assert inertness with `elementFromPoint`, never a visual check.
**UNGUARDED, and one site is still leaky at HEAD: `expandOption` (`app.src.jsx:3456`) stands the landing card down with opacity + pointer-events only.** No gate enumerates the hide-sites.
traps.instances: 5 by v1.100.2; 1 site still leaky as of v1.129.7

traps.group: 1. Before you add, move or hide a fixed overlay (or touch `attachInput`)
traps.entry:
**`_dockLandCard` · `_dockLandFilm` · `_dockOptionHint` · `_bandBot` — fixed chrome docks off a MEASURED rect, never a CSS constant.** The option tray is `bottom:84px` with no height and grows upward as card names wrap; anything tuned against it collides at some viewport. Measured overlaps: landing card 63px, escape tray 7px, option hint 2px at EVERY width, pane/card 108px at 1024, phone challenge cue 6,700 px².
**Two sub-rules:** keep the TIGHTEST measurement ever taken at this viewport (the band flickers because card and film mount on different frames, and a per-landing reset hands the loose answer straight back); and an element that has not laid out yet reads `rect.top == 0` — that is SKIP, not a constraint.
**STILL OPEN:** the phone challenge cue writes across the focus label and eats the tap on your own node. Reproduce: `node tests/artifacts/_cue_collision_probe.mjs`.
traps.instances: 12 (self-counted as "the third"); 1 still open

traps.group: 1. Before you add, move or hide a fixed overlay (or touch `attachInput`)
traps.entry: **The app wrap is `position:fixed` = its own stacking context, so a `z-index` inside it is trapped at plane 0.** A deliberate screen must PORTAL to the app root or ambient gameplay chrome paints over it (the pane at z:8 was buried by a root-plane landing card at z:5; the account menu needed z:46 on the root plane). Bands, documented in `neural/src/helmet.html`: **1-9 ambient state · 10-49 ambient fx · 50-79 coaching · 90-99 deliberate temporary screens.** Pick a band, never a loose number; Esc walks the ladder top-down, pane last.
traps.instances: 3 (dossier under the transport pill; the pane under the landcard; the account menu)

traps.group: 1. Before you add, move or hide a fixed overlay (or touch `attachInput`)
traps.entry: **`style.color = ""` DELETES an inline declaration; it does not restore one.** After `More → Less` the toggle went black on a dark card, because clearing removed the value the button's own `cssText` had written and it inherited the UA default. To return an element to a colour declared inline, WRITE it — `NG_LAND_MORE_COL` exists so the two sites that set it cannot drift. Related sizing rule: a 44px thumb target must not set a 24px row's layout box — shrink the box with a negative margin and keep the hit area (`.ng-lists-new` pattern).

traps.group: 2. Before you touch the canvas draw path, a node coordinate, or the camera
traps.entry:
**`n.y` vs `LY(n)` / `pairMid(n)` — never convert a node to a screen position from its STORED coordinate.** Each pair member is lifted off a shared ground point (~37px at roll zoom, against a 28px pick radius), so `n.y` is not where the orb is. **FIVE recorded instances as of v1.129.7:** the hover label AND the tap handler (clicking a visible orb matched nothing and fell through to `_tapBackground`), `rollFromPosition`'s camera aim, four specs at once in v1.125.0, and `headPos()` (`app.src.jsx:1333`), which also feeds `camFocus` through two callers — so the camera and the light were wrong TOGETHER and neither looked broken alone.
**Do:** the frame publishes its own lift (`this._LY = LY`, `app.src.jsx:12340`); every consumer AND every spec goes through `_LY` / `pairMid`. Both are the identity on an unpaired node, so applying the rule can never change production geometry. Companion quantity trap: `deg` is GEOMETRY (split per member), `siteDeg` is the STATE (whole) — reading `deg` where the state is meant halves the number the escape tray prints.

traps.group: 2. Before you touch the canvas draw path, a node coordinate, or the camera
traps.entry: **Never assert camera behaviour by reading `camTarget`.** It has nine writers and `updateCamera()`'s follow-cam rewrites it every frame, so a selection flight is overwritten within one frame of a live roll — which is exactly how that bug survived three reviews. **Do:** project the node through `draw()`'s transform and assert it lands inside the viewport rect (`e2e/journeys/share-camera.spec.ts:11-25` is the reference). A deliberate flight takes a LEASE (`holdCamera()`, `camHoldSec = 7`, released by any real pan/pinch/wheel and by the user's own go-elsewhere paths), and `frameNodes` fits BOTH axes because `vw` is a width.
traps.instances: 3 (the share-list flight; `challenge-curriculum`'s retired ±60 contract; `systems-surface` and `url-arrival` still read it directly)

traps.group: 2. Before you touch the canvas draw path, a node coordinate, or the camera
traps.entry: **`this.now` IS the game clock, so a paused roll freezes every age-derived value into a FALSE PASS.** `parkOn` pauses; `age = now - lit` then stops advancing, and a canvas floor assertion passed against a build with the glow deleted, reading a frozen arrival flare. **Do:** age the value out explicitly and assert that it did, or drive the pumped clock. Same family: one `advance()` is not a frame (the landing card's top read 588 on the frame the camera aimed against and 376 on the next — a second bare `advance` is not enough; an intervening `page.evaluate` is what forces layout).

traps.group: 2. Before you touch the canvas draw path, a node coordinate, or the camera
traps.entry: **Anchor a label off `halfW(n)` — the DRAWN silhouette — never `n.r * scale`.** `shapePath` widens a triangle to 1.242r and a diamond to 1.18r, and `nodeK` scales everything again, so `n.r` stopped being the drawn radius twice over. Measure text on a SCRATCH context (`_labelWidthPx`): `this.ctx.font` is mid-frame state during a draw. And **the graph never bakes a role into a name** — all 136 position hub titles end "… Top" as an artifact of the visual collapse, and `splitName().main` only strips a `from <position>` tail, so `graphName(n)` is the single rule for all four canvas label paths.
traps.instances: 2 (label anchoring; 136 of 136 roleless names)

traps.group: 3. Before you write — or trust — a Playwright assertion
traps.entry: **`locator.click()` is not a mouse.** It scrolls into view and dispatches ON the element, so it cannot prove reachability and it masks every overlay trap in group 1 completely. **`j.clickByMouse(sel)` is the only claim:** it measures the centre, refuses to scroll, refuses an off-screen centre, and fails if `elementFromPoint` is anything but the target or a DESCENDANT of it — an intercepting ANCESTOR is a failure, not a pass. On mobile use `page.mouse.click` / `page.touchscreen.tap` at MEASURED coordinates plus an effective-opacity walk up the ancestor chain.
traps.instances: 4+ (every instance in group 1 was masked by it)

traps.group: 3. Before you write — or trust — a Playwright assertion
traps.entry:
**Never assert a render by re-implementing it.** A spec-side copy of a filter, of "what the node set is", or of a screen coordinate is written from the same reading of the code under test — usually with the fix already in it — so it agrees by construction and reports green on a build you have already broken. **The v1.126.0 audit BUILT to find this class committed it:** its probe measured `nodes.filter(n => n.rep && …)` and reported "identical" about Explore's search, which was doubling every hit and halving its own 120-row cap.
**Do:** drive the real entry point (`renderExplorer()`, `optionsFor()`, `draw()`) and assert on what it EMITTED — DOM rows, duplicate row TEXT, read-back pixels. When the geometry lives in a draw-local closure (`halfW`, `ox`) you cannot recompute it at all: read what the frame PUBLISHED (`_lastPairLabel`, `_lastRichLabel`, `this._LY`), which is the render's output, not a second implementation. A second implementation is legitimate ONLY when it also asserts SET EQUALITY against the app's own result (`option-hand.spec.ts`).
traps.instances: 10 (6 specs in v1.125.0, the audit itself, 3 specs pinned to a moved label in v1.129.4)

traps.group: 3. Before you write — or trust — a Playwright assertion
traps.entry: **A probe is evidence for a commit message; only a spec is a gate.** `tests/artifacts/_*_probe.mjs` measured the mobile framing (v1.128.1) and the focus kicker (v1.129.1), both shipped, and in both cases the mutant SURVIVED the red-proof pass because no journey covered them — the same lesson two versions running. **Do:** mutate every claim; a surviving mutant means the claim has no gate. And **record non-kills in the spec's own header** — `dual-pair.spec.ts` names its two, so nobody later reads that spec as covering them.
traps.instances: 3 (v1.128.1, v1.129.1, plus the reverted tray drag whose own mutants could not kill its test)

traps.group: 3. Before you write — or trust — a Playwright assertion
traps.entry:
**A journey that leaves a gameplay `rng()` tag unrigged has not chosen a branch — it has bought a lottery ticket, and the ticket only prints when it loses.** `graph-naming` left `rng("opp-finish")` live, so the opponent could submit you and END the round before the journey's second landing: **6 failures in 78 un-rigged runs (7.7%) vs 0 in 30 rigged**, and P(four consecutive green full suites) ≈ 0.73, so three earlier clean reports were never evidence of absence. The fix is DEDUCTIVE — rig the value so the branch is unreachable — and the counts are corroboration, not proof.
**Do:** when a journey's subject is what happens AFTER an exchange, rig every draw that can end the exchange early. The 13 static tags: `start-pos role outcome resolve max-moves ai-skill opp-pick opp-sub-pick opp-finish mc-pick mc-shuffle escape checkpoint-pick`, plus surface-scoped variants (`land-mc-pick`, `land-mc-shuffle`) so a landing card can never eat the sidebar's rigged queue. `scripts/check_no_raw_random.sh` pins the seam: exactly 1 `Math.random()` in `app.src.jsx`, 0 in `sound.src.js`.
traps.instances: 1 measured, on a journey that had been a coin toss in every version it existed

traps.group: 3. Before you write — or trust — a Playwright assertion
traps.entry:
**A green gate is evidence only about what that gate can SEE.** `payload-first-hand` pins `start-pos:[0]` — a 7-card hand — so it reports the same bytes with the hand cap and without it: **do not read a green payload gate as evidence about hand size.** `replay-digest` rigs one scripted roll on a single-success-cell submission, so the outcome-kernel fix, the `cardOrder` retirement and the loss-aversion dial were all structurally invisible to it — and **no fixture holds the expected digest anywhere in the repo** (`triple_replay.sh` compares runs to each other), so the hashes in prose describe nothing checkable.
**Do:** cite a gate only for a claim a mutant of that claim makes red; otherwise write its blind spot in the same sentence as the green. **And if your change SHOULD have moved the digest and did not, that is the finding.**
traps.instances: 12 (incl. 4 separate re-discoveries of the digest case)

traps.group: 3. Before you write — or trust — a Playwright assertion
traps.entry: **An assertion stricter than its own claim goes RED on a CORRECT build.** "Nothing is drawn above the name" fails on the name's own ascenders; "nothing is drawn at merge scale" is false because the ordinary hover label takes over; "the announcer is blank after staging" is false because a staged landing may legitimately say something else. **Do:** assert the DIFFERENTIAL the change is about, against a CONTROL FRAME — everything the graph would draw anyway subtracts to zero, and the constant contribution cancels. **After relaxing an assertion, re-run its mutant**, so "less strict" does not become "less able to fail".
traps.instances: 3 named together in v1.129.0, plus 3 label-position specs in v1.129.4 and 5 mutants needed in v1.114.0

traps.group: 4. Before you rely on the harness (DSL, ports, payloads, which build is under test)
traps.entry: **A harness payload pattern is a SUBSTRING of the request URL, so a stale name matches nothing and holds nothing.** Twelve rules armed `"flashcards.json"`, which the app has not fetched since v1.80.4 (it fetches `flashcards/_index.json` via `_dataBase()`), so every cold-start assertion about the ~18s skew measured a fully-warm boot — root cause of 15 red journeys. The same dead name hid in `build.mjs`, whose guard only warned when EVERY rewrite missed. **Do:** a rewrite/substitution table must THROW when a rule's `from` string is absent from the source (`neural/build/build.mjs:91-108` does now); when a rule holds a payload, assert the timeline shows it held.
traps.instances: 2 (12 harness rules + 2 of 4 build rewrites)

traps.group: 4. Before you rely on the harness (DSL, ports, payloads, which build is under test)
traps.entry: **Name what the harness does NOT serve, beside every assertion — if the absence alone satisfies it, the assertion is about the harness.** The DSL serves `{}` for dossier chunks, so there is no film strip and most states legitimately have no `More` fold; a journey about either must AUTHOR content. `test.use({ reducedMotion })` leaves `matchMedia` FALSE here, so a spec relying on the fixture option **asserts nothing and passes forever** — use `page.emulateMedia`. Non-localhost requests are aborted, which is why the GitHub-stars `.catch` is load-bearing. A screenshot taken under the harness photographs the harness (`tests/artifacts/_owner_shoot.mjs` drives the real dev server for exactly this reason).

traps.group: 4. Before you rely on the harness (DSL, ports, payloads, which build is under test)
traps.entry: **A spec in a directory no config's `testDir` collects is a NOTE, not a gate.** `e2e/prototype/` was collected by nothing — not `package.json`, not `.github/workflows/`, not any config (only `playwright.{private,chrome}.config.ts` take `PW_TESTDIR`, from a hand-typed invocation) — so its three journeys ran when somebody remembered, through thirteen versions that included making their subject the DEFAULT and deleting the flag they booted with. **Do:** before claiming coverage, check the spec is actually collected. A spec that needs a gitignored payload cannot be a gate at all.
traps.instances: 1 (3 journeys, 13 versions)

traps.group: 4. Before you rely on the harness (DSL, ports, payloads, which build is under test)
traps.entry:
**A result taken while another process could write the tree under test is not a result.** A config with `reuseExistingServer:true` on a shared port means whichever WORKTREE started it owns it, and every later run tests THAT worktree's `source/public` — measured, a run was served a 343,153-byte `neural.js` where its own was 364,190. Every gate suite now owns a dedicated port with `reuseExistingServer:false` (core :8133 · gen :8127 · share :8129 · replay :8151 · catalog :8131; only `observe`/`quarantine` reuse, deliberately).
**And `npm run build` does NOT rebuild the neural bundle** — a stale served `neural.js` makes neural journeys silently 240s-timeout and looks exactly like contention or a regression. Refresh with `npm run dev:neural:app` (<1s). Cache keys must name the RESOLVED artifact version, never a file that changes on every commit (the Playwright cache was keyed on `package-lock` in a repo that bumps the version every commit: the key missed every run while still uploading 261 MiB).

traps.group: 5. Before you write app runtime logic
traps.entry: **A single-slot resource with many writers needs a stamped owner and an explicit lifetime.** The announcer (`setEvent`) has ONE slot: a share-arrival sentence was overwritten by the roll within seconds (hence `_announceArrival` HOLDS it for the next landing), "Decide 1…" outlived its hand (hence the `_evCountdown` stamp, which every other `setEvent` releases and `clearOptions` honours), and "Time's up" was overwritten SYNCHRONOUSLY on the next line (hence `HESITATE_HOLD = 1.1s`, and why `clearOptions()` must run BEFORE the sentence it precedes). Same shape: `camTarget` (nine writers, follow-cam rewrites it every frame → a 7s LEASE) and `scrollLeft` (ONE rAF owns it — `_trayStop()` is called by every competing animator). **Three remedies: a stamp released by every other writer, a lease with an expiry, or a single declared writer (`_bumpStageVer`).**

traps.group: 5. Before you write app runtime logic
traps.entry:
**Every suppression flag declares its complete set of LIFTERS at its definition.** `_bgRestore()` had exactly ONE caller (`setPaused(false)`), so a background tap could only be undone by the PLAY BUTTON — the app dealt the hand, built the card and flew the camera underneath a suppression nobody lifted, and it presents as "nothing happens when I click, but the node lights up". Pre-existing since the behaviour shipped.
**Diagnostic worth memorising: `_landHidden()` (`app.src.jsx:7373`) asks FOUR holders — `_landPaneHid`, `_traySup`, `_bgDown`, `_detailCtx`. Any one stuck leaves a built, mounted, correctly populated card invisible while every other surface behaves. Read the holders before you read the render path.** Good pattern: one latch per pauser (`_landAutoPaused` / `_paneAutoPaused` / `_replayAutoPaused` / `_dossierAutoPaused`) so releasing gives back only the pause you took. Never gate on `userActiveNow()` — it measures the GAME clock, so one click on a paused board latches "the user is active" forever.

traps.group: 5. Before you write app runtime logic
traps.entry:
**When one question is answered in two places, one of them is already wrong.** `playFrom` was a whole stale copy of `rollFromPosition` (hard-coded camera, no archive, no state reset); `rollFromPosition` then walked `adj[]` for a technique's origin while `confirmPlayFrom` had read `fromPositionId` all along — **wrong on 907 of 1,331 techniques, and the technique you just tapped was not in the hand you were dealt 68.4% of the time**; the same function kept a hard-coded `vw: graphW*0.42` after `rollCamTarget` existed, and still aimed at `{n.x, n.y}` one version after `camFocus` was fixed on the line beside it ("same defect, missed once"). A two-branch tap rule written before a third case existed is the same failure.
**Do:** collapse to ONE named seam (`rollCamTarget`, `techniqueOrigin`, `captureNode`, `siteIdOf`) BEFORE adding a third caller, and DELETE the copy rather than syncing it. Where two names for one value must coexist in a shared bundle scope (`NG_LIST_ITEM_CAP` / `NG_LIST_MAX_ITEMS`), a test pins them equal.

traps.group: 5. Before you write app runtime logic
traps.entry: **If the data states it, READ it — and a derivation that returns the same answer for the whole corpus is a constant with a function around it.** `optionsFor` inferred the performer from `myVal < oppVal - 0.05` while every technique carries `fromRole`; `performerRole(...) === "top"` stood in for an offence/defence test on an axis that is not top/bottom. All 136 position hub titles end "… Top", so deriving a role from a title IS the constant `top` — which is why `seatRole` exists (596 techniques are bottom-authored) and why `playFrom`/`confirmPlayFrom` take an explicit `role`. A fallback may relax ORIGIN; it must **never** relax ROLE.

traps.group: 6. Before you change a join, an id, a slug, an order or a persisted key
traps.entry:
**A CHECK THAT NEVER RAN REPORTS CLEAN — absence produces a plausible answer.** A bare `except Exception: return issues`, a matcher that matches nothing, a zero-length comparison loop and `git diff --quiet` on an UNTRACKED file all emit exactly what success emits. `check_position_type_vs_score` reported "0 disagreements" for months because a missing `import os` raised `NameError` into a bare except (real figure 95); a headers gate passed a Function that had stopped setting `Cache-Control` because "the comparison loop had nothing to iterate"; `keepalive.yml` had never committed anything, ever.
**Do: every matcher, join, gate and rewrite emits a POSITIVE coverage count and hard-fails below a floor, and a skip path PRINTS.** The repo invented this fix five separate times without naming it — `regenerate_neural_data.py:285` and `:575` (refuse a wire below 95% join coverage, printed every run), `build.mjs:100` (throw per dead rewrite rule), `check_headers_cache.py` check 6a (OMISSION, not only drift), and the `mc_pool_cold` / `land_warm_stalled` beats.

traps.group: 6. Before you change a join, an id, a slug, an order or a persisted key
traps.entry: **A fallback that produces a plausible value and never says it fired is strictly worse than a crash — it buys months of silence.** A missing `cal` made `calSuccess()` return null and `moveChance` fall through to `0.36 + dom*0.1`, so **~289 of 1,204 dealt cards printed a fabricated ~45.6% where authored rates span 10–74%**; `posId`-vs-slug left 54 of 136 positions running entirely on the no-candidates fallback; `posIdx` fell back to the technique itself and staged 1,331 of 2,934 nodes ON a technique node. **Do:** every fallback emits a NAMED beat or a counter (`mc_pool_cold`, `land_warm_stalled` are the pattern), and it is CHOSEN before any rng draw so the draw count cannot depend on content.

traps.group: 6. Before you change a join, an id, a slug, an order or a persisted key
traps.entry: **`_tech_keys` — a spelling-sensitive join must try every spelling and then COUNT itself.** `graph.json` keys a technique by `slugify(<display name>)`, one flat kebab token; a layout id keeps the authored PATH, so `Submissions/Kimura/from-Front-Headlock` arrives with a `/` where the key has a `-`. **0 of 297 submission keys contain an inner slash, so 294 of 297 submissions shipped no odds at all** and nothing went red, because the fallback above printed a plausible number. The ladder is three rungs, cheapest first, and the last is the key's OWN CONSTRUCTOR rather than another guess: `as-is` → `slash→hyphen` → `slugify(title)`. Together 1331 of 1331. The emitter now refuses to write a wire below 95% coverage per type and prints the figure every run.
traps.instances: 1, hidden for months, across 2 joins (`cal` and `tech_avail`)

traps.group: 6. Before you change a join, an id, a slug, an order or a persisted key
traps.entry: **`s` is TWO DIFFERENT PAIRS behind one shape: `[top, bottom]` on a POSITION, `[attacker, defender]` on a TECHNIQUE.** `roleIdx()` (side) indexed both, so every bottom-performed technique was read as its opponent's value: **a bottom player was shown ZERO of the 297 submission nodes**, and 144 of 596 bottom-authored techniques were silently discarded. **Use `valIdx(node)` — performer for a technique, side for a position — never `roleIdx()` on a technique.** Two nearly identical accessors sit side by side in `app.src.jsx:1388-1390` and the code cannot explain why both exist; this is why.
traps.instances: 1, corpus-wide

traps.group: 6. Before you change a join, an id, a slug, an order or a persisted key
traps.entry: **An index-keyed or positional join fails by printing the WRONG right-looking answer.** `cal.ev` is keyed `<position node index>/<role>` with `blk[0]` a list of TECHNIQUE node indexes: nothing is self-describing, so a wrong remap still finds rows, still prints an integer on every card, and prints a different technique's number on each — no exception, no warning, no blank. **Do: gate it with a whole-structure DIFFERENTIAL against a known-good graph (one build, booted twice) PLUS a non-triviality floor** — `dual-consumers.spec.ts` asserts >1200 cards carry a real mark, so it cannot pass on a build where `_ev` came back empty on BOTH sides and every comparison was trivially equal. Never a non-null count: a wrong-but-complete remap satisfies it perfectly. An index is safe only when it never leaves the file that defines it.
traps.instances: 6 (cal.ev, the `s` pair, `posId`-vs-`fromPositionId`, `deg`/`siteDeg`, the cal key, links-as-pairs)

traps.group: 6. Before you change a join, an id, a slug, an order or a persisted key
traps.entry:
**A node's ARRAY INDEX can never go in a URL, and any user-visible order needs a strict total order whose final tiebreak is stable CONTENT.** `regenerate_graph.py` walks an unsorted `rglob('*.json')` and the layout derives its node list from `adjacency` DICT INSERTION order seeded by that — so adding ONE content file renumbers pre-existing entries and an index-encoded share link would silently open a DIFFERENT set of techniques, with no error anywhere. Hence `node_ordinals.json`: permanent, append-only, never renumbered, never reused, retired-not-removed, minted in sorted-id order, hard-gated by `validate:ordinals`.
**Corollaries:** `Array#sort` is STABLE, so a comparator that can return 0 hands the decision to the node index — 21 dealt option pairs tie on EDGE, odds AND attempt%, and only the name separates them. And **a cap applied over an unordered list is a random sample**: a constant sort key made the 10-cap deal submissions ALPHABETICALLY and truncate the state's most-attempted move.

traps.group: 6. Before you change a join, an id, a slug, an order or a persisted key
traps.entry: **Lists hold SITES: `siteIdOf` normalises in the LIST LAYER — the writer AND every membership reader.** Only a hub carries a share ordinal; the derived pair's partner mints `<hub>/Bottom` / `<hub>/Defender` with `o: null` (**0 of 1467**), so a `+` pressed while standing on the lower orb filed an id the encoder reports as `missing`: **the technique was dropped from the share code with no error, and a one-item list of it encoded to the empty string.** Not an edge case — 136 of 272 position landings and 172 of 400 technique seats stand on a partner, i.e. every time the coach is playing bottom. **Normalising only the WRITE is the tempting half-fix and is wrong**: it makes a captured technique show `+` instead of `✓` on the very orb you captured it from. Nine call sites today (`addToList`, `removeFromList`, `removeListItem`, `activeListHas`, `nodeInAnyList`, `listsWith`, `listItemName`, `openListPicker`, the id lookup); it is the layer's invariant, so a surface added later cannot bypass it.
traps.instances: 1, reachable on half of all landings

traps.group: 6. Before you change a join, an id, a slug, an order or a persisted key
traps.entry: **DO NOT role-split `adj`.** `opponentDefend`, `_mcPool` and `_posIdx` walk `adj[currentPos]` with NO role filter, deliberately — they are asking about the EXCHANGE, not about your hand. A purely role-split adjacency handed the opponent YOUR hand, the belt-test opponent stopped finding submissions, and `content-capstone` went red. Each pair member therefore carries its SITE's technique set (link kind 2, one-way, never drawn). **Precise wording matters here:** the two members' `adj` are NOT byte-identical — measured 136 of 136 differ by exactly the pair tie, and order legitimately differs because a site link is pushed one-way. The design claim holds; a spec written against the retired "byte-for-byte, in the same order" phrasing goes red on a correct build.
traps.instances: 1 (found by the suite, not by review)

traps.group: 6. Before you change a join, an id, a slug, an order or a persisted key
traps.entry: **A settings key can NEVER be deleted — retire it by ceasing to READ it.** `_pullAndMerge`'s per-key settings merge is `if (!(sk in merged) || ct > lt)` with **no tombstone** (`app.src.jsx:4646`), so a key deleted locally is unconditionally RE-ADDED by the first pull from any device that still carries it; pruning on load is theatre. Dormant today, read by nothing: `cardOrder`, `studyOrder`, `challengePinnedTrack`. Same shape, chosen deliberately, elsewhere: list reconciliation is ADD-WINS, so a DELETE loses to a stale device (deleting again is trivial; losing the class a coach already posted is not), and `srs` merge is later-`last`-wins with a same-day tie going to the SMALLER interval. And a state-driven auto-flip is not a mint: driving a reward toggle off "belt is black" re-enables it on every device forever through LWW — flip it once, inside the mint.
traps.instances: 8 across three storage layers

traps.group: 6. Before you change a join, an id, a slug, an order or a persisted key
traps.entry: **A value identical across a whole category on screen is a CONSTANT until proven otherwise.** `movePotential` returned `1` for every submission, so the sort key was constant across all 297; the dominance fallback priced the entire submission corpus at **2 distinct values** where 37 are authored; "30+ weak spots" printed `get("dailyGoal",30) + "+"` and read the same for a player with 3 gaps and one with 700. **Detection, cheap and general: count the DISTINCT values a field actually produces, and where two printed values are bit-identical, assert the underlying source rows are identical too** (42 of 42 is the passing shape). An exact tie on screen must be a tie in the data, never a constant in the code.

traps.group: 7. Before you edit CI, a build emitter, or rename/delete a symbol
traps.entry:
**CI must not silently run a subset of the chain a human runs, and no emitted path may be allow-listed.** `votes-refresh.yml` once ran bare `regenerate_graph.py` and committed a graph.json with `strength` **stripped from 4,464 of 4,465 nodes**. `e2e-full.yml` tarred six allow-listed paths, so the PR gate for BOTH protected branches could not pass — an allow-list rots silently and that one predated every spec that broke on it; package by default and `--exclude` explicitly. A `paths:` filter must include the INPUTS its own gates read.
**Corrected rule, because the absolute version is contradicted by a deliberate fix:** `votes-refresh.yml` today runs `regenerate:graph-base` + `regenerate:graph-strength` and NOT the umbrella — the layout/ordinal steps need an ML stack that job does not install (the umbrella failed there every week) and would rewrite files the PR step never stages. So: **a partial chain must be justified AT THE CALL SITE and must include every step that mutates the artifact it commits.** Do not "fix" that workflow back to the umbrella.
**Standing hazard: deploy does NOT run root `npm run build`** — both workflows re-list the steps inline, so any new build step is absent in production unless added there too, and no gate compares the two lists.
